an existing edf6 flat normal map is used for <map>_normal.dds in the examined converter. to preserve a layer whose source had no multiplier, the builder appends an opaque white bc1 identity slice at every mip rather than writing an invalid negative sample index. the original colour slices and mips remain unchanged. in a d3d11 warp test, multiplying source colour by that identity slice preserved the sampled rgb. mad collision reconstruction the examined terrain collision builder creates one target map body named <piece>.<piece> with 2500 compressed-mesh tiles, each a 10×10-cell tile of the same 4 m lattice (100 quads / 200 triangles per tile). the output is encoded using an edf6 donor's havok-2020 structural schema rather than copying edf4.1's heightfield shape. additional placed objects are represented by named collision bodies when corresponding source model collision triangles are available. offline checks decoded the generated triangles back to the lattice within approximately 1e−5 m, compared bounds and used independent compressed-mesh readers. the old output still had open questions about triangleisinterior, material palette and object models missing from a map's rab. later sk collision work should be consulted before treating this historical builder as the final target. map-level resource wiring a successful export has to update all linked resources, not just fmb and mad: mac: replace the shfb's definition with an fmep definition, update the map object / mapo height linkage, write externals.sgo for the new fmb and remove obsolete source field members. rab: expose the colour array under the expected edf6 name and supply a normal array and valid multiplier slices. mad: supply target-format named collision bodies for terrain and included map objects. plants: reconstruct fmb table 2/3 and mapo height data rather than inheriting an empty grass placeholder; see the dedicated vegetation guide. navigation: donor hkt/nvmd remains geometrically mismatched unless explicitly rebuilt against this terrain. what was and was not demonstrated the historical report records extensive real-source offline tests, serializer round-trips, source-object-to-ground comparisons and a gpu warp texture test. it explicitly lists map load, black-block rendering, driveability and real ai pathing as still requiring game tests in that branch. do not turn those offline checks into blanket game-runtime claims. sources: components/maps/evidence/edf41-sk-terrain.md, pylib/sk_terrain.py, pylib/fmb_build.py, pylib/hkcms_build.py, pylib/sk_map.py from the retained edf4.1 r10 hf4 r9 source package; the 2026-10-17 feedback correction for fmb shader indices. subsequent source contact measurements the newer seven-map terrain–object contact census follows the native shfb, mapb and mad geometry relationships beyond bare terrain generation. r24–r28 examine 81 sampled placements and then 1,770 matched static-mesh placements. this demonstrates a source-geometry contact boundary, not native collision acceptance, full map coverage or pathfinding parity. cross-check: field lattice is not a navigation tile set (16 november source evidence) the seven original shfb fields also support a 4 m terrain lattice plan of 250,000 cells/500,000 triangles per map; this coincides in spatial sample spacing with the earlier 501×501 fmb render lattice, but neither the historical 625 fmb render leaves nor the 2,500 mad collision tiles is the same as the later 256 planned hkt navigation tiles. the hkt tile grid belongs to a separate streaming/agent representation. structural hkt/nvmd samples at 4 m have only been generated for bounded windows, while 32/64 m samples span the terrain domain. read the 4 m source-grid/hkt/nvmd evidence atlas before interpreting any of these numbers as gameplay-equivalent navmesh coverage.

edf4.1 foliage and power lines in edf6 — fmex cells, mapo heights and wire ownership why a correctly rendered map can still lose plants edf4.1's sk heightfield .shfb stores vegetation in its own source tables. edf6's outdoor vegetation is reconstructed from fmb table 2 and table 3 together with a per-occupied-cell height list in the terrain's mapo record. removing shfb while leaving the fmep/mapo grass pair empty makes vegetation disappear even if the ground mesh and textures are correct. the later 2026-10-17 reverse engineering corrected an earlier false assumption that all stock fmep ground pieces had empty vegetation. 17 native edf6 outdoor ground records in the examined set used populated vegetation. the exact data relationship is more useful than the old assumption. fmex / fmb table and mapo height contract the observed fmb table 2 (header +0x14) begins with {group_count, 8}. each vegetation group carries a 0x28-byte descriptor with group name, cell size, columns, rows, origin x/z, type count, grid-byte arrays and type references. grid arrays are column-count × row-count, with row along world z; 0xff denotes no object. the type records are 0x40-byte entries containing kind, referenced name and file, colour, size range and associated sgo data. fmb table 3 supplies a 256-record jitter table (angle, x/z offsets and size factor). a ground mapo entry starts with {height_count, 8} followed by one float32 height per occupied vegetation cell, across the groups in row-major order. its count must match the sum of occupied grid cells; it is not arbitrary padding. for the measured ig_heigen507 reference, that count was 159 441. a 240-sample comparison between mapped vegetation heights and fmb terrain reported differences below 5 cm. the source sk vegetation table itself has a 0x28-byte type record with source kinds 1 (grass/flower) and 2 (model). in the inspected reconstruction, grass and flowers become one edf6 vegetation group. trees, bushes and small placed models become three additional model groups, matching the native edf6 four-group pattern. sk_heigen02 generated counts in that historical offline pass: 202 275 grass/flower instances, and model groups of 1820 trees, 714 bushes, 853 small objects. these are sample counts, not universal distributions for all sk maps. file identity and format conversion for tree types an edf6 type can point to <model>.tree or <model>.mls, backed by resource .trb and .mlb respectively. the examined edf4.1 .trb first rule omits a field present in the edf6 reader. in the target corpus, 79 of 83 first-rule instances used zero for that additional integer. appending the extra zero and rebuilding the depth-first sgo made two source tree files match corresponding edf6 native files byte-for-byte. .mlb did not require this same structural change in the examined profile. missing plant models and their dds/mdb dependencies remain a separate resource-resolution risk. correct grids do not prove the objects draw, collide, or choose the right randomized dimensions in game; those were explicitly pending real runtime verification. why power lines can be missing even when rmpa parses several source routes labelled cable_elec_wire_* / cable_soudentettou_* carry links to mapb 0x7c wire points, not just positions in the current route. a naive route-local index conversion may discard those links or connect unrelated points. the audited repair matched wire-point coordinates back to their actual route sections and repaired 156 hillycity, 22 kasenjiki and 140 sinsuikouen references in the historical dataset; two still could not be resolved. however, the edf6 rendering path was traced primarily through the mapb 0x7c point-pair table rather than the editable rmpa cable route. therefore rewriting rmpa links alone is not demonstrated to restore visible wires. a second plausible explanation, missing wire_test.dds inside mac, was subsequently deprioritized: the engine's common map texture lookup container also resolves textures stored only in rab, including terrain colour arrays, grass.merge.dds and tree textures. the study recorded the distinct resource packing patterns — all 24/24 examined edf6 maps with power-line pairs had wire_test.dds in mac, versus 0/26 maps without such pairs — but this correlation does not prove that copying the dds into mac fixes rendering. follow-up checks found mapb point-pair sets retained across the conversion, compatible .erb references and no confirmed downstream map-dependent culling in the traversed drawing code. whether missing lines stem from tower objects, runtime path or another cause requires a game/runtime observation, not another guessed metadata rewrite. what to check when debugging for missing grass, compare fmb group grids and occupied-cell count against mapo's float-height list, then check per-grid terrain interpolation and .dds/.trb/.mlb resource identity. for missing trees, check the additional edf6 trb first-rule field and that the referenced model and textures are actually resolvable. for missing wires, inspect mapb wire-point and paired-edge tables before rmpa; do not label the dds packing discrepancy the root cause without observing lookup failure. for wrong terrain colour, check the fmb mesh shader-table index and the colour/multiplier array, not only foliage. distinguish source-data + offline validation, engine-static analysis and confirmed behaviour in the running game. sources: components/maps/evidence/feedback-2026-10-17-edf41-maps.md, pylib/fmex.py, pylib/sk_map.py, pylib/rmpa_legacy.py, and pylib/map_legacy.py in edf4.1 r10 hf4 r9. the source feedback was originally written in chinese and reconciled here by mechanism, not copied verbatim.

edf4.1 hector ai on an edf6 berserker — attack selection, back-off, aiming and gait why model-and-gun replacement is not enough the studied edf4.1 hector was mapped onto an edf6 berserker large base class. both have arms and weapons, but the two native movement, target-aim and animation controllers are not semantically equivalent. a hector can look correct while walking sideways or firing through a pose that no longer matches its weapon muzzle. the r10 hf4 r9 source contains a class-specific bridge for actors explicitly marked by edf41_hector; ordinary edf6 berserkers pass through unchanged. the following are bounded native-class findings, drawn from exact-build edf4.1/edf6 binary analysis embodied in the source. they are not a claim that every game/patch version shares the same addresses or that the historical plugin received fresh runtime qualification here. weapon choice depends on each arm's effective range the original selection procedure runs on a firing interval of 300 + rand(300) frames, and compares the target's horizontal xz distance with the per-arm hector_weapon_range. neither arm in range: do not start a battery. exactly one arm in range: use that arm. both in range: sometimes fire both, otherwise choose an arm randomly. two arms of the same weapon class can fire together according to the source's distinct check. selecting guns from a single combined maximum range can fire a short-range weapon at a target only the long-range arm can reach. the bridge picks the arm mask once per attack and starts only the eligible batteries. back-off as a stateful timer, not a pathfinding order a source hector facing a target moves along its own forward axis, or backwards along the same axis while continuing to face the target. it does not pick an arbitrary lateral waypoint. the captured source configuration defaults to: hector_ai_setting = [720, 1440, 540, 720, 150, 20, 80] [dwell_base, dwell_rand, retreat_base, retreat_rand, near_range, stop_min, stop_max] when within 150 units, a dwell counter decreases 1 per frame outside its chosen stop radius or 2 per frame inside it; at zero the actor retreats for 540 + rand(720) frames and begins a fresh cycle. it may stop and turn within a random stop radius of approximately 20–80 units. the source's walk command is ±1 in its facing axis; the smoothed native velocity corresponds to approximately 6 world units per second in the examined configuration, both forwards and backwards. by contrast, the donor berserker's follow state can walk toward a slot beside the target while facing it, causing lateral slide. historical 2026-10-18 m113 observation reported 43% of walking frames more than 11° off facing; one actor appeared to walk against a wall for about 140 seconds. those are recorded observations of that test, not universal statistics for hectors. separate four operations that look like one animation body steering points the hector toward the target; movement is applied along the body's current facing. gait selection is based on the actual change in yaw and eased local velocity, rather than the command state alone. arm aiming rotates the weapon-bearing arm bones and all dependent muzzle/world matrices. the source gait decision distinguishes stand, turn_l, turn_r, walk_f, walk_b, walk_l, walk_r. it chooses turning if angular change dominates local movement, otherwise selects the larger local velocity axis. walk and turn playback rates follow velocity and yaw changes; source parameters named v_walk_animation_speed and v_turn_animation_speed are applied at this layer. replacing them with the target berserker's generic stand/walk state can make a stationary turning hector rotate without playing a turning animation. for an attacking arm, the target is transformed to the arm's frame and the desired angles are approximately: pitch = -atan2(local_y, sqrt(local_x² + local_z²)) yaw = atan2(local_x, local_z) the source constrains pitch to [-π/2, 0.4π], has mirrored per-side yaw limits (0.6π gives up, 0.7π clamps) and eases 10% toward the target each frame while attacking. outside an attack the angles relax by multiplying by 0.95 per frame. the target berserker's own gun controller adjusts a shot aim point, but does not automatically rotate the hector's arm bone and dependent muzzle geometry the same way. the retained bridge therefore updates local arm rotation, world matrices of descendants, relevant weapon clips, charge/death presentation and the dedicated head cas player in a measured order. without the world rebuild, the visible arm may move but projectiles can still originate from stale muzzle transforms. such hooks must be exact-build guarded; they are not portable numeric patch offsets. integration and evidence boundaries the object metadata for the source-specific behaviour contains two arm ranges, a same-weapon flag and seven ai timing parameters. a state cache must not key only on a reused object address: the source compares live control-block identity and the edf41_hector marker to avoid carrying a dead actor's retreat and aim state into a new one. this is actor ai and animation parity. it does not repair donor-map nav geometry, mission route semantics, source-only havok conversion or missing physical shields. verify each independently before attributing an ai failure to this controller. sources: components/compatibility/src/hector_ai.h and edf41ai.cpp plus comments pointing to exact edf41.exe and edf6.dll analyses, edf4.1 r10 hf4 r9 source archive. no new game execution was performed for this wiki article.

edf4.1 vehicles on edf6 — why tank, motorcycle and begaruta need distinct class adapters asset compatibility and class compatibility are different questions the edf4.1→edf6 source research contains three particularly revealing vehicle ports: vehicletank301 (v301 tank), vehicle408_motorbike (v408 sdl1 sidecar) and vehicle406_begaruta (v406 mech). each keeps source-facing models/animations/physics where possible, but their edf6 runtime classes impose different seat, wheel, ik, collision and named-animation requirements. a source asset can pass binary format validation and still fail catastrophically when its native class uses it. these are specific class and sample contracts, not a universal edf5→6 vehicle importer; no fresh game runtime test was conducted while writing this guide. case a: v301 tank — an accumulating barrel rotation can hide the world the edf4.1 vehicletank301 class no longer exists in the studied edf6 target. the port uses vehicle601_tank rather than a superficially similar class that assumes extra mudguard and antenna parts. the original tank keeps seven wheel pairs and its source mesh, wheel bindings and collision bodies. the target class's animation pose callback rotates the cannon bone's local transform in place every frame according to seat-0 aim pitch. the donor v601_tank.cas has a static rest-pose track for every class-posed bone, so a fresh animation update writes the original local transform before each frame's rotation. if the imported v301 cas lacks the equivalent cannon rest track, the next frame rotates yesterday's already-rotated transform. under the studied failure, repeated turns made the matrix enormous (historically reported above 1e20 within about a second); umbra subsequently received that impossible object-to-cell matrix and culled the visible scene, leaving only sky/grey. the scene-culling symptom was not proof that terrain geometry or textures were corrupt. there is an additional recoil ownership issue. physics writes a ragdoll body through animation_from_ragdoll while cas controls the visible barrel cannon_slide. the bounded fix adds a meshless hidden binding leaf (edf6vc_cannon_slide_physics) with exactly the source barrel's bind frame. physics writes that sibling leaf, while the visible barrel continues its animation. it preserves both directions of the ragdoll/animation relationship rather than letting two systems overwrite one bone. check before attributing the symptom to the map: per-bone rest tracks, wheel count and drawing indices, every ragdoll body-to-bone link, unchanged bind-frame relationships and whether the class modifies local transforms cumulatively. case b: v408 motorcycle — drive parameter layout, rider pose and hand ik the edf4.1 sidecar has three physical wheels and one independent gunner. its native vehiclebike class is absent in edf6; the examined bridge uses a vehicle_car chassis, but this is not the same as the donor's complete vehicle semantics. the original v408 vehicle_setup drivetrain segment has four numbers: grip, slip angle, top speed, max torque. edf6's vehicle_car expects seven numbers in a different meaning/order: friction/brake scale, gear-speed scale, gear-drive scale, steering rate factors and traction parameters. passing the old four numbers directly yields nonsensical steering and zeroed traction fields rather than “similar driving.” the validated narrow mapping for the studied sdl1 families scales three target fields relative to a known base: source base [grip=2.0, slip=0.9, speed=30, torque=100] edf6 base drive [0.8, 30, 0.0075, 0.7, 0.075, 0.3, 0.6] target[0] = 0.8 * grip / 2.0 target[1] = 30 * speed / 30 target[2] = 0.0075 * (torque / 100) * (30 / speed) target[3..6] = base steering/traction values the old slip-angle field has no verified direct vehicle_car equivalent and is not guessed. this mapping was constructed from five original sdl1 request profiles, including weapon688, 700, 721, 739 and 753; it is not a universal conversion for all wheel-based vehicles. the original rider states differ too. vehicle503_bike_driver is a real edf6 driver pose, while vehicle_striker_rear is a sidecar/bench pose; a class missing the bike driver clip falls back rather than borrowing motion from an unrelated skeleton. the donor bike class populates two seat hand-ik grip matrices, but generic vehicle_car does not. the result is a driver's hands reaching toward identity/world-origin transforms rather than the handlebar. the bounded bridge adds named te_ik_l / te_ik_r locator bones under the steering handle and updates the seat matrices in the same role as the native bike. lesson: model/physics correctness does not establish vehicle drivability or rider fidelity. validate each class's parameter schema, pose-state names and live per-frame ik producers. case c: v406 begaruta — preserved six mounts versus remake's eight the source edf4.1 v406 has six weapon mounts. edf6's redesigned v504 has eight. the studied bridge retains the edf6 vehiclebegaruta class path that can consume v406's actual original geometry; it does not retarget the old gun list onto v504's unrelated skeleton and does not silently add missing mounts. a later engine foot lookup requires a named begaruta_foot_node list (ashi_l, ashi_r) not supplied by edf4.1's original sgo. the source-only writer adds that target field while retaining source weapon mounts, three source seat/sight locators, collision and animation events. the pilot may inherit edf6 pilot animation where compatible, but its old rig is not replaced wholesale. same-named weapon archives are isolated under a private resource namespace so a v406 mab muzzle cannot be accidentally resolved against the redesigned v504 model. every locator node, ragdoll proxy, player group (main / addaim) and mab event track must still resolve after conversion. general principles supported by these cases model, cas, mab, sgo, havok and native class are a single runtime contract, even if all files parse independently. when a native class writes a bone's current transform in place, provide an authored rest track or prove a reset before repeated updates. physics and animation cannot both own the same transform without a deliberate and measured mediation layer. a class name or apparently related vehicle model does not establish wheel setup, control-parameter schema, seat pose or ik compatibility. remake weapon and mount counts are not interchangeable with source-era vehicle geometry; keep identity and names coherent. validate separately: structurally parsed data, source meaning, actual runtime class consumption, correct npc/player controls and multiplayer behavior. sources: retained edf41tank.py, edf41bike.py and edf41mech.py from the edf4.1→edf6 r10 hf4 r9 source package. their comments cite historical exact-build binary and in-game debugging; this article reports those findings but does not rerun the original game. a fourth independent vehicle abi: v302 nereid helicopter the source v302 vehiclehelicopter302 can use an edf6 vehicle506_helicopter runtime contract only while preserving its original mdb/cas/havok rig, converting mab locator names, validating real rotor/wheel/seat/muzzle bone references, and retaining the target-added fuel block and final fuel-weapon record. it is not equivalent to replacing a v506 model field. the r9 adapter source is inspected, but no new helicopter gameplay pass is claimed. see the nereid v302 compatibility guide. physics skeleton consistency with moved donor bones moving a turret or suspension bone in the mdb without also moving the corresponding shkt proxy/joint and both sgo ragdoll mapping offsets creates competing rest frames for a single part. the retained source includes a bounded vehicle-ragdoll re-fit algorithm that moves proxies without changing their orientation, recalculates parent joint pivots and reference poses, then validates the result. its companion cas code rebases absolute local animation translations when a bone bind position changes.

moving a model bone is not enough to move a vehicle's physics rig an edf6 vehicle has three coupled coordinate systems: its mdb's model bind pose, its shkt's havok physics bodies and joint pivots, and its sgo's bidirectional bone↔proxy mappings. an animation file can introduce a fourth frame: cas/canm stores local animation poses in the source rig's coordinates, not universal deltas from the current mdb bind pose. replacing the mdb alone can therefore cause a turret to lock, wheels to detach, or an animation to pull the mesh back to a donor skeleton. the retained ragdoll_fit.py and cas_pose.py provide an explicit, bounded approach to this problem. they are source implementations, not proof every new vehicle type passes game runtime. bone ↔ proxy offsets the sgo ragdoll binding has two directional arrays: ragdoll_from_animation: proxy_frame = bone_frame ∘ offset animation_from_ragdoll: bone_frame = proxy_frame ∘ offset a rigid transform combines (translation, quaternion): a ∘ b = (a.t + rotate(a.q, b.t), a.q * b.q). the shkt also contains body proxy world poses, each joint's child- and parent-local anchors, and a ragdoll skeleton reference pose relative to its parent. the retained validator asserts all four interpretations reproduce the same stock bind pose. the vehicle fit is conservative. first require that stock mdb, shkt and sgo binding already agree. for every source bone with a new translation, move its havok proxy to where the corresponding ragdoll_from_animation mapping now puts it. the function does not rotate the proxies: if a moved bone would require changing a proxy's orientation, it rejects the case rather than silently reorienting the constraint graph. then re-establish the joint and pose relationships: keep each child-local joint pivot (transforma) unchanged and move its parent-local pivot (transformb) so both refer to the same world point after the proxy shifts. recompute each ragdoll skeleton's reference translation from the new proxy/parent pair. recompute the animation-from-ragdoll translation offset so each model bone is still reconstructed from its dynamic proxy. preserve valid orientation offsets. run the same bind-pose consistency checks again on the rewritten shkt and binding blob. abort on any mismatch. the implementation uses 1 mm (1e-3) for broad geometry/rotation agreement, a 10 µm (1e-5 m) small-change guard to avoid rewriting float noise, and serialization that preserves the sgo's intended depth-first structure. cas/canm may move the mesh back to the old rest pose an edf6 cas 0x204 with embedded canm 0x300 stores absolute local translations for the studied clips. if a model bone moves from (x,y,z) to (x+dx,y+dy,z+dz), a source animation clip that explicitly keys its original local translation can still place it at (x,y,z) when played. its absolute clips need a (+dx,+dy,+dz) base adjustment to their translation channels; additive animation must keep its original bytes. the source implementation's bounded decoder covers static (kind=0) or quantized animated (kind=1) translation channels with translation = base + key_uint16 × scale, and quaternion rotation channels (kind=2 static or kind=3 float32 key sequence). the rebasing writes only the base of supported translation channels, leaving key arrays, timing, names, clip graph and file size unchanged. there is an important aliasing condition: if two tracks refer to the same canm channel index but require incompatible rebase deltas, the converter must reject the edit. otherwise a single channel mutation changes an unrelated clip or bone. tracks deliberately owned by a runtime plugin can instead be removed from selected clips while retaining their bone names for the renderer. root motion must have one owner a vehicle or boss controller may use cas root-motion curves to move the scene object itself. if that controller translates the object while the mesh also applies the same root-bone animation, displacement is counted twice. the retained strip_bone operation disables selected root translation/rotation tracks (-1 channel indices) only for the named clips, retaining the rest of cas. a separate root_motion decoder extracts planar x/z displacement and unwrapped yaw against the first key. unknown scale-track cases fail closed rather than being silently ignored. safe verification order start by checking stock mdb ↔ shkt ↔ sgo internal consistency; then check moved mdb ↔ refitted shkt ↔ updated binding; then validate absolute cas clip rebasing and channel aliasing; then, separately, test turret movement, wheel articulation, animation transitions, damage and physics state in the actual game. a correct file-level transform graph does not prove runtime vehicle behavior. related: object shkt validation, edf4.1 vehicle adapters and cas controllers.

edf4.1 nereid is not a v506 helicopter with a different model the edf4.1 vehicle302_heli nereid and edf6's v506_heli can share a host runtime class contract, but their models, animation controllers, havok bodies and weapon locators are not interchangeable. a retained source-only adapter preserves the original v302 geometry while using the target edf6 vehicle506_helicopter class. this section describes the adapter's evidenced requirements; it is not a fresh successful helicopter flight test. preserve a coherent source rig the source sgo class is vehiclehelicopter302; edf6's host template uses vehicle506_helicopter. the adapter retains from v302: original converted mdb model and source rab resource identity; original cas animation with corresponding rest pose; original ragdoll/shkt and both animation-to-ragdoll and ragdoll-to-animation bone maps; source durability, helicopter rigid-body data, dead-effect names, and boarding/camera locators; gun mounting coordinates and source-associated mab locator frames. do not graft the v506 cas or its ragdoll binding blob onto the v302 mesh. the adapter's documentation records that the mixed rig shifts the helicopter body and leaves tail-rotor and wheel bone names unresolved. an mdb that parses fine does not pass a class-level animation/physics contract. the edf4.1 object also advertises a second _light lod archive that was not present in the studied source installation. the bounded converter retains the real primary mdb rather than fabricating an unavailable second lod path. what must be adapted to the edf6 class the host expects seven-field seat/boarding rows, while source v302 supplies the first three locator roles and edf6 supplies the remaining riding/animation/input-related fields. the source 302_heli_driver animation token is absent from the target runtime, so copying it as a required target player state is unsafe; the adapter uses the target-registered rider animation contract. a source mab conversion preserves v302's locator node frames while translating the damage-locator names into the target v506 class's expected names. the code checks: every mab locator references a real source model bone; every required host locator name is present; each seat has exactly seven fields, with real seat/camera locator identities; each weapon holder names a real model bone and an existing seat index (or the studied -1 special holder); death-effect bone references all resolve to source geometry; all target-required animation player states and control variables exist in the resulting v302 cas; each ragdoll mapping's bone name resolves against the source mdb. these are explicit checked invariants, not evidence that a conversion succeeds merely because xgs_scene_object_class is renamed. weapon and fuel records the source v302 uses dedicated left/right gatling and laser-mount resources; missiles and napalm have their own model-local emitters. the target v506 has a different setup shape, including an additional fuel block and final fuel weapon. the adapter carries source durability and flight/gun values where the corresponding shape is proven, but retains the target fuel data instead of trying to treat absent source entries as zero or moving the last list element. in the studied setup, two left/right gatling holders map to seat 0, a body missile holder maps to seat 0, and the target's final body/fuel holder carries the profile's -1 seat semantics. the generated weapon resources have private names and cross-check that their mab muzzle locator bones exist in the target weapon mdbs. the source calls are likewise reshaped to preserve v302's three-part setup while supplying the v506 fourth/fuel-compatible component. what this does not prove the retained r9 source only proves the implemented bounded conversion algorithm and its fail-closed checks. it does not independently show that the generated nereid was flown through a full edf6 mission, that every weapon fired in-game, or that its multiplayer ownership/network effects are qualified. the historical r9 object reference inventory lists zero mission uses for this root in that census — it does not mean the engine lacks support or that the asset is universally unused. compare other vehicles' class mismatches, cas player/control variables and map/model resource identity.

edf6 multiplayer object authority — registered objects, local copies and projectile ownership why running identical code on every peer can be wrong the examined edf6 modding layer models objects on all peers, but not all instances represent one registered network object. a vehicle with a registered network identity has a machine responsible for its core simulation. a plugin-created aircraft, drone or summoned creature may be unregistered and exist separately on each peer. the first category requires single-authority decisions; the second may require per-peer simulation while allowing the damage result to count only once. this article describes the specific researched edf6 engine/version and compatibility adapter. it is not a universal law saying edf6 never replicates any spawn, nor does it replace direct network protocol analysis. network flags and authority inputs in the retained online_authority.h model, the network-object word at object +0x128 includes: bits meaning in the examined path bit 0 (0x01) object is remote/operated elsewhere bit 1 (0x02) object is locally operated neither no registered network identity — a local copy a vehicle's native operator resolver uses seat-0's current rider, then possibly the previous rider, then host fallback. this can be wrong for additional plugin work when seat 0 is now empty: after a client leaves, native “last driver” state may still select that client, while the host's npc controller would also run its work. the bounded adapter assigns host authority when there is no live registered seat-0 rider. for an unregistered object, each peer can continue simulating its local copy. a separate copyowner marker (host, here, elsewhere) records the player who created that logical entity so the authoritative damage result is not multiplied across peers. this owner marker is adapter-owned metadata, not a magic bit stored by the original game for every spawn. four decisions that must not be collapsed into one boolean question relevant behavior who simulates the object? registered object: its authority; unregistered local copy: every peer simulates its copy who performs host-only actions? one host handles room-wide operations, such as assigning certain npc drivers where does its damage count? registered vehicle: its authority for npc/vehicle-owned weapons; unregistered copy: the recorded copy owner who is the attacker of a locally fired gun? online, a player firing a registered vehicle's gun may need to be named as attacker so hit authority resolves to that player's machine a player firing a registered vehicle's local gun is a special case: the player's input and the vehicle simulation may be owned by different machines. treating “vehicle is remote” as “this player cannot fire” breaks that use case. conversely, every peer applying an npc turret's damage independently doubles or triples damage. for online rounds whose attacker is named as the player, the mod also had to preserve the native rule that a vehicle-mounted gun does not immediately damage its own ridden vehicle. merely ignoring the attacker pointer is insufficient when the player and the player's current vehicle are distinct objects; explosive splash has a separate filter and is not automatically solved by a single direct-hit exclusion. lifecycle and safety rules in offline sessions, normal local behavior can remain enabled; in online sessions with unknown build-specific session hooks, fail closed rather than declare each peer authoritative. do not use a stale former seat-0 rider as authority for added npc/vehicle behavior. for local copies, separate simulation from who owns the outcome; spawning on every peer is not the same as counting the result on every peer. ensure weak identity/control blocks are checked across object destruction and recreation. object addresses can be reused; a stale raw pointer is not durable identity. verify host/client, enter/exit seat, npc seat adoption, local player gunner, unregistered summon/drone and restart/rejoin paths independently. evidence and limits the retained source includes pure authority, runshere, shotcounts, shooterisattacker, sparesride and mayseatnpc decisions and historical exact-build native-address research. it documents an actual class of desynchronization/double-damage risks. it does not show that every such path was runtime qualified for every multiplayer configuration in r64. source: edf4.1→edf6 r10 hf4 r9 components/compatibility/src/online_authority.h, supported by the preserved edf41net.cpp network-object identity discussion. the addresses and hooks are build-specific; the semantics are the transferable findings. team identity is not projectile authority an actor's native teammanager relation and a controlled-boss pvp lease are separate from per-peer object simulation and damage ownership. native team roles and relation overlays explain target/hazard roles, while typed emitter team propagation and spawn rollback explains why changing a root's team alone may leave bullets and newborn parts in the wrong faction. for a worked example of a custom, bounded per-object event envelope that reuses native networkobject send/receive slots without redefining stock messages, see edf4.1 tag-12 event wire and native child identities. related native edf6 networking systems transporter508 online vehicle delivery native enemy ai authority and rng

edf6 vehicle cameras, physical eye locators and aiming: native evidence scope. this page records the original game's vehicle-camera mechanism, not instructions for implementing custom sights, first-person view, sight magnification steps or a ballistic-range drum. those were design specifications for a separate adapter and are not established as stock edf6 features. the native ride camera is bound to the seat and model in the examined edf6 build, the ride camera's eye and look target can be read from model-authored mab locators referenced by the seat's vehicle_riding_position sgo record. the seat carries parent-bone association, easing, a camera type and xangleadjust. when the animated parent bone moves, the camera's desired eye may move with it. this can place the eye behind the chassis, as observed for gun-attached locators, even though the character remains correctly seated. the main native camera reference lists exact field offsets and examples from blacker, titan, naegling, nix and proteus. see edf4.1/edf5/edf6 boarding records for seat eligibility; seat eligibility alone does not define camera placement. zoom and camera clipping are separate native mechanisms the player camera's fov is derived from weapon/character zoom state in normal follow mode; it is not proven that a vehicle gunner automatically has the same scope input path. the inspected ride camera has its own state and locators. the native camera collision helper can constrain the eye with havok queries, so magnification, obstruction and true gun line-of-fire must not be conflated. in particular, source data containing secondaryfire_type=1 on a vehicle weapon is not sufficient proof that the shipped vehicle ui provides a working optical zoom mode. nor do the historically proposed 1×/3×/6× magnification sequence, a round eyepiece mask, or configurable ballistic zero belong to the established list of stock edf6 features. ballistic sight models are not native game measurements a conventional idealized ballistic range model may use alpha = asin(g*d/v²)/2, with v and g expressed in compatible units. this is a generic model, not a measured edf6 trajectory for every weapon class. edf6 contains guided and class-specific projectile paths, and the gun's parent bone, aim controller and projectile origin can differ from the camera location. sources: edf6 camera knowledge hub, native camera field guide, and the independently analyzed vehicle seat reference. historical custom optic design text is preserved outside the reader wiki in the r118 maintainer audit. no new game runtime test.

mab animation events — clip clocks, event parameters, and owned sound channels why a valid animation may still be silent or mistimed cas/canm describes the animation controller and joint tracks, while mab can supply named, timed events associated with a cas clip. an importer that moves bones but discards mab event tracks can silently lose sounds, muzzle actions, attack windows or hitboxes. the same event name may be meaningful only to a specific source class; do not treat all events as engine-wide commands. for the validated mab v15 family, a track record is 0x10 bytes: first-key offset, key-end pointer, utf-16le track-name pointer and key count. each 0x10-byte key holds an event-name string reference at +0, float32 time at +4, zero at +8, and an embedded sgo\0 parameter pointer at +0x0c. offset bases depend on mab pointer mode (0x03 = mab-relative, 0x83 = owning-struct-relative). full decoder: mab format and pointer migration. a concrete event list the retained mab reader reconstructs data like: clip_name -> [ (event_name, event_time_seconds, event_params), ... ] observed object-specific event families include se, se_stop, the dragonbig401 pair 火炎開始 / 火炎終了, and uforobo events whose parameter sgo includes names such as collision, damage, quake, scale and charge_frame. the embedded sgo can change an event's meaning; dispatching only its bare name is not complete semantic preservation. channel ownership is part of the sound lifecycle for the studied edf4.1 se / se_stop mechanism, an event includes a channel. a negative channel means fire-and-forget, with no retained channel handle. for a nonnegative channel, a new play event stops that channel's old sound first, then owns the resulting handle. a corresponding stop event, replacement, state exit, or object destruction can end that handle. there is no universal fixed playback time limit. the retained compatibility implementation models these rules in channels<handle> and timeline (edf41_sound_channels.h). its timeline reads the animation state and time before/after the update: crossing multiple key times in one update dispatches every crossed event in order. polling the same timestamp repeatedly must not replay a key. a clip/state change resets the relevant event clock. a valid next clip within a multi-clip state may retain channels; a full state exit cancels them. a backward time jump must be interpreted as a clip restart or reset according to the state's known clip layout. this is a source-backed model for specific edf4.1 class behavior, not a generic promise that every mab event should be converted to this dispatcher unchanged. an easy-to-miss attack/sound difference one studied uforobo weapon group owns separate charge and shot audio handles. charge audio ends when leaving its charging state. a looping shot cue persists across rounds only while its play handle remains active; finite shot tails are not indiscriminately cut off on the next round. replacing this with a single global “play sound at fire” call loses the intended behavior. relating mab, sound banks and the game an event may identify its cue by name, but that name still must resolve to an audio bank. in the edf4.1→edf6 research, many source cue names collide with edf6's resident names. the correct semantic route must distinguish bank identity, cue identity, channel ownership and clip timing. see edf4.1 se/voice bank lookup and lifetime. what is and is not proven source and exact-build re evidence: mab key structure, recognized event/argument examples, channels, timeline ordering and the class-specific sound lifecycle. not proven by this article: that every arbitrary edf6 class consumes imported mab event names, that a copied clip has identical timing under a different animation controller, or that every source cue is present in a newly built bank. sources: retained mab_legacy.py (mab_events, mab_event_params) and edf41_sound_channels.h in the edf4.1→edf6 r10 hf4 r9 source package; source comments cite exact historical edf4.1/edf6 binary investigations. no fresh runtime sound-playback test was performed in r63.

edf4.1 audio in edf6 — se cue names, bank priority, voice playback and shutdown one cue name may belong to multiple banks the documented edf4.1→edf6 sound port faced 1,469 edf4.1 weapon-effect cue names. 1,087 names already appeared in edf6, while 332 did not. a naive “merge every source cue into the active stock bank” strategy changes the meaning of common names. a naive “load an additional bank and search all banks equally” can also shadow native edf6 effects. the inspected edf6 sound system looks up a cue by name and bank type, returning a (bank pointer, cue index) pair from the first eligible matching bank. in the examined implementation, se callers request type 0, while voices use a distinct bank category. the source-only compatibility design therefore registers the edf4.1 se bank under a private bank type and uses this priority: 1. native edf6 se bank (normal type-0 lookup) 2. imported edf4.1 se bank (private-type lookup when stock misses) 3. finite resident fallback for selected source cues if the imported bank is absent for source objects that explicitly need their edf4.1 identity, the retained implementation has source-aware exception handling; this is not a universal native-first policy for every sound in every mod. in particular, the finite fallback table avoids substituting an indefinitely looping cue where no caller can stop it. acb identity is not just the file name the edf4.1 weapon se bank (tikyuux_se.acb) carried a name/guid that collided with edf6's own bank identity. its acfmd5hash also belonged to a different acf configuration. the documented converter patches fixed-width identity fields to form edf41_weapon_se.acb, using a distinct bank name/guid and the target acf hash, without moving the @utf tables. these are bounded observations about the exact studied cri acb 1.23 and edf6 runtime, not instructions for arbitrary acb rewrite. why the same mods path works for acb but fails for awb the examined engine has two file-access paths: an acb may be read through the game's hooked/redirected stream layer. an app:/sound/pc/... request can reach a virtual /cri_bind/... path and be redirected under mods/sound/pc. the awb audio table of contents can be opened by cri's own filesystem, bypassing the game stream hook. a seemingly successful awb existence test and accepted _list.awe are therefore insufficient: the cri toc load can still return null. in the documented fix, voice loading requests an actual readable path such as ./mods/sound/pc/edf41_voice.ja.awb. with a raw virtual /cri_bind/... path, the game-level existence probe and awe reader succeeded but cri's toc load did not. this explains the otherwise misleading symptom “bank exists, no voice plays.” do not automatically transfer this exact directory convention to every loader version; the principle is to find which subsystem performs the final physical open. voice awb / awe and subtitles edf4.1 provides ja and en source voice audio. the investigated converter promotes the source awb version byte to 2 for the target-compatible bank and writes an awe v2 list containing names, wave ids and cue duration derived from each hca wave's header. subtitles use edf6's voice table rather than replacing its native rows. the game looks up the caption using the voice cue name after stripping one trailing _e or _s, never an embedded substring. when extra caption data is unavailable, the documented source-only approach retains the cue identity and falls back to available language text rather than deleting a cue. the audio source intentionally includes only two recorded language banks. a locale without a matching edf4.1 recording may fall back to ja and then en, but subtitle language and recording language remain separate decisions. bank lifetime can cause a crash on exit the sound system uses a reference-counted bank cache. the loaded se bank must return its cache reference before the game destroys the sound system. if a mod retains its final reference until a later atexit destructor, cleanup can attempt to unregister a bank from a null sound-system pointer. the researched failure manifested as a shutdown crash rather than a gameplay sound failure. the maintained adapter releases its cache reference at the application's normal shutdown boundary, while the sound system still exists. this is a broader lesson for native mod loaders: successful sound playback does not prove correct resource lifetime. status and verification boundaries the retained evidence combines target-binary path analysis, historical runtime diagnosis and source implementation. it does not prove every cue in every user installation plays correctly. verify bank identity, cue hit/miss counts, cri toc success, playback, voice-text lookup, locale switching and shutdown separately. offsets and hook locations are build-specific, not public api contracts. sources: edf4.1→edf6 r10 hf4 r9 edf41_sounds.py, edf41sound.cpp, edf41_sound_fallbacks.inc, edf41_sound_channels.h and the source-only audio r5 audit. this article documents the findings; it redistributes no original acb/awb game audio. further native edf references edf4.1 native soundcontroller and radio

edf4.1 dragonbig401 — timed breath, glide versus hover and the edf6 class mismatch the concrete class mismatch edf4.1's giant dragon breathes flamebullet02 during attack windows keyed by mab animation events 火炎開始 (“flame begin”) and 火炎終了 (“flame end”). the original weapon fires one projectile per simulation frame from a named mab muzzle locator 発射口 in the locator's local +z direction, with a random angular cone up to 0.2 radians. the investigated edf6 dragonsmall donor class instead fires flamebullet01 fireballs, and its existing event dispatcher does not register the edf4.1 pair. merely importing the old mesh, cas and mab while keeping the class's new firing action does not preserve attack semantics. this is a direct example where a file parser can be correct while the port's gameplay is not. source event windows and firing direction the retained compatibility research decodes each source attack state's mab begin/end times, looks up the corresponding cas state, and observes the active animation player. when the player enters that state's interval and the actor is alive, the adapter creates flamebullet02 using the target projectile factory. for each shot, the implementation: reads the source muzzle world transform. samples tilt 0 ... 0.2 radians and spin 0 ... 2π, constructs a normalized direction around the muzzle's local +z. builds the shot transform at the original muzzle position. attaches a projectile parameter block, team ownership and owner weak reference. uses the source projectile configuration for speed, lifetime, width, hit-stop, color and custom sgo parameters. computes the documented source damage scaling as actor_level × 0.00375 in the examined class path. the projectile factory and memory fields are exact-build native contracts. a generic script-level implementation cannot assume these offsets or that the projectile factory accepts another class's parameter structure. glide attack is a behavior choice, not a replacement fireball the source 4.1 behavior chooses between two attack forms at approach: attack form intended behavior fly_glide_attack pass over the target while breathing flame, return to glide after the clip fly_attack hover and breathe during the clip's source flame window the studied branch makes the two choices with approximately equal probability. replacing both with edf6's donor fireball volley changes the animation, trajectory and damage opportunity. source ranges also differ: the recorded wander radius was 500 units versus 100 in the donor's relevant sampled cruise path; the source-ground-fight radius was 500 rather than the donor field's 100. these are specific researched class constants, not default values for all aerial enemies. the same adapter tracks knockdown animation states, a source settle/rest condition and return-to-glide behavior. those systems must be handled independently of the flame projectile's emission window. why this matters for asset authors a faithful enemy import must reconcile at least four distinct layers: model/locator data (mdb/mab), timed clip events (cas/mab), native ai/state transitions and projectile class/parameter semantics. the presence of a visually correct flamethrower animation does not establish that shots use the source damage or fire at the source timings. this is not a general animation retargeting recipe. an arbitrary donor class can require its own named cas players, controller variables and init parameters; see cas player/vcontrol abi. scope and evidence the retained edf41dragon.cpp documents exact edf4.1 binary and edf6 target-class reverse engineering and a source-only compatibility implementation whose hooks are conditional on the edf41_dragon sgo marker. unmarked native edf6 dragons remain on their original path. the r9 checkpoint is offline-qualified source work; it is not an independent new windows/runtime verification of dragonbig401 in r63. the original dragonbig sound-preset/bank mapping was later recovered statically from the source sgo/exe in r14/r17: five sound roles plus a separate ragdoll-contact preset, using a shared dragon sound bank. target dragonsmall slot 0 introduces an extra eight-frame-cooldown hurt roar absent from original dragonbig; its sound parity is not runtime-confirmed. see dragonbig401 source audio roles and mab event timing. source: edf4.1→edf6 r10 hf4 r9 components/compatibility/src/edf41dragon.cpp, mab_legacy.py, and its retained historical exact-build comments.

edf 4.1 / edf 5 / edf 6 cas and canm: actual record layouts and key conversion the games have different cas state-controller layouts and canm key encodings. a version-word edit can make a file look plausible to a parser while still mapping the wrong commands or rotations. this guide describes the measured 2026 paired-file and exact-binary research, not an independently established universal conversion law for every modded asset. container generations layer edf 4.1 edf 5 edf 6 cas\0 version word 0x200 0x203 0x204 cas data command record 0x24 bytes 0x34 bytes 0x34 bytes embedded canm version 0x200 0x200 0x300 canm channel record 0x20 bytes 0x20 bytes 0x30 bytes a studied cas header uses 0x30 bytes, with its embedded-canm offset at cas +0x08, followed by the counts and offsets for tcontrol, vcontrol, animation groups and bones. the embedded canm begins on a 16-byte boundary. cas string references include signed relative offsets to utf-16le names. do not transplant offsets from the old layout after inserting new records. a canm has a 0x20-byte header, 28-byte clip records and 8-byte track records. each track contains a uint16 bone index and three signed 16-bit indices for translation, rotation and scale (-1 = no channel). clip records hold a name pointer, duration, step/frame interval, frame count, and track count/location. edf5/4.1 canm 0x200 channels the measured 0x20-byte channel stores a keyed/static flag, count, three float32 base values, three float32 scale/step values, and an offset to key data. animated xyz keys are stored as three uint16 integers per key. for each component: [ v_i(k)=\operatorname{float32}\bigl(base_i + \operatorname{float32}(key_i(k)\cdot step_i)\bigr). ] in the studied rotation lane, the resulting xyz values are euler angles in radians, applied in source rotation order rz · ry · rx. floating-point evaluation order matters when comparing exact converted bytes. edf6 canm 0x300 channel kinds the channel expands to 0x30 bytes: eight float32 values (base xyzw and multiplier xyzw), then four signed 32-bit values (key offset, kind, count, reserved). in the analyzed native channels: kind role stored values 0 static vector base xyz (w and steps set appropriately) 1 animated quantized vector base + uint16 xyz key × multiplier 2 static quaternion base float32 xyzw 3 animated quaternion one float32 xyzw quadruplet per key the target engine reads quaternion vector data with aligned vector loads. the native writer therefore places quaternion key blocks on 16-byte boundaries. for every reused source channel, a converter must separate vector and quaternion roles, because edf5 can reuse a zero-valued channel for translation and euler rotation, while edf6 needs different representations. euler → quaternion: not merely degree conversion the examined edf6 path converts source euler radians to an xyzw quaternion through an explicit sequence of x, y and z rotations, applying float32 rounding and the target runtime's sinf/cosf behavior. if the source has quantized keys, the exact original unquantized authoring angles may already be lost. producing a geometrically equivalent rotation does not guarantee byte-exact target quaternions. measured evidence from retained matched-file tests: all 836 analyzed cas files across the three root.cpk corpora could be parsed and round-tripped under the retained model. among 230 same-name edf5/edf6 pairs, 66 matched byte-for-byte after conversion; 21 target files were substantively re-authored. the other 143 paired conversions were byte-identical apart from quaternion float differences and, in 69 cases, quaternion key-block ordering. 1,487/1,487 measured static quaternions matched bitwise; among 1,958,796 animated quaternion keys, 88,038 matched bitwise, with the others differing within the source quantization/float rounding envelope reported by the original analysis. 204/205 tested edf4.1 cas assets converted under the bounded implementation. giantant_hokao contained uncommon source command ids 2/3 without demonstrated mappings and was intentionally rejected. these numbers are corpus results, not proof that arbitrary custom cas variants or future game builds have the same command set. cas commands also need semantic remapping command ids changed between generations; the observed converter mapped known commands by same-named control/state/slot position in paired assets, not by blindly adding a constant to every opcode. edf4.1's 0x24-byte data structs expand to 0x34 and inherited pointers/unused words require clearing where the destination native representation does. unknown command identities must fail closed rather than adopting the nearest numeric opcode. retargeting after a skeleton/bind-pose change if an mdb bone's bind translation changes, absolute canm animation translations can pull it back to its original location. the qualified source procedure computes a per-bone local translation delta, applies it only to explicitly named absolute clips and modifies the base xyz of a channel, leaving quantized keys and time steps intact. additive/recoil clips should not automatically receive this offset. a channel shared by two tracks needing different translation adjustments cannot be patched unambiguously and must be rejected. removing a runtime-plugin-owned bone track also differs from changing its key values. quaternion rotation poses follow edf's row-vector matrix convention; directly substituting the more common column-vector matrix will produce a wrong world-space result. evidence: retained cas_legacy.py, cas_pose.py source and their embedded research notes/tests. no new native game run was performed for this release. see cas player/controller requirements and mab record format.

edf6 cas player groups, controller variables and safe trackless grafts why can a converted object appear to have valid bones and clips but still crash when its native edf6 class spawns? the class can require named cas controller groups (players) and variables that did not exist in edf4.1. the important distinction: player group, state and track a cas anmgroup owns named states (mcanm) and their animation/control data. a class may resolve an entire player group by name during construction. in the examined edf6 path, a missing player can produce an invalid unchecked lookup. a missing state or clip within an existing player may instead be tolerated, which does not make the missing whole group safe. the retained example is an edf4.1 ufocarrier301 grafted onto the target edf6 ufocarrier508 class: the edf6 class looks for in_ring and out_ring animation players, representing motion absent from the old carrier. removing their graphical motion is fine; omitting required names is not. variable (vcontrol) safety a target edf6 class may set controller variables by name every frame. the analyzed lookup for a missing setter target returns -1; the setter then treats that index as a valid array position and can write out of bounds. a missing getter-only variable can return 0.0, changing tuning behavior without an immediate crash. known requirements for the studied berserker-like class include v_move_angle, v_move_velocity, v_tilt_dir and v_tilt_lerp during update, plus v_damage_reaction_ratio when hit. a vcontrol record in this family occupies 0x14 bytes: byte offset field in measured record +0x00 relative name reference +0x04 mode flag; 0 plain variable, 1 follows a tcontrol +0x08 variable kind +0x0c initial float32 value +0x10 additional word / tcontrol index when applicable a bounded graft may copy plain donor variables that the source cas lacks. variables coupled to another tcontrol require extra index rewriting and were intentionally refused by the retained safe implementation. trackless grafting for target-runtime compatibility the source-compatible approach does not copy the donor's animation motion onto the edf4.1 model. it inserts only missing named player/controller structures and appends trackless canm clips preserving their donor names, loop flag, duration, step and frame count. the target class can find and trigger the required control paths without moving alien donor bones. the measured graft procedure: parse the source-compatible edf6 cas and the edf6 donor cas; reject other/unknown generations. find target-required anmgroup names and plain vcontrol names that are missing from the source cas. append donor animation groups and their associated tcontrols, renumbering control indices against the target's existing table. append corresponding canm clips, but with zero tracks, and remap old clip indices inside appended tcontrols. recompute signed relative offsets for strings and records after the new clip table has grown. refuse data commands whose argument layout is not proven to contain only a tcontrol index. the retained code permits data-command ids 0 and 4 when their discriminator at +0x14 is 2; it treats mcanm +0x20 as a possible tcontrol index, with the special 0xbf800000 sentinel meaning no tcontrol. these are measured in that grafting path, not a specification of every possible custom cas opcode. some class-required states can be aliases of existing states, preserving a compatible state name without inventing new movement. a separate hollow procedure clears clip track counts for placeholder donor motion while keeping the state/clip metadata. only explicitly identified runtime-owned tracks should be stripped. practical failure signs symptom first thing to inspect immediate crash when object spawns missing class-required anmgroup player name crash after updates or on taking damage missing class-written vcontrol or invalid index model animates into donor pose donor tracks were copied instead of adding trackless clips wrong clip or broken string new tcontrol/clip indices or relative offsets were not rebased odd lean/recoil without crash missing getter-only variable reads zero or additive clip semantics changed this information explains one measured class/controller abi family, not a guarantee that every edf6 class uses the same names or tolerates identical missing states. evidence: retained cas_graft.py, cas_legacy.py and cas_pose.py source; exact edf6 binary lookup analyses described in those source comments. the grafted content is source-only compatibility evidence, not a new windows/runtime pass. for canm channel bytes and euler→quaternion handling, see actual cross-generation cas/canm conversion. deliberate missing variables versus true missing-controller defects do not graft every target-only cas variable automatically. in the preserved edf4.1 soldier profile, target v_vehicle_grip_l_ik_target and v_vehicle_grip_r_ik_target are intentionally left absent: target code checks -1 indices before writing, while the source cas lacks a matching consumer. this is unlike a required player/control-variable absence that the native class dereferences unchecked. related source-only policies for torso-axis mode and ledge-climb are in friendly soldier skeleton compatibility. absolute canm clip rebasing is not a trackless graft the studied edf6 cas 0x204 / canm 0x300 format stores absolute local transforms in selected clips. if mdb bind translations change, a source absolute clip can pull a bone to the old position. a retained source-only rig/cas rebasing procedure adjusts only supported translation channel bases and rejects shared channel indices that require incompatible deltas. it leaves additive clips and keyframes unchanged and avoids double application of root motion.

edf4.1 soldiers need different aim-spine axes and animation policies a friendly ranger, fencer/heavyarmor or pale wing from edf4.1 may share an edf6 native runtime class while preserving its own mdb skeleton, cas animation and weapon model. the source investigation found three independent failure modes: a different local axis for torso aiming, an incomplete foreign-weapon ik chain, and a ledge-climb animation that can enter but never finish on older cas assets. those are runtime class semantics, not faults in file serialization. torso twist: human_direction_adjust is not an interchangeable number the native human_direction_adjust key selects model spine bones and an axis mode for the target class to rotate toward the aim yaw. in the examined edf6 implementation, mode 2 rotates around the bone's local x axis; the source's mode 1 rotates around local y. the retained census found: studied model corpus up-axis of spine bind matrix human_direction_adjust mode edf6 native soldiers, 101 sampled models local x 2 edf4.1 native soldiers, 31 sampled models local y 1 if a converter uses the target edf6 default mode 2 with a preserved edf4.1 spine, yaw aim becomes a forward/back bend instead of a torso twist. the safe source algorithm reads the bind-pose up-axis of the actual converted model and derives the matching mode rather than globally setting every imported soldier to 1. mixed/ambiguous up-axes fail closed. the stated 101/31 counts come from retained historical source annotations and were not independently re-censused against installed game assets in this release. hand grip and weapon animation form a chained transform a source weapon's look, muzzle and hands depend on its own mdb/cas/mab and named ik locators. the analyzed native weapon-grip path composes transforms in the direction: grab_frame × weapon_ik × weapon_node_world a one-time wrist/bind correction cannot replace a per-frame, weapon-dependent animation ik producer. the retained investigations report 8–30 degrees of remaining grip mismatch when attempting that shortcut. for source-exact rendering, keep the correct weapon model and named animation/control transforms together and validate their actual class consumption. two target-only variables, v_vehicle_grip_l_ik_target and v_vehicle_grip_r_ik_target, are intentionally not grafted into edf4.1 soldier cas in this supported profile. the edf6 native class checks whether their indices are -1 before writing them; the source cas has no target ik consumer. fabricating two dangling variables would not create a working ik chain, and naïvely copying donor tcontrol blocks would require correct index rebasing. why a soldier can freeze upright at a ledge the target edf6 climbing behavior can enter a ledge-climb native state for an npc. four named animation states are expected on the cas main player: common_elude_large_up common_elude_middle_over common_elude_middle_up common_elude_small_up the studied edf4.1 soldier cas has none of those four. if the target human_climb_settings remains active, a ledge test enters climb, tries to play a missing state (-1 index), and receives failure. the old walking/standing clip remains active, with an endless/looping end condition; the climb-state exit waits for that clip to finish. the soldier may therefore remain motionless indefinitely, apparently in an idle attention stance, while ai movements are ignored. the bounded source fix removes human_climb_settings when all four named climb states are absent, restoring edf4.1's non-climbing traversal. if only some states are present, it rejects the resource rather than forcing an arbitrary subset. leaving the key absent is safe in the studied target build because the native climb readers are guarded by a null check; route exploration then reports zero climb height. only alias source motion to semantically equivalent target states the retained cas adapter synthesizes missing target state names using source animation states with matching roles: unarmed movement reuses source unarmed movement, knockout reuses down, bike rider reuses the source bike seat, and ranger sprint uses the corresponding run clip. it does not invent ledge climbing, sword moves, jump-dash-lance actions or npc talk gestures when edf4.1 has no matching animation role. one-shot versus looping state types must remain coherent. evidence boundary: these rules are based on source code plus retained exact-build static reverse engineering and historical symptoms. this release does not contain new retail edf6 npc traversal or visual-ik tests. see friendly-npc hybrid runtime, cas and animation players, and mab event identity.

edf 4.1 map mapo conversion: object-row relayout and exact-size traps scope: source-backed offline reconstruction of one nw_hillycity_light edf4.1→edf6 map. these offsets and counts describe the particular legacy/target mapo record family, not a universal mapo revision rule. the two layers that must not be confused a mac file is an outer map container. map.mapo is one embedded payload. byte positions, sizes and digests for the whole container are therefore not mapo dimensions. a historical reconstruction mistakenly treated 7,872,840 bytes (whole mac) as a mapo-sized figure; that claim and the derived missing-edge hypothesis were disproved. the verified source mapo in this case is 3,034,994 bytes, with a 0x58-byte header and 44,213 object rows, each 0x38 bytes. the edf6-compatible serializer expands the core to a 0x60-byte header and 0x3c-byte object rows. core field older source layout reconstructed target layout change mapo header 0x58 (88 b) 0x60 (96 b) +8 b object row 0x38 (56 b) 0x3c (60 b) +4 b per row object rows 44,213 44,213 preserved in this map object table growth — 44,213 × 4 +176,852 b header + table growth — 8 + 176,852 +176,860 b this is a record relayout, not a demand to add 176,860 arbitrary padding bytes at the file end. pointer tables, offsets and later payloads need to agree with the new locations. why the final mapo is much larger the converted payload also carries additional target structures including collision and collapse data. in the observed r1d reconstruction these were 291 groups, 2,863 t58 pieces, 8,980 t50 outer records and 386,865 t50 subrecords, with zero t50 edges. those figures are a case-specific evidence census, not an engine-wide rule that t50 always has no edges; other native edf6 maps do have substantial collapse-link graphs. the reconstruction yielded a 6,816,056-byte mapo candidate. that exactly matches the retained historical target length but does not match its sha-256. an assembled 7,872,840-byte mac also matches the old whole-mac length without matching the historical bytes. therefore the formerly suspected missing bulk payload was not the remaining problem; ordering, serialization and source semantics remain. how to validate a converter identify the outer container size and the inner mapo size independently. read the actual object-row count before changing a stride; never borrow an object's count from a donor map. rebuild offsets and relative references after header and record expansion. validate auxiliary t58/t50 placement and source/collision-body identity independently of total byte length. compare the exact target digest only when the relevant target build and original bytes are available. do not mix mapo table families the separate 0x1c (28-byte) mapo item stride documented elsewhere in this wiki applies to another measured table family. it is not an alternative spelling of this 0x38→0x3c object-row relayout. always identify the table/record family before reusing a stride. evidence: edf41_r1d_mapo_core_relayout_closure_2026-11-14_r1.json, r1d map reconstruction outputs, source/target size and hash controls. evidence class: offline reconstruction, not game-runtime verification. related: r1d collision-body eligibility and mapb table rebasing.

edf 4.1 navigation reconstruction: collision-body eligibility versus group ranking a source map may expose the correct set of geometry groups without exposing the correct active collision bodies within those groups. this distinction is central to the studied edf4.1→edf6 nw_hillycity_light navigation reconstruction. current technical correction a later source-semantic reconstruction does reproduce the exact historical 4,971 body-level footprint census from 4,994 pre-dedupe instances and 23 fixb semantic removals, while retaining the exact 65/1,405/251/1,153/1 group/placement/rotation census. it is an offline candidate, not recovered historical source or byte-exact final r1d hkt. the r75 best natural candidate is 381,544 bytes (+32 from the historical target); the 381,528-byte (+16) path uses a non-natural group swap. selected-source audits through r100 close simple body-role, source-base, mapb placement identity and shared havok-object alias hypotheses in this corpus. see current r1d authority rules, mapo transform evidence, and source identity/audit details. the older sections below are retained as historical diagnostics from before the r32/r75 source recovery. they describe then-open hypotheses, not the latest pending tests. what is actually reproduced a source-static group rank based on geometry transformed by each body's motionstate reproduces the retained historical selection census: measured quantity reconstructed / historical source-static selected groups 65 selected placements 1,405 exact-zero rotations 251 yaw-only rotations 1,153 mixed x/z rotations 1 historical active body footprints 4,971, still unresolved these equalities do not prove the historical algorithm has been recovered. multiple group selections can yield the same aggregated placement census, and group membership alone does not determine the eligible groupgeometry.pieces set. the hard distinction between the historical note and retained code the historical classifier was described as testing a body-level condition max_xz >= 5.75. the retained r1/r1b harness, however, ranks full source-static groupgeometry, counts primitive pieces and contains no persisted body-filter implementation. a later reconstructed filter is therefore a hypothesis about missing logic, not proven source code. the latest recovered natural experiment ranks the full geometry by xz area, requires at least one active raw body and then applies the raw max_xz body filter. it reproduces the historical placement/rotation census but produces 5,026 footprints: 55 too many. a prior r18 baseline produced 4,948: 23 too few under a different candidate. the figures are results of different semantics, not a monotonically converging universal threshold. further structural searches did not find a natural category of the 13–14 problematic body cases whose contributions simply account for the missing 55. one remaining known parser/body failure (sk_car_bus01_hk.polymsh3) must stay fail-closed; adding arbitrary bodies to hit the count is not evidence. why the exact 4,971 matters the historical r1d target removes 277 triangles from the prior exact r1c navigation output, with 1,562 vertices and 2,651 triangles. a candidate already matched the tile counts and exact nvmd, yet the low hkt remained 16 bytes larger and differed in sha-256. matching geometry statistics, target byte length and runtime traversal are three separate tests. for this reason a correct reproduction requires natural eligibility and exact source-backed ordering rather than numerical fitting. do not change the 5.75 threshold, inject bodies manually, swap arbitrary groups or delete a seam record to make a length or sha match. earlier proposed discriminator (subsequently audited) compare source hkplistshape cached aabb semantics against bounds recomputed from its children with real convex-radius and motion-state behavior; preserve the same population and group ranking rules. if that produces a natural 4,971, record the named group set, per-group body membership, geometry method and deterministic reproduction, not only a count. evidence: exact historical r1d oracle; edf41_r1d_active_builder_frontier_2026-11-14_r18.json and superseding r19; associated listshape-family and linked-primitive censuses. status: unresolved offline reverse engineering; not an exact nav or runtime pass. related: mapo object-row relayout, source binding and exact r1c/r1d controls, havok collision and navigation architecture.

edf5 → edf6 conversion: which parts can be carried across? edf5 and edf6 reuse recognizable names and resource roles, but the same filename extension does not guarantee that an edf5 payload is valid inside edf6. reliable conversion works per subsystem and per observed target profile. conversion at a glance subsystem what the research establishes unsafe shortcut mdb model vertex declarations, materials, texture bindings, bone/object relationships may differ header version bump or one universal vertex stride material/shader shader, ordered parameters, samplers, sampler state and vertex layout are coupled rename the shader alone texture masks native target pairs can be rebaked with family-specific packing one global fpr channel shuffle canm animation edf5 0x200 to edf6 0x300 changes channel layout and rotation representation rewrite version field only cas wrapper has independent generation and references surrounding canm assume the wrapper version equals canm version mab validated v15 0x03→0x83 migration changes internal pointer bases;
