1,318 paired resources show separate content retargeting assume all mab offsets are absolute or treat re-encoding as gameplay parity mad collision older havok data must be structurally re-encoded into target hknp layouts copy old motion/shape bytes into new headers hkt/nvmd navigation semantic geometry and target binary output are separately important assume matching triangle counts prove correctness mission bvm → ac event graph, scheduler, control/dataflow and engine api semantics need translation text-only opcode replacement mission rmpa dedicated target record layout and reference rebasing reuse the map-rmpa converter archive/resource lookup container and path identity must be preserved across packaging rename every .trb to .mdx example: one mdb leaf mesh changes even when index count does not a paired native palm example found an edf5 leaf mesh with 888 vertices and 1,944 indices whose edf6 counterpart had 1,380 vertices and the same 1,944 indices. another paired leaf mesh changed 36 → 72 vertices, keeping 144 indices. tangent/normal/uv seam splitting changed the vertex representation without changing the polygon index count. the study also showed that an edf5 snd_map_simple_clip material does not generally map to one universal edf6 shader: of 38 paired source materials, only one native target used snd_brdf_map_simple_clip; other target families differed. that one target still changed its parameter abi. a shader-string-only experiment produced black leaves; restoring a coherent material contract resolved that observed failure. this is a paired-case result, not a rule that every edf5 leaf must increase its vertices by a fixed ratio. example: binormal migration must be contextual in retained compatibility-pair research, tangent and texcoord could remain stable while binormal changed to: edf6 binormal = (-source.x, -source.y, -source.z, source.w) the retained fixture measured 16,796 half-float binormals and 1,093 float32 binormals matching that sign behaviour; the 1,093 sampled float32 tangents matched exactly. this is a cross-game migration observation, not a command to negate binormals already correct inside a native edf6 file. example: version numbers are not the animation format the studied canm generations differ in record size and semantic encoding: edf5: 0x200, roughly 0x20-byte channel records and euler-radian animation representation; edf6: 0x300, roughly 0x30-byte channel records with xyzw base/multiplier/encoding fields and quaternion animation representation. the associated cas wrapper may be a separate generation. a conversion tool should parse both generations explicitly and retain unknown data safely instead of assuming that the first successful parse proves compatible animation behaviour. conversion evidence levels a conversion can be: structurally valid — reader/writer and invariants pass. source-semantically reconciled — events, references or vertex/sample semantics are retained against studied source/target data. target-runtime accepted — the exact modified asset/game build loads and behaves in the relevant test. gameplay faithful — the particular behaviour has been compared at runtime, not inferred from file layout alone. these are progressively stronger claims. a source-only pass is valuable research but not automatic gameplay parity. for the detailed rules, open mab v15 pointer migration, mdb model structure, native material families, animation formats, collision and navigation and mission events. evidence status: exact paired same-asset source/target observations for several mdb/animation rules, sampled native shader corpora, source/binary collision research, mission translator and runtime case studies. no universal across-all-assets converter is claimed.

edf archives and resource lookup: cpk, rab, marc and cmpl a game asset has at least three separate questions: where it is found, how its container bytes are decoded, and whether the decoded content has the correct format for the game that reads it. passing one stage does not establish correctness of the other two. cpk: finding an asset in the installed game studied edf6 installations use criware cpk packages. a read-only catalog can inspect toc/@utf records to expose virtual paths without extracting an entire installed game. in one observed installation, root.cpk, chunk01.cpk, chunk02.cpk and dx11.cpk supplied 9,717 virtual asset paths. the number reflects that exact installation, not a universal constant. for compressed entries, the researched path uses direct random access and crilayla decompression in memory. there was an offline-qualified decoder path for literal, backreference and variable-length-code cases, but that qualification did not by itself prove every shipped compressed asset under a windows runtime. itoc was not needed for the four observed toc-backed cpks; that does not prove it is unnecessary in all cpks. rab and mrab: embedded resources still have their own formats rab/mrab are resource-container roles. a reconstructed rab with a valid archive directory can still hold an invalid mdb, texture, sgo or another payload. edf5 and edf6 share enough ssa archive grammar for common tooling but not enough to declare every edf5 archive byte-copy-safe in edf6. a source-side conversion needs both a valid target container and target-compatible contained resources. the observed mdb simple_clip/high-lod foliage repair is an example: archive packaging and the material/shader abi had to be coherent together for a runtime-positive visual result. marc: a specific cross-game difference the compared edf5 and edf6 marc grammar is similar, but a measured map-entry field u1 has different values: edf5 2, edf6 0. this is a verified per-profile difference, not permission to add a global offset transform to all marc records. cmpl: corrected token interpretation the researched cmpl token decoder is: length = (token & 0xf) + 3; position = token >> 4; an older interpretation that used the high nibble for length and the low twelve bits for position was superseded. wrong token interpretation can appear to decompress some inputs while invalidating conclusions about other data. virtual paths and cache freshness logical asset identity can span multiple archives and optional mod overlays. paths and registration names need normalized comparison appropriate to the game's resource namespace. a stale toc or cached catalog can present the wrong apparent resource inventory even if archive parsing is correct. never silently resolve an ambiguous resource stem to an arbitrary model. a resource browser should preserve read-only access to the installed archives, report unresolved identities, and keep archive lookup, decompression, native payload interpretation and actual in-game behavior as separately testable steps. for deeper detail see cpk and crilayla, rab/marc/cmpl measured contracts and resource identity/virtual paths. diagnosing “the model is valid but the map crashes” in one checked desert-map conversion, a byte-valid mdb was delivered under a .trb registration and entered the wrong resource loader. independently, an obsolete cmpl compressor damaged 45/76 model bodies while preserving their first bytes. these demonstrate two separate checks: typed registration must match the payload, and decoded content must be verified in full. see the detailed case study.

rab and mrab: the ssa archive header, entry table and name resolution rab and mrab archives are named-resource containers. in the edf5/edf6 samples we inspected, both use an ssa\0 header. each entry has its own name, resource type and compressed or opaque payload; the entire archive does not represent one indivisible model or texture. this page describes the measured binary parsing contract, independently of how mods should combine their changes. container header the inspected ssa header occupies 0x28 bytes and consists of ten little-endian 32-bit words. positions below are relative to the beginning of the archive: file offset size field meaning +0x00 4 magic ascii ssa followed by nul +0x04 4 version container version; observed value depends on input family +0x08 4 content_start start of entry payload area in the measured serializer +0x0c 4 max_comp maximum entry payload byte length +0x10 4 max_dec maximum declared decompressed entry length +0x14 4 entry_count number of entry records +0x18 4 info_pos absolute offset of entry-record array +0x1c 4 names_pos offset of name lookup table +0x20 4 type_count number of resource type strings +0x24 4 type_table offset of resource type reference table the tested normalizing writer places info_pos at 0x28. a parser should read these offsets from the header, not hardcode every archive to the normalized writer's layout. validate info_pos + entry_count × 0x20 <= file_length before reading the table. one entry is 0x20 bytes entry record i starts at info_pos + i × 0x20: record offset size interpretation in the canonical parser +0x00 s32 relative offset from this entry's start to its utf-16le name +0x04 u32 stored payload byte size (csize) +0x08 u32 index into the archive's resource type strings +0x0c u32 entry-specific hd attribute +0x10 u32 ft1 attribute +0x14 u32 ft2 attribute +0x18 u32 absolute file offset to the entry payload (doff) +0x1c u32 z / additional entry attribute the two most important offset rules are not interchangeable: entry_address = info_pos + i * 0x20 name_address = entry_address + signed_name_relative_offset payload = file_bytes[absolute_doff : absolute_doff + csize] a reader that mistakenly interprets name_rel as absolute will look up unrelated bytes. a reader must reject out-of-range names, unterminated utf-16 strings and payload spans extending beyond the file. name lookup and type-string references the measured lookup array at names_pos consists of 8-byte records: a 32-bit relative string offset and a 32-bit entry index. the string offset is relative to the lookup record's own address. the type table is an array of 32-bit signed relative offsets; each is likewise relative to its own table word and points to a utf-16le type name. this means there are three distinct identities: entry name: case-sensitive resource name, such as a dds/mdb resource path. type string: the semantic resource kind, resolved from the type table. type index: a local index into that archive's type table, not a globally portable type identifier. the exact named entry is the stable merge identity across inputs. a writer may rebuild the local type index when combining multiple archives, but should preserve baseline type-string order and append new types rather than assuming that two input index numbers have identical meanings. payload and cmpl boundaries each entry's blob is the stored payload. a cmpl blob exposes a big-endian 32-bit uncompressed size at blob offset +0x04. the outer ssa csize measures the stored blob, including its compression envelope. other entries may contain opaque/uncompressed dds or mdb bytes. the archive itself does not establish whether the mdb body is suitable for edf6 rendering. a lossless container round-trip must compare all entry metadata and payload bytes. in the studied controls, byte-identical parse/rebuild with stable ordering was demonstrated on ig_cave503.rab (5 entries), ig_heigen507.rab (279) and ig_desert508.rab (424). these are sample counts, not fixed limits. what this permits — and what it does not because entry names and payload bytes are individually addressable, two mods that add different named textures can often be merged at the entry layer without byte-merging texture data. different edits to the same named dds/mdb are still a conflict unless another format-specific merger is proven. mission image rabs may also be coupled to mission list/txt ordering, so an archive-only successful merge does not establish correct menu images. evidence: the maintained converter/rab/rab_tool.py parser/writer and its byte-identical control archives; the independently documented rab/mrab entry-merge experiments. the header/entry descriptions are verified for this sampled ssa family and are not a claim that every edf resource or every arbitrary ssa variation has the same semantics. see rab/marc/cmpl overview, resource archive behavior and a measured cmpl corruption case.

edf6 rab and mrab — merge named entries, not whole archive bytes rab/mrab uses the ssa\0 container: its entries have names, types and independent payloads. two mods can add different dds textures to the same outer rab path without overwriting each other, but a normal file-level overlay will keep only one provider's archive. the useful merge unit is the named ssa entry. identity and conflict model a named entry is identified by its exact logical name. its state includes its type string (rather than only its numeric type-table index), hd, ft1, ft2, z, and its opaque payload bytes/hash. preserve unknown metadata and payloads rather than attempting to interpret the internals of dds/mdb without a separate proven format-aware merge. two provider deltas safe action different entry names are added or changed merge both same entry added/changed to identical final state deduplicate same name with different final type, metadata or payload conflict a deletes an entry that the other edits conflict a deletes an entry the other leaves unchanged delete exact names differ only by case keep identity distinction but warn for likely virtual-path collision for type strings, retain the baseline table's order and append genuinely new types. do not confuse the two mods' numeric type indices: identical integers can point at different strings after independent compilation. byte-exact observed controls a retained rab_tool.py test used preserve_order=true and produced byte-identical parse → rebuild results on these exact files: measured archive entries size ig_cave503.rab 5 34,932,784 b ig_heigen507.rab 279 88,866,805 b accepted ig_desert508.rab 424 217,373,434 b the studied e506 mrab controls also used the same archive grammar: e506_biggrey contained 71 entries, e506_ha_biggrey 47, and e506_ha_weapon 28. these are sample-specific observations, not promises that any arbitrary rab round-trips identically under every serializer setting. four offline poc scenarios checked independent dds additions, identical addition deduplication, same-name/different-payload conflict, and deletion versus unchanged/edited entries. the resulting archive was stable under another parse/rebuild. the test did not run a merged archive inside the game. image archives are related to mission metadata missionlist.*.image.rab is a logical companion of config.modelist, mission list and localized txt. treat it as an entry-merge candidate, not an opaque last-wins file. but a successful ssa entry merge does not prove which preview image a changed list row selects. the later r29 mission-studio contract resolves that relationship for the studied edf6 list format: list field2, with / normalized to _ and .dds appended, gives the entry identity. unknown profiles must not automatically inherit that rule; see thumbnail binary and runtime provenance. a safe composer must therefore mark mission-image archives cross_file_coupled and validate the resulting list/txt/image relationship after a mission insertion or reorder. an archive can be byte-valid and still show the wrong thumbnail. know when entry merge is not the right approach a pair of complete custom object/map families may need namespace rebasing of the whole resource closure, not entry merge at a shared vanilla path. conversely, two different mdb/mad/cas/hkt payloads with the same embedded name cannot be byte-concatenated or patched without a separate schema-level merger. for opaque resources, identical hashes may deduplicate; differing hashes should fail closed. see ssa binary header and entry layout, mission thumbnails and list linkage and sgo/dsgo semantic composition. evidence boundary: september 1, 2026 offline rab/mrab composition research. not an unqualified runtime guarantee across all archive families.

mdb model format overview mdb is a model resource containing structural metadata, geometry streams and material relationships. the bytes must agree with the mesh's vertex declaration; animation and object collision add further bone and physics constraints. model part what it controls vertex declaration attribute types, sizes and stride for every mesh buffer mesh indices and weights geometry topology and skin binding material and sampler records shader family, parameters and texture slots bones, bind pose and sockets animation, attachments and related shkt physics start at models for the subject index. use the detailed sections below for exact source-backed findings and generation differences. native material schema versus shader reflection how to read and write native mdb materials explains the exact parameter sequence, sampler order, integer-bit parameter exceptions and why a reflected shader catalog must not be serialized directly as a material. for roughness and metallic formulas, see mdb shading parameters. an mdb is a model resource used by earth defense force. its observable data can include name/bone/object relationships, meshes, vertex declarations and buffers, material records, shader identifiers and texture references. those parts have to agree: a model is not just vertex positions with a shader name attached. we have strongest detailed structural examples from edf5/edf6 ordinary model assets, including buildings and props used in maps. these are not fieldrender/fmep terrain formats. geometry and vertex declarations each mesh describes how the bytes in its vertex stream should be interpreted. the declaration supplies a semantic (such as position, texcoord or blendindices), a stored element type and a per-vertex layout. do not infer a universal stride from the game version alone. observed declaration encodings in paired edf5/edf6 research: type observed lane shape bytes common use 1 float32 × 4 16 blendweight and four-component lanes 4 float32 × 3 12 three-component float lanes 7 float16 × 4 8 position/normal/tangent/binormal profiles 12 float32 × 2 8 texcoord 21 uint8 × 4 4 blendindices important correction: declaration type 1 is 16 bytes, not four. a parser using four bytes shifts all later elements and silently damages its view of the vertex buffer. meshes can carry multiple uv streams, including repeated texcoord semantics in non-obvious order. vertices may need to be duplicated at uv, tangent and normal seams when constructing a target mesh. in observed static edf6 map-model profiles, 60-, 68- and 76-byte strides occur, sometimes including rigid blend weight/index channels for visually static assets. those are observed profiles, not universal mdb requirements. the studied exporter path uses 16-bit mesh indices. a mesh that exceeds that range needs rejection or a deliberate triangle-boundary split, rather than index truncation or an invented 32-bit variant. sampled native edf6 multi-mesh resources align each mesh vertex-buffer start to 16 bytes; this is a strong native-conformance practice, not proof that every misaligned mdb crashes. object names, bones and mesh relationships name, bone, object and mesh records are connected rather than freely interchangeable. a source-to-source writer should preserve shared name identity, relative-offset conventions, object-to-bone links, bounds and skinning metadata. some games or authoring utilities support ordinary static geometry without a visible character rig, but that does not justify discarding blend channels from every native static-model profile. a reliable importer/exporter should parse the declaration and semantic relationships, preserve unknown records and shader abi metadata where possible, and only regenerate fields it has a defensible interpretation for. materials: what is actually stored a material is not fully described by a familiar pbr tuple of color/roughness/metallic. native mdb material profiles can include: an exact shader family, for example snd_brdf_map_common, snd_brdf_map_common_clip, snd_brdf_map_build_basic_nc or older snd_map_* families. an ordered parameter list, where each entry has a name, type/size encoding and stored value bytes. an ordered sampler list, with texture resource identities and filtering/addressing/lod metadata. render metadata and a corresponding vertex/uv/tangent contract. for example, observed edf6 snd_brdf_map_common material records use parameters diffuse, metallic, normal_amount, roughness, specular_color and specular_diffuse_blend, with sampler order albedo, normal, param_r_m_xxx_hr. common_clip adds alpha_clip. these are observations for named families, not a schema for all mdb shaders. how do roughness and metallic work in mdb materials? for the studied edf6 snd_brdf_map_common / param_r_m_* ordinary-model path, the packed texture modifies the scalar material parameters. in the observed family, g controls metallic and r controls roughness; an _hr packed texture also uses a to scale roughness: float metallicvalue = saturate(packed.g * material.metallic); float roughnessvalue = saturate(packed.r * material.roughness); // if this is the _hr family: roughnessvalue = saturate(packed.r * packed.a * material.roughness); for the studied common/water-like normal-map convention, x is reconstructed from r×a, y from g, and z from the remaining unit-normal length. this is why a standard rgb normal map or a plain principled bsdf can disagree with the edf material. these formulas are specific to the identified shader family: legacy reflect/spec materials, some character shaders and fieldrender terrain use different or incompletely recovered semantics. see mdb shader parameters explained for normal decoding, specular_color, cutouts, light masks and the broader shader family caveats. the exact native profile tables give family-specific parameter order and type/size values. texture data and resource identity an mdb can refer to logical texture identities, while texture payloads live in separate resource packaging such as rab/dds. the resource name, payload, filtering rules, sampler order and shader expectation have to agree. a working model may have editable mdb material bindings without forcing a rewrite of its geometry or collision. what changes between edf5 and edf6? paired models show changes beyond a header version: tangent/binormal streams may be added, vertices split at seams, materials reauthored, samplers reordered, texture channels changed, and object/name responsibilities altered. there is no universal conversion rule of “write edf6 version, rename the shader, keep everything else.” nor is there one mandatory edf6 vertex declaration order for every material. a conversion tool must recognize supported source/target profiles, preserve semantic identities, and validate material abi, shader, texture packing and required vertex lanes together. native observations are stronger than plausible-looking imported previews. important boundaries ordinary mdb mesh materials are not fmep/fieldrender terrain. the latter uses a different terrain-material and texture-array path. _lod.mdb does not guarantee a specific lod shader; some native lod companions reuse normal material families. a preserved unknown material can round-trip correctly even when a blender/gltf-style preview is approximate. a shader's register-level texture binding order need not equal its mdb material sampler-list order. for deeper reading: mdb migration profiles, vertex layouts and skinning, type-4 parameter encodings and map render/collision separation. source-tree cases and version rewrites are not full model parity a historical paired-tree resource comparison reported 218 position-only placement records (t2) that were byte-identical in its edf5/edf6 samples, while the displayed tree size remained a separate open question in that test. that finite record equivalence cannot establish general mdb mesh/material parity or native render-size rules. likewise, an older converter upgrading a measured mdb version and rewriting fields was a conversion attempt, not proof that every model, skeleton and material family is equivalent across the games. when debugging a correct mdb that still crashes, check the resource type registration first: an earlier byte-exact in-memory mdb was fed into the wrong .trb handler. see typed-dispatch failure analysis.

mdb material parameters — roughness, metallic and normals how these values are actually stored in mdb the equations above describe shader semantics. a native mdb also has its own typed parameter and sampler record order. for example, snd_brdf_map_common parameters are stored as diffuse, metallic, normal_amount, roughness, specular_color, specular_diffuse_blend, which differs from the reflected shader-variable order. read how to read and write native mdb materials before creating a fresh material; it includes the type/size records, observed defaults, texture slot order and raw integer exceptions. edf6 mdb materials combine an exact shader family, parameters and textures. their values should be interpreted according to that family, not according to a universal pbr importer. the equations below describe the studied ordinary mdb common/brdf-style material path, with provenance and exceptions stated explicitly. they do not apply wholesale to legacy character shaders or fieldrender terrain. albedo and diffuse for the described common-family material path, the simple base color is approximately: float3 basecolor = albedotexture.rgb * diffuse.rgb; diffuse is a material color factor. the albedo sampler supplies texture color. depending on the family, other masks can modify the color before it reaches the compositor. metallic: which texture channel matters? for observed param_r_m_* packed-texture families, the material's metallic scalar is modulated by the green (g) channel: metallicvalue = saturate(packedtexture.g * material.metallic); thus neither metallic=1 nor a white albedo guarantees a metallic surface; the packed texture can reduce the effective value. treat the stored texture's semantic family as part of the rule. older reflect/spec masks are not automatically the same thing as this packed metallic channel. roughness, including _hr for the same common/brdf param_r_m_* family, the red (r) channel modulates the material roughness scalar: roughnessvalue = saturate(packedtexture.r * material.roughness); for the sampled _hr variant, alpha (a) is an additional roughness multiplier: roughnessvalue = saturate(packedtexture.r * packedtexture.a * material.roughness); this explains a common blender/helix/gltf preview mismatch: connecting only roughness to a pbr shader ignores the red/alpha texture contribution. roughness is not a synonym for older specular_pow values. normal maps and normal_amount in the described ordinary common/model-style path, the normal texture uses a nonstandard r×a / g decode: float x = texture.r * texture.a * 2.0 - 1.0; float y = texture.g * 2.0 - 1.0; float z = sqrt(max(0.00001, 1.0 - x*x - y*y)); x *= normal_amount; y *= normal_amount; // transform (x,y,z) with tangent, binormal and geometric-normal basis, // then normalize for the relevant material path. a conventional rgb or rg normal-map import can therefore be visibly wrong. normal_amount=0 disables the tangent-plane perturbation; values greater than one exaggerate it and negative values reverse its x/y direction. the convention is supported by the supplied rendering description and corroborated in the analyzed water shader, but not every edf shader family has been proven to use it. fieldrender exception: the studied terrain normal path reconstructs x from r×b, and y has an inverted sign; see fieldrender textures and normals. do not reuse the mdb decoder blindly for terrain. color-change masks for two-channel param_cm0_cm1, the supplied rendering description uses sequential interpolation, not one combined tint multiply: float3 c = lerp(diffuse, change_color0, colormask.r); c = lerp(c, change_color1, colormask.g); float3 result = albedo.rgb * c; the second interpolation sees the result of the first. channel order and family-specific uv routing matter. cutout/alpha clip in snd_brdf_map_common_clip, pixels below the alpha_clip threshold are discarded: if (albedoalpha < alpha_clip) discard; in a 44-material native sample, 42 used alpha_clip=0.5 and two used 0.3435. those counts are sample results, not universal defaults. native bc1/dxt1 textures with one-bit transparency have been observed in foliage using this path. specular_color and specular_diffuse_blend the supplied compositor description gives the following brdf-family logical mixing rule: float blend = metallicvalue * specular_diffuse_blend; float3 specularrgb = lerp(specular_color, preemissionalbedo * specular_color, blend); float3 f0 = specularrgb * (0.04 + 0.96 * metallicvalue); this is a guide-derived model of the general path, not a claim of native-byte verification for every shader. specular_color participates in specular/fresnel computation; it is not simply an albedo tint. the described direct-specular term is ggx/schlick-like, subject to family-specific differences. emission and light masks emission is not universal across edf6 shader families. for the studied snd_brdf_map_common_light shader, native shader analysis supports an accumulation term equivalent to: emissionaccum.rgb = packedlightmask.b * light_color.rgb; a mandatory extra multiplication by albedo has not been established for that exact write. do not force one generic albedo × light_color × mask formula onto all families. occlusion and why a standard pbr preview differs the supplied rendering model describes an unusual intermediate where the length of the stored surface normal carries occlusion information: normalxyz = normalizedsurfacenormal * occlusion; for the described composition, ambient diffuse can scale approximately with squared normal length, while several directional/specular/environment terms scale with length. this is not the same as applying a conventional ambient-occlusion texture only to base-color darkening. the system also includes distinct environment weighting, fog and hdr/exposure/bloom behavior. a principled bsdf or generic gltf preview is therefore only a useful approximation. shader names do not imply interchangeable data older snd_map_*, snd_chara_basic and specialized window/glass/parallax/dirtscroll/signboard materials can use different parameter and sampler abis. specular_pow must not be silently renamed roughness. raw integer type=4 parameters must retain their u32 bits, not float32 numeric values (for example raw integer 2 is 02 00 00 00, whereas float 2.0 is 00 00 00 40). for material-by-material tables and typed parameter order, see native shader profiles, specialized shader families and raw type-4 values. for sampled shader-family counts, ordered sampler layouts and the type=4 raw-u32 exception, see the native mdb shader family field guide. evidence and limits native observations: sampled mdb material schemas and texture binding; exact common_clip/light family behavior where audited; native texture/channel and source paired-asset findings. corroborated but not universal: common/water-style normal decoding, selected packed r/m rules. external descriptive guide: parts of the high-level specular, occlusion and scene compositor equations above. treat these as useful qualified descriptions, not proof for every shader binary. still unknown: universal behavior of legacy snd_chara_basic/non-brdf scene composition, and a universally faithful stock blender/gltf preview. native water is a separate mdb shader family one retained native mdb, eu1_nw_field01_water.mdb, uses snd_brdf_map_water and has associated water-shore and normal texture resources. the wider four-map retained census does not establish separate river/ocean shader families. see native static-water shader evidence. the existence of this specialized family does not change how unrelated brdf or legacy mdb shaders should be interpreted.

native mdb shader families: parameters, textures and practical interpretation overview a shader family is a contract between mdb mesh attributes, ordered native material parameters, sampler slots and render state. a shader identifier alone is not enough to reproduce the original material, and shader-reflection order cannot be assumed to be serialization order. material workflow identify the actual shader family and required vertex attributes. read parameters in native mdb order, preserving their stored types. keep texture samplers in their native slot order. preserve blend, alpha and family-specific render state. validate visually in the target renderer, not just by parsing the mdb. see shaders for the central reference and the snd_brdf_map_common example. starting from a real material for a self-contained implementation guide, read how to read and write native mdb materials. it explains why these observed sampler and parameter tables are not interchangeable with shader reflection and demonstrates common metallic/roughness channels and integer controls. an mdb material is not defined by its shader name alone. the shader family, the ordered parameter records, the ordered sampler bindings, their states, and the mesh vertex declaration form a contract. changing only the shader identifier can create an apparently valid file that renders incorrectly. this page describes ordinary edf6 mdb materials, including map props and building models. it does not describe the separate fmep/fieldrender terrain pipeline. common brdf material: the basic interpretation for sampled snd_brdf_map_common materials, the useful logical model is: input meaning in the observed/common guide-backed path important caveat diffuse multiplies sampled albedo rgb colour customization can interpolate in additional colours first metallic scales the packed metallic channel typically packed.g × metallic, then clamped downstream roughness scales the packed roughness channel typically packed.r × roughness; _hr can multiply alpha too normal_amount multiplies normal-map tangent-plane perturbation affects normal direction before normalization, not stored normal length specular_color participates in the specular/fresnel term not equivalent to tinting the final diffuse colour specular_diffuse_blend mixes specular colour behaviour as metallic increases formula is based on a supplied rendering guide; not independently established for every shader the retained guide models the packed channels as: metallic = clamp(packed.g × material.metallic, 0, 1) roughness = clamp(packed.r × material.roughness, 0, 1) roughness_hr = clamp(packed.r × packed.a × material.roughness, 0, 1) these formulas apply to the identified common packed r/m path. they do not license a universal channel reinterpretation of arbitrary edf5/edf6 textures. the same shader guide describes a fresnel baseline resembling specularrgb × (0.04 + 0.96 × metallic); use it as a reference-derived compositor model, not as a proven exact fragment-program identity for every material. normal textures: packed channels and occlusion for the common-model path described by the supplied guide: nx = (r × a × 2) - 1 ny = (g × 2) - 1 nz = sqrt(max(0.00001, 1 - nx² - ny²)) the tangent-space perturbation is scaled by normal_amount, transformed through the tangent/binormal/geometric-normal frame, then normalized. normal-map strength and stored normal-vector length are separate concepts. the guide describes a later normalxyz = normalizednormal × occlusion operation. its author subsequently clarified that normal length enters diffuse/specular/compositor lighting in different ways; those detailed downstream rules are guide-derived and should not be generalized across every shader family without more binary evidence. what native material sampling establishes the audited ordinary mdb map-model corpora contained the following material samples. counts are sampled occurrences, not global edf6 usage statistics. edf6 shader family studied occurrences notable verified structure / use snd_brdf_map_common 101 albedo, normal and packed r/m sampler set; six familiar brdf parameters snd_brdf_map_common_clip 44 common parameters plus alpha_clip; sampled 60-byte mesh profile snd_brdf_map_common_light 5 includes light_color; sampled packed light mask and dedicated emissive path snd_brdf_map_build_basic_nc 28 five samplers including occlusion and dirt; sampled 76-byte profile and three uv uses snd_brdf_map_build_para_nc 9 parallax parameters; sampled 76-byte material/mesh abi snd_brdf_map_build_dirtscroll 7 dirt-scroll controls, sampled 76-byte profile snd_brdf_map_signboard_pattern 1 animated/switching controls including integer-bit (type=4) lanes; sampled 68-byte profile for build_basic_nc, sampled geometry uses texcoord0 for close-range sampling, texcoord1 for occlusion and texcoord2 for macro/dirt data. a generic renderer that feeds every sampler from uv0 discards that relationship. alpha cutout is not general transparency in the sampled common_clip path, fragments are discarded when sampled albedo alpha falls below the material's alpha_clip threshold. within the 44 sampled common_clip materials, alpha_clip was 0.5 in 42 and 0.3435 in 2. these are observed defaults, not a game-wide invariant. a native foliage texture (sk_pshrub003-df.dds) demonstrated actual bc1/dxt1 one-bit transparency. bc1 cutout is therefore a valid native example, not the sole permitted cutout encoding. common_light is a real exception to generic emission assumptions an exact inspected snd_brdf_map_common_light path wrote an emission accumulation equivalent to: emissionaccum.rgb = packedlightmask.b × light_color.rgb no base-colour multiply was established for that exact write. do not turn a guide's more general emissive model into a compulsory rule for common_light, or claim that this exact write describes every emissive family. raw integer parameter lanes (type=4) some material parameters occupy a four-byte lane but represent a raw 32-bit integer, not a numeric float. an unmodified bit-preserving round trip may happen to work through a float container; creation/editing through float arithmetic is not safe. preserve the declared type and raw bits; expose known fields as integer/flag controls. for example, reinterpreting raw 0x00000001 as ieee float produces a subnormal number, not the numeric value 1.0. what a model viewer or exporter should do identify the model's actual shader family, parameter list and sampler order. decode the material-specific texture packing, not a global rgba assumption. use the mesh's actual semantic streams, including extra uvs and tangent/binormal data. preserve unknown fields and type=4 raw bits. label a stock principled/gltf preview approximate when it does not reproduce edf's compositor and lighting rules. when converting edf5 materials, use a compatible full target profile; a shader-name substitution is not a complete migration. further details mdb model structure and vertex layouts how roughness, metallic, normals and emission work observed native mdb shader/material families texture packing and dds cutouts evidence status: native edf6 mdb corpus for shader/material counts, sampled layouts, common_clip and common_light exceptions; supplied shader guide for several general compositor and packed-channel equations; separate author clarification for normal-length lighting. do not merge these evidence classes.

edf texture observations: dds, packed masks, bc1 cutouts and fpr edf materials often put multiple logical values into different channels of one texture, and the channels have meaning only in combination with the chosen shader family. a texture can be valid dds and still be wrong for the material that reads it. packed channels for ordinary mdb brdf materials in the studied param_r_m_* common-family materials, g modulates metallic and r modulates roughness. for _hr textures, alpha is another roughness multiplier. normal textures in the studied common/water-like path decode x using r×a, y from g and reconstruct z. see mdb shader equations. do not generalize these rules into universal fpr channel conversion or fieldrender normal decoding. older reflect/spec textures, _hr material masks, change-color masks and true field terrain arrays are different semantic families. bc1/dxt1 cutout textures are a real native path an observed edf6 foliage texture sk_pshrub003-df.dds used bc1/dxt1 one-bit transparency. in its top mip, all 32,768 blocks were in the transparent (color0 ≤ color1) mode, and 427,079 pixels selected the transparent palette entry. this proves one native cutout example, not a requirement for all edf textures. the mipmap coverage problem an offline source-owned 64×64 test retained 50% transparent coverage down to 8×8, but a naive majority downsampler produced 0% transparency at 4×4, 2×2 and 1×1. that can make distant cutout foliage look opaque. a tested deterministic, optional coverage-preserving bc1 mip policy retained 8 transparent pixels at 4×4 and 2 at 2×2, while 1×1 cannot represent a 50% fractional pixel. this is a useful authored-texture repair strategy, not a recovered universal native sandlot mip-generation algorithm or proof of in-game visual parity for all assets. resource binding is separate from image content in a runtime-positive custom-texture case, logical mdb texture identities, authored hd/lod dds payloads and canonical archive insertion worked as a coherent chain. the identity and reference metadata are not interchangeable with the dds bytes. a converter that writes valid mipmaps but leaves the material bound to the wrong resource has not finished the conversion. for detailed fpr/mask exceptions and native tests see dds, fpr and texture-binding research, native material abis and fieldrender texture arrays.

collision and navigation architecture a rendered map and a usable game world are different products. visual terrain, placed objects, their collision bodies and the geometry consulted by navigation do not all come from the same file or the same generation of havok structures. this is especially important when taking edf4.1/edf5 map content into edf6. which data answers which question? need relevant data family what it does not establish by itself which map resources exist? mac, mapb, related asset registry collision behaviour or ai walkability which objects appear where? mapo, placed mdb resources exact collision-body identity from a name alone what is drawn? ordinary mdb or separate fmep/fieldrender terrain all physics surfaces what can physically collide? mad, shkt/havok-derived shapes and bodies ai route decisions or mission triggers what is considered traversable? navigation hkt/nvmd lineage that a mission-specific rmpa route exists how mission actors are routed/spawned? mission rmpa and mission scripts map-owned navigation or map rmpa identity the categories overlap in space but must not be collapsed into one interchangeable converter. havok generation changes require structural conversion the studied edf5 collision data uses older havok-style structures, while edf6 uses 2020-era hknp structures. changing a header or version marker does not make old hkp motion/shape records into valid target records. measured/qualified facts include: field or layout observed rule selected hknp shape types convex 0, cylinder 3, box 5, compressed mesh 8, compound 11 qualified edf6 motion-properties record 104 bytes; not a dump of edf5 hkpmotion material-descriptor flags in a qualified path uint32 0x0000ffff compressed-mesh dispatch type at +0x01 3 in the studied 52-byte record family canonical serializer bitfield array entry at +0x20 hkuint32 primitive with c == d one triangle/primitive key primitive with c != d two triangles/primitive keys these observations concern particular audited profiles. the same investigation found different valid convexradius values (0.00 and 0.01), so either value as a global hard-coded constant would overstate the evidence. native body identity is more than a similar filename the edf4.1 collision/mapo study contains 40,920 non-empty collision references. their resolution, reconstructed through structural source relations, yielded: binding class resolved references strict base + collision pair 27,018 base-only empty .hkt family 420 unique stationwindow fallback 12 additional list-shape groups 1,945 dual base/collision-source identity 3,988 resolved 33,383 unresolved without unsafe guesses 7,537 these are corpus counts, not an edf-wide constant. the remaining entries cannot be assigned with approximate string matching without introducing unproven collision-body ownership. a navmesh with correct triangle counts need not be the correct navmesh one sampled historical four-tile navigation case has an exact base geometry of 1,562 vertices / 2,928 triangles. a second target has 1,562 vertices / 2,651 triangles, a difference of 277 removed triangles. reaching those counts is necessary but not sufficient: triangle choice, geometry semantics, binary layout and hash must all match the native target when claiming byte-exact reconstruction. the study recovered natural map-body selection of 65 groups / 1,405 placements (251 unrotated, 1,153 yaw-only and one mixed-xz). the blocker is the historical creation of 4,971 active body-level collision footprints before classification. a 277-face candidate produced incorrect hkt bytes despite matching important summary counts and nav metadata. this is an open reconstruction problem, not a solved general clipping algorithm. what should an exporter or map editor validate? resource identity and object placements separately from visual mesh content. collision shapes, materials and filter/query semantics separately from texture/rendering data. ownership of each placed collision body, including ambiguous source pairs. navmesh geometry and serialization separately from mere in-game visual correctness. mission route data separately from native navigation surfaces. offline parse/build checks separately from in-game collision/pathfinding tests. see map formats and runtime consumers, havok mad / shkt exact observations, edf4.1 nav reconstruction details and mission rmpa. evidence status: sampled native assets, independently recovered havok-derived structures, exact/offline reconstruction and specific runtime-qualified mad compatibility cases. no blanket gameplay parity or fully recovered r1d classifier is claimed. do not conflate mesh quantization with a collision seam a measured edfroom mad conversion retained 297,951 post-filter triangles and 166,084 reachable unique compressed-mesh shape keys. in 20 audited wall/collider records, decoded coordinates were quantized relative to source coordinates yet shared-section seam discontinuity was zero under the exact source-key comparison. independent runtime observation confirmed physical wall/projectile blocking while ai targeting remained anomalous. see edfroom physical collision reconstruction. closed mad obstacle solids versus open mad surfaces: a source-grounded counterexample an original edf4.1 sk_heigen02 mad/mapb example isolates why contact with a triangle does not establish the presence of an interior solid obstacle. the tested weld tolerance was 0.0001 m and the closed-solid gate required every undirected edge to have exactly two incident oriented faces in opposite directions. it was not a full self-intersection proof. source placement / mesh original triangles boundary edges 2-manifold closed? supported interpretation sk_rockm01, mapb record 96 172 14 no open-surface contact hints only; no interior carve sk_rockm02, mapb record 154 96 0 yes closed-solid candidate; one interior-positive 4 m cell at (241,202) using a hypothetical 1.8 m high, 0.45 m radius upright capsule, the same two records produce two open-surface hint cells for the first rock and one closed-solid candidate cell for the second. the point-in-solid-only method does not detect arbitrary capsule-to-face proximity; the later 3d segment/triangle check adds that separate evidence. the reported one closed cell is an offline hypothesis, not measured edf4.1/edf6 object blocking or npc behavior. in the complete one-map sk_heigen02 recognized static-placement sample, closed/open instance counts were 166 / 99. at 0.45 m hypothetical capsule radius the survey found 243 unique closed-candidate cells, versus 158 interior-positive cells from the earlier point-only method (all 158 are contained, 85 additional distinct cells arise from proximity). 495 other unique cells were classed as open-mesh contact hints; they were not automatically deleted from nav. distinct cells are deduplicated across placements and are not counts of individual collision contacts. see the native 4 m source nav sample. do not assume: closed topology guarantees an impassable body, an open mesh is decorative, source object transform equals target actor matrix bit-for-bit, the example capsule is an edf6 agent, or the count proves original game walkability. these results characterize geometry, not sandlot's runtime controller/navmesh policy.

mae weather resources: weathers.dsgo, environment maps and rmpa binding edf6 mae is an environment/atmosphere resource carried in a marc envelope. a mae file may be structurally valid and still fail to supply the resource that its weather profile requests. the important relationship is not merely the mae filename, but the identity of the rmpa block referenced by the weather dsgo. the two embedded resources the measured builder creates a marc container with two named blocks: mae (marc archive) <environment-area>.rmpa -> weather-area data weathers.dsgo -> weather profiles and shader/environment parameters do not confuse the embedded weather rmpa with mission rmpa or assume its area name must equal the main map's base name. the weathers.dsgo payload is parsed as a dsgo tree. each relevant extra profile may contain an _envmap pointer-like node. in the examined format, its first two typed values must be strings: _envmap[0] = "<environment-area>.rmpa" _envmap[1] = "<environment-texture-identity>" the first string must match an actual embedded mae rmpa block name (comparison is case-insensitive in the qualified validator). the second is the texture identity; matching it to the rmpa name is not a valid shortcut. why a plausible mae can have a broken binding suppose a port creates an mae for ig_desert508 and automatically names the embedded resource ig_desert508.rmpa, but the source-authored weather dsgo actually says _envmap[0] = "ig_base502.rmpa". then the weather profile's lookup points to a different resource name from the block that was packaged. the two pieces are both parseable but semantically disconnected. the retained builder refuses this mismatch unless the appropriate explicit rmpa identity is selected. the corresponding validator requires exactly one weathers.dsgo in the tested profile, parses each weather profile and checks that every _envmap[0] resolves to an embedded rmpa. a repair can rename a single rmpa block when every profile shares exactly one target identity and the rebuilt marc passes validation. this is an identity fix — not reconstruction of weather visuals. weather is more than a resource header within the observed edf6 weather dsgo profile, named fields also include: _lights _ambient _sky _envmap _tone _sun _lowbloom _highbloom _fog _brightnessfog _farclipz _shadowoffset _wind an edf4.1→edf6 validation path found that a missing _brightnessfog was sufficient to violate its target resource contract. this list is the measured validation envelope of that pathway, not a claim that all native files must contain precisely the same global set. edf5 did not supply one native mae counterpart for every edf6 map. earlier paired comparisons showed map-specific weather-dsgo parameter differences that are not derivable from the edf5 name alone. using an edf6 reference can help a compatibility build load; copying one donor's parameters does not prove the authored environment matches the edf5 original. what was actually runtime-qualified a later source-derived desert508 workflow addressed the two retained shipping consumers: dm018 selects evening and dm020 selects sunset. both presets were tested successfully in game. in that specific branch the source weather texture/rab payloads were retained and mae/dsgo components constructed for the required profiles; the result should not be confused with the earlier reference-assisted experiments. the four additional desert presets remained offline/source-qualified but lacked a retained mission bvm consumer. checklist for authors and parsers inspect the outer marc entry table. check that the mae contains the expected named rmpa and weathers.dsgo blocks. parse weather dsgo structurally and verify every relevant _envmap pointer has the expected string fields. resolve _envmap[0] to the embedded rmpa name, not to an assumed map-base name. validate weather rmpa content and the referenced textures/rab resources separately. distinguish a source-authored weather profile from an edf6-reference-derived donor profile. confirm actual use in the relevant mission and scene before claiming visual/runtime parity. evidence: maintained converter/weather/mae_tool.py and weather_mae_binding.py plus the qualified desert508 runtime evidence. this is a source/target binding rule, not a universal weather profile conversion algorithm. why an edf5 weather source may not exist to copy in the historically audited shared-map edf5 → edf6 set, edf5 did not supply mae files of the target kind; edf6 native profiles were used as observational references. a cave501-versus-cave503 comparison found roughly 308 bytes of differing weathers.dsgo parameter data even where the profile did not spell out the map name. this is a measured difference in two native examples, not a fixed per-map header segment or a magic 308-byte patch rule. it demonstrates why a new weather profile cannot be obtained by renaming one mae file or mechanically generating parameter bytes from an edf5 source that contains no equivalent mae resource. native named-record lookup: the desert508 mismatch a bounded edf6 edf.dll analysis traced _envmap[0] as an actual lookup key in the currently loaded mae descriptor, not display-only metadata. around edf+0x162fc2..0x163054, the weather reader extracts _envmap[1] as a texture string and _envmap[0] as the area-resource string; a later call near edf+0x164b80 resolves the area name through the resource lookup route near edf+0x1198d0. offsets apply to the specified binary, not every edf6 build. the original edf5 ig_desert508.mac and its six authored weather profiles refer to ig_base502.rmpa. two effective edf6-compatible maes, ig_desert508_evening.mae and ig_desert508_sunset.mae, retained _envmap[0] = ig_base502.rmpa but packaged the weather rmpa record under ig_desert508.rmpa. that name mismatch can leave the local environment-area binding unresolved, even though marc and dsgo both parse. a source-faithful identity correction changes the embedded rmpa entry name to ig_base502.rmpa, preserving weathers.dsgo, rmpa payload and _envmap strings. the audited effective five-mae set contained exactly these two failed names before correction, zero afterward. the additional four desert weather profiles were source-checked research variants, not additional released mission consumers. do not generalize an _envmap rewrite to the map filename or copy an assumed _sub_spec_factor_max from a donor mae. native edf6 examples vary in that optional field. this specific named-record correction has structural evidence; its weather appearance must be judged independently in a relevant scene. primary evidence: edf5_edf6_tester_feedback_r5_offline_checkpoint_2026-09-27.md and its native binary-lookup notes. weather rmpa ids have their own namespace for the examined ig_2000mcity / evening profile, original edf5 embedded weather-area ig_2000mcity.rmpa measures 2,062 bytes, while the native same-map edf6 counterpart is 2,080 bytes; the separate ig_2000mcity601 counterpart is 1,412 bytes. their measured shape ids are local to the weather rmpa, not offset by the main map's mapb actor count. therefore the formula gid_base = final mapb t2 count + 3, which is useful only in certain map-rmpa contexts, is invalid as a global weather-rmpa rule. do not confuse either with mission rmpa identity. the same-source ig_2000mcity weather rab and the exact native same-map rab contain the same five logical resource names modulo case in the sampled comparison; one examined sky cubemap was byte-identical. this is not permission to substitute ig_2000mcity601 as a donor. its mae was only 5,712 bytes versus 25,984 for the native exact-name ig_2000mcity_evening.mae; they are materially different weather profiles, despite overlapping map nomenclature. a later five-file release set passed its specific effective-mae _envmap/embedded-rmpa binding audit 5/5, including ig_2000mcity_e5evening, desert evening/sunset, and two e5cloudy city profiles. this is structural source-binding confirmation only; it does not certify full image fidelity or all six optional desert presets. the source audit and five-path list remain identified in edf5_edf6_ig2000mcity_weather_rmpa_bridge_r68_offline_audit_2026-09-05.md and edf5_edf6_release_plus_r5_mae_binding_gate_2026-09-27.json. the five effective maes: before/after binding outcomes the retained effective-release audit is particularly informative because the same validation rule was run before and after a narrowly scoped fix. this is not a general rewrite of the source weather. name-resolution mismatches, not a parser rejection or malformed dds count. the corrected six-profile desert research files have their own source identities, but only evening and sunset are present in this five-file effective release set. the source-history test of all six models and the effective release five-file test are different populations. a mission can have a previously observed good edf5_edf6_current_release_mae_binding_census_pre_r5_2026-09-27.json; edf5_edf6_release_plus_r5_mae_binding_gate_2026-09-27.json. record-level before/after hash and source rmpa identity are retained in the bounded archive evidence, not inferred from file naming. recovering the six original edf5 weather sgos from mapb the tested edf5 mac/mapb source layout stores six classic weather sgo objects inside map.mapb; they are not six top-level mae/marc members. mapb has six signed little-endian self-relative 32-bit pointer fields at offsets: 0x28 0x30 0x38 0x40 0x48 0x50 decode each pointer with target_offset = pointer_field_offset + int32_le(mapb[pointer_field_offset]). the immediately adjacent +4 word was zero/reserved in both examined source maps. all 12 decoded targets in the ig_heigen507 and ig_desert508 cases landed on sgo\0 magic; the six source object names in both maps were fine, sunset, cloudy, evening, finecloud, cloudy2 in the measured slot order. use the sgo's name field for identity, not its pointer index. the underlying source mac sizes were 794,906 and 329,052 bytes respectively. every sampled source sgo exposed 116 variables; 80 matched the examined edf6 legacy weather reader's named-field contract. from these originals one source-only translation produced weathers.dsgo of 18,688 bytes for heigen507 and 18,660 bytes for desert508. both compiled/re-decompiled and reproduced byte-identically on a second generation. an independent minimal dsgo writer also reproduced the exact same bytes: the two header pointers at dsgo +0x04 and +0x0c are expressed relative to the header base (0), not relative to their individual pointer-field locations. that is a measured format rule of the tested weather subset, not a guarantee of a complete generic dsgo serializer. the classic fields include the four light groups, sky/ambient, envmaparea/envmaptexture, sun, bloom, fog, brightness fog, clipping, shadow offset and wind. constructor completion is used only where the tested target reader would leave an omitted legacy member at its canonical initial value. for the measured maps a missing sunmasktexture maps to the empty string by exact target reader behavior; do not invent a texture name. importantly, some old source members not consumed by this specific native reader (such as legacy36 names) remain unresolved rather than automatically obsolete. the source-owned ig_2000mcity / evening profile independently confirmed envmaparea = ig_2000mcity.rmpa, fogbegin = 300, fogend = 800, farclipz = 1000 and wind = 3 in that original profile. these are source-authored numbers, not visual evidence that edf6 interprets the final composed image identically. the exact two-map pointer/sgo observations are tabulated in data/r164_edf5_mapb_embedded_weather_sgo_12_pointers.csv. evidence: source mac/mapb extraction and byte-exact reserialization: edf5_edf6_source_weather_mapb_bridge_r67_offline_audit_2026-09-05.md and edf5_edf6_weather_dsgo_python_backend_r72_offline_audit_2026-09-05.md; exact later ig_2000mcity source profile: edf5_edf6_ig2000mcity_weather_rmpa_bridge_r68_offline_audit_2026-09-05.md. these are static/source and offline construction findings, not new in-game validation. modern weather nodes: a missing-field crash is not fog tuning the source-derived ig_2000mcity / e5evening candidate exposed a separate target-format hazard. in an earlier runtime test, edf6.dll raised 0xc0000005 at the examined build's edf+0x52e44 data-accessor dereference. the fault registers matched a missing named-node lookup returning -1, subsequently scaled into an invalid indexed access. the source profile had omitted the modern _brightnessfog dsgo node, but the relevant edf6 weather reader accessed it without a fmb terrain and field records an edf map's fmb carries field/terrain rendering data and a spatial directory; it is not the same thing as the ordinary mdb model format, and successful fmb rendering is not proof that a map's physical floor collision was reconstructed. this reference describes the measured file envelope and what can and cannot yet be converted generically. binary container envelope the maintained fmb inspector recognizes magic fmb\0 and at least 0x2c bytes of header. its measured little-endian header fields are: offset field use in the inspected family 0x00 fmb\0 magic 0x04 u32 version version value (record it, do not silently force one) 0x08 u32 directorycount number of directory offsets 0x0c u32 directoryoffset file offset of the directory 0x10 u32 t10 internal section position 0x14 u32 t14 internal section position 0x18 u32 t18 internal section position 0x1c u32 x1c profile-specific field 0x20 u32 chunkoffset chunk/table section position 0x24 u32 chunkcount measured chunk count 0x28 u32 x28 additional profile-specific field the directory at directoryoffset contains directorycount 32-bit absolute record offsets. each must point inside the file. the inspector uses the next known record/section boundary to determine each record span. field names such as t10 and x28 are deliberately descriptive placeholders: the available evidence does not justify inventing detailed semantics for every word. recognizing compressed field records in the measured wrapper layout, a record with cmpl at record offset +0x24 has its stored cmpl span length at record +0x20. the decoder unpacks that inner cmpl data and, where long enough, inspects the decoded byte +0x58. wrapper_start + 0x20 -> stored compressed span length wrapper_start + 0x24 -> 'cmpl' header uncompressed_wrapper + 0x58 -> observed per-record configuration byte the +0x58 byte is not governed by a universal +5 source→target formula. native/paired profiles have different values and bindings. recompressing a stream and obtaining a correct wrapper length does not prove correct terrain shader/config selection. the inspector distinguishes recognizable compressed wrapper records from apparent spatial-tree records; unknown records are reported, not silently assigned a type. a generic writer needs a validated relationship among wrapper configuration, chunk table and spatial directory. mapb: binary header, model records and cross-generation pointer rebasing what is it? mapb describes registered map resources and their placed instances. in the examined edf5/edf6 map-mac family, it contains a header, string/sgo content, a first table (t1) of resource descriptors and a second table (t2) of placed references. this is a measured binary contract, not a statement that every map, every version or every future resource shares the same stride. header: where the data is the verified parser reads a little-endian mapb magic at offset 0x00, followed by nine uint32 fields starting at 0x04: file offset field meaning 0x00 mapb magic bytes 0x04 version the measured parser expects 2 0x08 stringoffset absolute start of string material 0x0c stringcount count of string elements 0x10 sgooffset absolute start of embedded sgo material 0x14 sgocount count of embedded sgos 0x18 t1offset start of resource descriptors 0x1c t1count count of resource descriptors 0x20 t2offset start of placements 0x24 t2count count of placement records these offsets belong to the mapb header, not to an individual t1 record. in a known contiguous table profile, t2offset - t1offset equals t1count × stride(t1), so it is a useful way to distinguish the measured generations. if that relation does not hold, the file is ambiguous for this heuristic; do not guess the stride. table widths and exact conversion structure edf5 edf6 examined change t1 resource descriptor 0x38 / 56 b 0x3c / 60 b one zero dword inserted at entry +0x20 t2 instance/placement 0x44 / 68 b 0x48 / 72 b one zero dword appended the t1 insertion occurs at entry offset +0x20, not +0x24. in particular, the edf5 field previously at +0x20 is moved to +0x24 in edf6. the two known lod-relative references occupy the old +0x20 and +0x28 slots and must be moved/rebased to the examined target positions. blindly inserting four bytes after the wrong field makes the record look plausibly sized but corrupts its meaning. the source parser identifies selected t1 relative references at +0x04 (embedded sgo), +0x0c (utf-16le resource name), +0x14 and the two lod locations. a relative reference is computed from the address of the dword containing the relative value, not from the start of the file: reference_target = entry_file_offset + field_offset + signed_relative_value the examined reference sentinels are 0 and -1; leave them as sentinels rather than rebasing them. a t2 placement's first signed dword is likewise relative to its own record address and must point to a valid t1 record boundary. the correct target relative value changes when the t1 table stride changes. rebuilding without silently changing the map the measured conversion preserves source t1 and t2 counts. if the source tables are contiguous, their size increase shifts subsequent data by: shift = 4 * t1count + 4 * t2count every absolute pointer into the moved tail must be adjusted by that shift; the pointer's own position and interpretation determine its relative correction. in the retained conservative implementation, the tail is kept byte-identical and moved as a unit. it re-bases known absolute table pointers, t1 embedded sgo/string/lod refs and all t2→t1 parent refs. the measured edf6 weather-pointer span 0x28..0x5c in the mapb header is zeroed in this conversion profile; do not generalize that operation beyond the verified family. map.mapb normally exists inside the enclosing marc/mac map archive. map.mapo is converted separately. a valid mapb cannot tell you whether mapo placement, physics collision, terrain rendering or navigation also work. embedded prop sgo semantics are a second conversion a well-formed t1 pointer can still resolve to an sgo whose property schema is incompatible with edf6. in a paired edfroom test, 30 of 30 matched prop sgos confirmed the target crashtype schema extension (int32(0) in the measured family). a separate older desert build had runtime-positive behavior while preserving missing crashtype, so a fixed-index insertion cannot be declared universally mandatory. classic sgo variable-node records in that context are 12 bytes, not 16. an obsolete 16-byte hardcoded insertion corrupted relative strings/pointers. implementation rule: resolve the embedded sgo by its graph/name and transform only the relevant semantic family; never patch it as a generic positional byte array. practical checks validate magic, header fields, table bounds and the t1/t2 contiguous-stride relation. resolve each relative resource/sgo reference within the file, checking utf-16le termination and target magic where known. validate every t2 parent pointer lands exactly on a t1 record boundary. confirm the target has the expected inserted/append-only fields and that source cardinalities are preserved. parse relevant embedded sgos semantically rather than applying one global property insertion. test actual resource dispatch and map runtime behavior separately from byte/offset correctness. evidence: maintained converter/mac/mac_tool.py parser and structural conversion, paired native mapb measurements and edfroom prop-sgo evidence. target conversion remains constrained by the chosen mapo profile and other resource payloads, not solved by mapb alone. a correct header does not guarantee a compatible prop one target-only prop-sgo field, crashtype, was present as int32(0) across 30/30 paired edfroom t1-linked sgos, while a separate desert runtime-positive profile did not require a universal insertion. the safe rule is to parse and translate the actual named sgo graph, not to insert an arbitrary fixed-index record. see map prop sgo and crashtype. the parallel mapo record count, object row identity and child-index remapping matter when duplicating a placement, not just when converting record strides. see the source-derived map cloning/relative-reference guide for a bounded mapb/mapo edit algorithm and its collision/nav limitations.

copying an edf6 map object means moving an entire identity graph a new mapb placement is not only another (x,y,z) triplet. the studied edf6 map.mapb and map.mapo represent the same ordered placement set through parallel indexed tables, relative references, stable/unique identifiers and parent-child relationships. a retained map-tile duplication utility demonstrates the minimum identity work needed when a placement is cloned or relocated. parallel placement tables the studied mapb v2 format has a 0x48-byte placement record and 0x3c-byte definition row; the mapo profile has a 0x1c-byte placement-linked entry and a 0x0c-byte named placement row. for the implemented profile, the three counts must agree: mapb +0x24 placement count mapo +0x0c per-placement entry count mapo +0x54 named-object row count a record's definition reference at mapb record +0x00 is signed and relative to the record base. its position starts at record +0x04. the record's child-list reference is at +0x2c and likewise uses the record's base. the 16-byte guid occupies +0x34..+0x43. the mapo entry array uses record-relative offsets at +0x00, +0x04, +0x10, +0x14, +0x18; named rows use +0x00 (name) and +0x04 (sub-list). copying a raw record without correcting these offsets moves its targets, often pointing at the wrong model/strings or outside the file. the studied duplication algorithm select (source_record_index, dx, dy, dz) placements; optionally traverse all children recursively using the +0x2c child-list relation, preventing duplicate (index,offset) copies. rebuild/relocate the entire mapb placement-record array and rebase the old references so originals continue pointing to exactly the same definitions and child lists. append cloned records with offset positions and fresh guids, then rewrite cloned child indices to refer to the matching cloned children at the same offset. add corresponding mapo entries and named rows; the studied profile names each row by its decimal placement index. rebase all mapo relative references and update both placement-table header offsets and counts. rebuild the outer marc archive, changing map.mapb and map.mapo while preserving every unrelated member payload. reparse the output and check bounds, references, counts, preexisting semantics, no unintentionally modified archived members, and no new guid collision. the utility generates a reproducible uuidv5-style identifier from the source guid, new index, displacement and a collision salt. that generation formula is a tool-side identity policy, not proof that the edf6 engine itself creates guids this way. it deliberately does not require that all original native placements have unique guids: one retained native map (nw_dlcmap601) reportedly contains duplicates. new duplicated placements must not add collisions. child references are the subtle trap the +0x2c list points to {relative index-array offset, count}, then to placement indices. when cloning a parent and children together, parent references should point at the new child records. if only the parent is copied, the retained tool preserves references to the original children and emits a warning; this may be structurally parseable but semantically wrong for a coherent relocated assembly. it should not be silently treated as a valid object hierarchy. likewise, if the source mapo string pool is not the last block, new names cannot simply be counted as an extension of that pool. the retained utility warns rather than inventing a global pool rewrite. format correctness does not complete the map this tool proves a bounded mac/mapb/mapo placement-copy approach. it does not independently rebake an object's collision body in mad, native navmesh hkt/nvmd, terrain fmb, occlusion or any dependency introduced by a new placement. a map can have perfectly valid pointers and still produce missing physical collision or bad ai routes. those systems have their own authorities and runtime qualifications. evidence boundary: bigmap.py names the observed edf6 mapb/mapo endian/fixup functions and reconstructs the record fields in python. this description derives from that retained implementation. it is not evidence that a new large map generated by this tool was accepted in the target game's runtime in this release. see mapb record layout, map format consumers and havok navigation/collision architecture. original edf4.1 linked-group census the seven-map contact and placement analysis reports 193 child references across 18 linked groups in a 16-map original edf4.1 source group list. a correctly linked child placement may be rejected by a flat walker and accepted when its parentage is recognized (r26 → r27 valley case). the count is of source references, not an inventory of records, 17 group owners and 169 child-index references. there are 169 unique referenced children, no child owned by multiple groups and no nested group owner in this sampled scope. the grouping is concentrated in nw_hillycity_light (5 owners / 40 children), nw_kasenjiki01 (2 / 3) and nw_kousoubld01 (10 / 126). of these, 7 group owners and 16 child records have matching static-mesh collision composition or native edf4.1 actor transform behavior. unknown auxiliary integer fields are likewise not automatically scale or collision flags. mapo visual model, explicit .hkt resource and mad body
