edf 4.1 → edf 5 → edf 6 generation and version matrix the useful model for the three games is shared lineage with subsystem-specific migration, not “the same engine with version numbers changed.” some containers remain recognizable, some abis change structurally, and some runtime systems are rewritten while preserving familiar names. high-value matrix subsystem edf 4.1 edf 5 edf 6 current migration rule main runtime binary older generation mission/runtime code concentrated in monolithic edf5.exe in the retained build small edf6.exe plus large edf.dll compare edf5 runtime primarily against edf6 edf.dll, never port rvas numerically cas wrapper version 0x00020000 0x03020000 0x04020000 incompletely understood; version-only rewrite is unsafe canm older/related generation 0x200, ~0x20 channel record 0x300, ~0x30 channel record with xyzw base/multiplier + encoding type semantic conversion required; animated rotation representation changes mdb older model generation header gate 0x14 in retained edf5 work header gate 0x20 plus target-native material/vertex semantics header patch alone is not canonical conversion nvmd generation-specific 0x120 in measured source path 0x130 in canonical target path structural/version migration; several record/offset changes havok map collision older havok generation hkp-era source lineage in conversion research hknp2020 target structures re-encode/rebuild target structures; sdk-string edits are insufficient sgo/dsgo familiar typed-tree family sgo and mission/resource schemas sgo plus dsgo usage in edf6 mission/list workflows shared container grammar does not imply shared resource schema mission code older bvm/script conventions bvm/ac mission source is the major conversion input angelscript/native edf6 apis plus retained bvm-facing compatibility surfaces semantic transpilation: cfg, events, stack/dataflow, timing and api meaning matter rmpa older generation source mission/map rmpa layouts different edf6 parser/layout expectations structural conversion; mission rmpa and map rmpa are separate subsystems save crypto shared lineage shared lineage retained reference reports same gst iv/keys across 4.1–6 encryption reuse is not structural save parity materials legacy shader families common legacy snd_map_* remains important brdf/common/build/lod families dominate many native targets while legacy lanes still exist migrate the whole shader/material/sampler/vertex contract; shader-name swaps are unsafe where edf5 is a useful intermediate oracle for edf4.1 → edf6 edf5 is especially valuable where edf5 and edf6 already agree on the rewritten target-side runtime contract. a concrete example is vehicle404: edf4.1 uses a different class generation and source control values, while edf5 and edf6 share the target-era vehicle404_tank contract and the same [0, 2] nested main-cannon tuple. in such cases edf5 helps distinguish a deliberate generation change from an edf6-specific regression. edf5 also provides paired same-asset evidence for model/material migration: it exposes what the older asset looked like immediately before the edf6 brdf/material generation, making native edf6 same-asset targets useful conversion oracles. where edf5 is not a safe universal bridge do not assume “edf4.1 → edf5 → edf6” is always composable as two mechanical converters. examples: edf4.1 source gameplay semantics may need to be preserved even when edf5/edf6 rewrote the underlying runtime class. nav/havok geometry must be judged against the source mission/map and target runtime; donor edf5/edf6 topology is not automatically source-faithful. shared container names such as sgo, rab, mac or rmpa do not prove identical embedded schemas. common save encryption does not prove common offsets or table meaning. a native edf6 asset can be a target abi oracle without being a semantic donor for the edf4.1 content. three different kinds of “same” when reconciling generations, classify similarity explicitly: container same — parser/container family is recognizable, but payload schema may differ. runtime abi same — target-side field/class behavior matches across generations, as with some edf5/edf6 vehicle contracts. semantic same — gameplay/visual behavior is actually equivalent. only the third is gameplay parity. the first two are useful evidence, not substitutes for runtime or source-semantic validation. practical conversion policy for every format or subsystem, prefer this order: source semantics -> measured source structure -> paired target-native oracle -> target writer/runtime contract -> runtime validation do not replace it with: copy bytes -> bump version -> rename resource -> assume parity. that distinction is the central cross-generation rule of this wiki.

config.sgo three-way semantic merge: air raider and edf5 mission port evidence: september 1, 2026 offline merge audit. status offline_three_way_semantic_merge_pass__runtime_test_recommended. this is a reproducible case study, not a universal sgo conflict-resolution algorithm or successful game-runtime qualification. inputs, identity and output file role size evidence baseline recompiled 27,826 b json-level canonical baseline air raider original/recompiled 27,938 b exact sgott round-trip; binary identity preserved edf5-missions port 41,592 b adds mission pack modes while retaining baseline weapon-category scopes merged sgo 41,704 b port + 112 b, the same independent air raider delta the observed air raider delta and port delta occupy disjoint semantic scopes. the merger reported zero conflicts and zero warnings, exact json round-trip, and preservation of top-level field ordering from the port. field ownership: do not blindly pick one whole file port-owned modelist: six additions: offline and online modes for missionpack03, missionpack04 and missionpack05. air raider-owned soldierinit: appends class/weapon category values to its existing arrays: elimpetgun01, edrone_attacker01 and edrone_airstrike01: add 302, 331 after the original 310, 311, 312, 313, 314, 303, 305. evehiclenone: add 8, 9, 10 after the original 306, 307, 308, 309, 320. the audit confirms that packagename, soldierweaponcategory, weapontable and weapontext agree with both inputs. modelist is exactly the port version and soldierinit exactly the air raider version. merge algorithm contract demonstrated by this case parse baseline, feature a, feature b as the same known sgo schema; validate exact structural round-trip before transformation. compute semantic deltas relative to baseline, not whole-file byte differences. detect field ownership conflicts at record and array level. no generic append/union rule is justified for arbitrary sgo arrays. apply nonoverlapping deltas in a deterministic order; retain target port's ordered names and mode list where documented. recompile, reparse and assert exact expected fields, order and delta. preserve the source and output hashes in the evidence ledger. run edf6 game tests separately; successful parse/round-trip is not gameplay qualification. why this matters replacing the target config.sgo wholesale with either mod's file would lose the other feature. conversely, treating all sgo arrays as commutative merges could produce syntactically valid but semantically wrong output. the observed +112 b exact difference is evidence for this specific pair of changes, not a size-based merge technique.

edf6 cpk archives: toc, crilayla and resource identity evidence evidence scope: an observed edf6 windows installation and separate read-only reverse-engineering of its resource archive formats. do not confuse a tool's ability to index, preview or cache an asset with a native game loader guarantee. audited installation and archive index in one retained windows edf6 installation, four game archives were enumerated: root.cpk chunk01.cpk chunk02.cpk dx11.cpk their parsed toc records produced 9,717 indexed virtual resource paths. this number is the measured inventory of one installation, not a constant of every patch, storefront or region. other loose/custom paths and later resource overrides are separate namespaces. container grammar and compressed entries the investigated read-only parsing path had this source layout: cpk header/toc -> cri @utf table -> file offset + packed length -> plain entry or crilayla decompression -> native rab/mac/mdb/fmb/rmpa reader both unencrypted and standard encrypted @utf table forms were represented in the research reader. crilayla literal, backreference and variable-length decoding were checked in synthetic offline fixtures; this does not establish complete runtime fidelity against every original compressed cpk entry. a research decoder's 1 gib safety cap is not a native edf6 resource-size limit. the four sampled archives were toc-backed; an itoc-only fallback was not needed for that narrow inventory. this does not mean the itoc family is universally absent, unnecessary or unsupported across cri archives. resource path and archive identity must be distinguished a virtual resource path is not enough to establish a unique source when two indexed archives or overrides contain a path with the same normalized spelling. the historical research index treated case-insensitive duplicates as ambiguous archive-origin candidates rather than arbitrarily choosing the first. this is a conservative research identification policy, not independent proof of the game's exact case-folding, search precedence or override resolution. resource-family readers were checked at different levels: marc/mac section headers, mapb type/placement tables, ssa/rab and cmpl envelopes, mdb position/index data, and mission-specific rmpa summaries. native model identity and correct rendering/material bindings require further evidence than a successful cpk toc decode. for a concrete negative cpk lookup, the source-derived desert508 fine weather rab had four known dds dependencies absent from the particular vanilla cpk set searched on one windows host. that result is not equivalent to a claim that those textures or fine weather do not exist in edf6 generally. see fine mae/rab resource closure. evidence and failure boundaries a readable toc and entry offset do not by themselves prove the entry's crilayla decode or downstream format parse. identical normalized filenames from different cpk origins do not prove identical bytes or that the game chooses the same entry as a research tool. the 9,717-path count is installation-specific; inventory changes may be version changes rather than corruption. neither cache metadata nor a generated preview is part of the native cpk file specification. their implementation, ui behavior and performance are outside this wiki's subject. this research did not establish a general cpk writer or byte-identical repacker. the public wiki contains no native game archive payloads. source family: edf5_edf6_research/research/active/map_authoring read-only cpk indexing and resource-reader evidence, plus the source-specific desert fine negative control. archive source identity is distinct from a product's asset-browser lifecycle. a separate read-only three-archive unpacked-file census (september 2026) another measured edf6 windows baseline, recorded on 2 september 2026, indexed a complete local extraction of three of the game's archives, not the four-archive toc census above. this source independently counted: archive extracted files aggregate decompressed-file bytes root.cpk 8,300 8,635,277,053 chunk01.cpk 11 468,567,682 chunk02.cpk 921 24,155,715,208 these three combined 9,232 33,259,559,943 (~30.98 gib) the three extracted archive namespaces contained no duplicate virtual paths in the measured baseline. the separately retained tree_edf6.txt catalog had the same per-archive counts. the recorded 86 apparent source-tree spelling disagreements were restricted to non-ascii mission-path names affected by an older windows console/codepage text representation, not a measured loss of 86 game resources. the observation comes from a real read-only extraction/inventory, not a synthetic file list. the earlier 9,717 virtual paths figure covers four cpk archives, including dx11.cpk, and came from a different inventory procedure. do not subtract 9,232 from 9,717 to infer a dx11 file count, patch delta, duplicate count, missing files or changes in the game. the compared inventories do not share a demonstrated identical build, inclusion policy, archive-entry normalization or effective resource namespace. in particular the second inventory counts extracted files, whereas the first counts indexed toc paths. both measurements are valid within their original scopes; neither is a universal edf6 asset total. original measurement: edf6_legacy_mod_composer_full_baseline_result_r9_2026-09-02.md, section “user full-size report” and “completeness cross-check”, based on the local edf6_baseline_smoke_upload_me.zip manifest. this article retains only the numerical source evidence and its limits; the original 30+ gib archive extraction is not distributed here.

gst and mst save/progress tables — reference boundaries the retained save-format research is useful for inspection and compatibility diagnostics, but it is not a license to treat edf4.1, edf5 and edf6 save structures as byte-identical. gst the historical gst reference records the same encryption iv/keys across edf4.1–edf6. that is an encryption-layer observation only; it does not prove complete structural parity. the retained format notes contain many offsets for armor/progress/stat counters and identify a large weapon-stat table. a reconciled summary records 2,068 entries × 0x0c bytes for that table. individual entries are documented as carrying an id/index-like field plus eight one-byte stat-level values, but some older field labels remain tentative. some raw notes label the edf6 gst/dat version as “3?”; the question mark matters. do not turn that annotation into an exact cross-version conversion rule without a fresh paired-save audit. mst mst is documented as a mission save table. in the retained edf6-oriented layout: version field is at +0x04 and historically annotated 3?; ranger mission table: +0x1c, size 0x200; wing diver: +0x21c, size 0x200; air raider: +0x41c, size 0x200; fencer: +0x61c, size 0x200. each class chunk uses additive difficulty bits per mission: difficulty bit easy 0x01 normal 0x02 hard 0x04 hardest 0x08 inferno 0x10 later parts of the documented mst include lobby/password and unknown fields, but those unknowns remain unknown. save-format conversion evidence boundary the corpus does not establish a general edf5→edf6 mst or gst binary conversion rule. a mistaken association between mode identity, mission-pack namespace and save fields can change the resulting progress state. any hypothesis about on-disk compatibility requires version-specific verification; a modified-environment experiment is not evidence that the original game rewrites progression in the same way. the live package namespace is separate from the mst file layout in the studied edf6 manager, the native package materialization path included an msvc std::wstring-style package/mst namespace at active package+0x68, while the active package object itself was held at manager +0x130. those are live-memory layout observations, not fields at on-disk offsets 0x68 and 0x130 in .mst or .gst files. confusing the two would produce a false save-format specification. see native mode and package memory. a real modified-runtime test that injected an extra mode transition resulted in saved progression loss; this is a bounded integration regression, not a property of the unmodified save format. additional native-game references edf6 achievement and trophy.dat save structure

mtab v0x200 — map attribute table reference boundary mtab is a map attribute table associated with mac/map data. the retained raw format documentation identifies magic mtab (4d 54 41 42) and version 0x00020000. documented block shapes the historical format note describes a 0x1c header following a 16-byte prefix and several referenced tables: a1 — 0x0c bytes per record; describes which material is adjusted; a2 — 0x0c bytes per record; selects/identifies the parameter to adjust; b1 — 0x14 bytes per record; a float-group region referenced by offsets; ascii parameter-name strings and utf-16 material-name strings. offsets/counts in the raw note include pointers to a1/a2/b1/float-group blocks. the note also contains uncertain field interpretations; those question-marked interpretations are not promoted to exact semantics here. ownership and validation treat mtab as an owning-mac/profile-dependent block, not a universal free-standing payload. safe parsing/writing requires: validating all record spans and counts; confirming string offsets resolve inside the string area; preserving other mac blocks when editing one declared block; retaining map-family/profile context instead of importing an mtab from an unrelated map as a generic template. presence is not universal the edfroom source census found no standalone mtab block name in the audited mac even though other expected map blocks were present. therefore “a mac must contain mtab” is not an established invariant. likewise, the corpus does not establish one universal edf5→edf6 mtab transformation. use same-map/target-native evidence where available; otherwise preserve or rebuild only with validated references.

rab, marc and cmpl archive contracts evidence level: reconciled structural rules with runtime-positive rendering evidence for the rab/mdb simple-clip path. rab rab is an archive/container layer. embedded mdb and related payloads still require their own abi conversion; archive rebuilding cannot make an incompatible model/material payload native. observed native behavior: the palm/high-lod leaf rendering regression was fixed through the combined rab/mdb simple-clip material abi work. this is runtime-positive evidence that archive reconstruction and material abi must be treated together. do not assume: a rab that parses successfully means every embedded payload is semantically valid. mrab and the shared-ssa boundary the retained cross-game reconciliation classifies rab / mrab as convert_required. their ssa archive grammar is shared enough to support common tooling, but that does not make an edf5 archive byte-copy-safe in edf6. edf6 archive type conventions and every embedded payload's own abi still control correctness. implementation rule: rebuild/normalize the archive for the target profile and convert each contained resource according to its owning format contract. an mdb, sgo, cmpl or other payload does not become edf6-native merely because it sits inside a structurally valid rab/mrab. do not assume: .rab and .mrab are interchangeable extensions, that archive grammar proves payload parity, or that a successful extraction/repack establishes runtime identity. marc: entry records, names and version-specific flags the researched marc envelope uses magic marc, a 0x24-byte header in the measured version-5 family, and 24-byte entry records. a known entry has six 4-byte words: entry +0x00 name_off (relative offset to utf-16 name) entry +0x04 addr (payload address) entry +0x08 size (payload length) entry +0x0c u1 (profile-dependent entry flag) entry +0x10 u2 (zero in the measured normalized form) entry +0x14 u3 (zero in the measured normalized form) the historical measured entry table starts at 0x14 + header[5] in the documented parser profile; do not generalize that formula without checking the version and header interpretation of the actual file. the edf5 desert-map samples frequently had u1=2; the normalized edf6 map-entry profile used u1=0. a later conflict review explicitly warns that edf5 values are content/profile dependent, so u1=2 is not a universal edf5 rule. implementation rule: retain the original entry order, names and payload identity, then apply only the exact target-profile differences that are supported by a paired asset. a header/version edit alone cannot make incompatible entry contents or offsets valid. cmpl the current corrected cmpl token decode uses: len = (tok & 0xf) + 3 pos = tok >> 4 the older interpretation using the high nibble as length and low 12 bits as position is superseded. implementation rule: a corrected exact encoder/decoder is preferred over the old literal-only safety workaround. historical conclusions reached with the wrong token decoder must not be reused as format evidence without rechecking them. cross-layer rule implementation rule: archive/container correctness, payload format correctness and runtime behavior are separate gates. a parseable container with structurally wrong mdb/mad/sgo content is not a successful conversion. rab/mrab as named-entry ssa containers the measured rab and mrab samples use the shared ssa\0 container grammar. a reader can distinguish archive-level entry names, type strings, entry attributes and opaque payload bytes. an archive is not a single indivisible resource. in a lossless parse/rebuild control (preserve_order=true), these exact rab samples were byte-identical after reserialization: control archive entries size ig_cave503.rab 5 34,932,784 b ig_heigen507.rab 279 88,866,805 b ig_desert508.rab 424 217,373,434 b the sampled e506 mrab archives parsed through the same ssa tool: e506_biggrey.mrab had 71 entries (52 dds, 19 mdb), e506_ha_biggrey.mrab had 47 (36 dds, 11 mdb), and e506_ha_weapon.mrab had 28 (24 dds, 4 mdb). these are sample measurements, not universal entry counts. entry identity is its exact case-sensitive name; entry state comprises its type string (rather than a transient numeric type-table index), hd, ft1/ft2, z and the payload bytes/hash. the hd flag was a real per-entry attribute in the samples. duplicate exact/case-folded names were absent in those three rab controls, but case-fold collisions should still trigger a warning in a composer. when two mods modify one rab/mrab a viable composition strategy is a baseline-relative, named-entry three-way merge, with the contained dds/mdb and other assets treated as atomic blobs: scenario default treatment different named entries modified or added merge same entry set to identical final state deduplicate same entry changed to different final states conflict one mod deletes an entry another edits conflict one deletes, other leaves unchanged delete no proven semantic identity within an atomic dds/mdb blob do not byte-merge maintain baseline type-string order and append genuinely new types. exact case-sensitive names remain distinct, but case-fold collisions should be surfaced. in private custom resource families, namespace-rebasing the whole coherent closure can be safer than merging two conflicting roots. cross-file exception: a mission-image .image.rab is coupled to mission list and localized txt resources through config. named entry merging does not prove that list row insertions/reordering still select the correct mission preview image. later r29 native-resource evidence resolves the identity for the studied edf6 mission-list profile: use list field2, replace / with _, append .dds. that corrects an older september 1 unresolved-note, while preserving the requirement to validate any newly composed list/txt/image relationship. see the exact thumbnail lookup guide. the named-entry merge was tested in offline pocs; those tests establish a deterministic archive operation, not game-runtime acceptance for every merged pack. a measured cmpl failure: header preserved, payload corrupted in a tested edf5→edf6 desert archive, a faulty lz recompressor produced entries whose mdb0 first eight bytes survived, but 45/76 decompressed mdb bodies failed independent byte-for-byte round-trip. a simple version check therefore returned a false sense of correctness. rebuilding the affected rab from pristine source with the tested literal-only cmpl fallback yielded 76/76 mdb bodies correct (aside from the sanctioned version byte), plus 348/348 dds byte-identical. this is evidence for a specific obsolete encoder defect, not evidence that cmpl lz is intrinsically broken or that literal-only is the optimal current encoder. recommended diagnostic: require independent full-body decompression checks before attributing a loader crash to the mdb abi. see typed resource dispatch versus cmpl corruption. implementing an ssa reader the ssa header and entry-layout reference gives the measured 0x28-byte header, 0x20-byte entry records, utf-16le name/type offsets, distinction between relative string offsets and absolute payload addresses, and the safe bounds checks for parsing. its central lesson is that archive-level type indices are local: the type string and exact resource name supply the meaningful identity. a valid ssa archive can still contain a wrongly compressed or incorrectly typed mdb. entry-level three-way merge also does not establish the safety of a coupled list/txt/image-rab change. marc header and payload/name addressing (verified parser) the maintained marc parser/rebuilder permits the following version-5 envelope inspection (the checked code handles the measured 0x24-byte family): offset in marc meaning in the examined record 0x00 marc magic 0x04 parsed version, 5 in emitted controls 0x08 header start/size value 0x24 in the emitted profile 0x0c string-table offset relative to 0x24 0x10 sum of embedded payload sizes in the emitted profile 0x14 entry-table address relative to 0x14 0x18 number of 24-byte entries 0x1c absolute string-table address 0x20 utf-16 code-unit count of the strings an entry at entryoffset contains <iiiiii: signed name offset relative to the entry itself, absolute payload offset, payload length, u1, u2, u3. names are null-terminated utf-16le, not ascii. the measured rebuilder aligns payload and table regions to 16 bytes. a historical ascii-written collision.hkt block name was a real bug even when the embedded havok payload was correct. do not interpret entry-relative name pointers as absolute offsets or generalize a measured u1 value to every marc variant. mae uses the same enclosing marc grammar but has an additional internal resource-identity rule: see weather dsgo-to-rmpa binding. mission preview images are a coupled resource a mission-image rab can be valid and merge cleanly while its images remain invisible in the menu. in an observed edf5-content deployment the game requested the shared missionlist.offline.image.rab name, not arbitrary pack-local image filenames. the archive, list ordering and localized txt need joint validation. see mission list and preview-image identity for the runtime-derived case and its scope. for multi-mod composition, a rab/mrab is an ssa archive of named entries, not an atomic blob. see entry-level merge policy and cross-file coupling before assuming last-wins or byte-level patching.

edf resource identity across cpk virtual paths, rab/mrab and missionpack tables edf resources may have several distinct identities: an outer cpk virtual path, the archive of origin, a typed rab/mrab entry, an sgo internal name and a reference held by a mission list/config. equality of filenames alone does not establish that two logical resources are interchangeable. virtual-path collisions and archive origins the studied edf source/catalog workflow compared virtual-path identities case-insensitively and recorded the archive of origin. two cpks containing normalized-equivalent paths are ambiguous without a mount/lookup precedence rule. this is a conservative source-reader finding, not a universal proof that all stock edf game file lookups are case-insensitive. a safe conversion must identify the actual path and owning mounted archive rather than choose a binary by directory enumeration order. edf4.1 dlc examples demonstrate the collision: separately mounted mp01:/ (app 410780) and mp02:/ (app 411380) can contain the same names anthill301large.sgo, giantant04sb.sgo and ari_half.rab with distinct payloads. see dlc mount namespace and collisions. rab/mrab resources have inner identities an rab/mrab archive's outer filename is insufficient: resource type, embedded logical name/stem, entry order and the expected mdb sampler/type relationship matter. a tested custom dds path failed when resource layout was noncanonical despite matching the logical filename. the working tested configuration kept texture and hd-texture in their canonical contiguous type placement and the matching mdb sampler names. unknown opaque binaries under one virtual path must not be assumed mergeable merely because two mods can be unpacked successfully. the game-facing fact is the typed payload and reference contract, not how a particular package composer resolves conflicts. missionpack list versus mission-content lookup a retained modded edf6 mp07 test selected missionlist_missionpack07.offline.list.sgo but still black-screened because a row in that list referenced an obsolete loose global mission-content path. after correcting the row to the actual provider-scoped mission resource, the bounded offline run reached mission clear. this distinguishes two native resource steps: (1) locating the selected list; (2) resolving each list row's mission resource. a successful list lookup does not prove the row targets exist. see native missionpack identity and two-stage list routing. map suffixes and name preservation map suffixes such as .trb, .mdx, .mosb and .fmep distinguish source resource families and their registration/lookup roles. a global .trb -> .mdx rename is not a justified general edf conversion rule. preserve the exact native source and requested target profile before changing a resource suffix. evidence boundaries successful extraction/cpk indexing is not an in-game mission or shader result. a data viewer's cache fingerprint is a utility state, not an edf file-format field. a json representation is not authoritative over the bytes of the game's effective binary list/sgo. a successful host-side missionpack selection does not establish identical resource resolution on a remote peer.

edf4.1 dlc object names are not globally unique edf4.1's two dlc packs are independently mounted cri cpk archives. their object-resource namespace can contain the same filename with different contents, and edf6 can already ship yet another resource under that name. porting a dlc is therefore not merely copying a folder into mods: every original reference in its missions and nested sgos must resolve to the matching source pack's resource identity. native mounts and identification the retained edf4.1 source reader identifies the two original dlc products by their cpk-internal steam application ids, not by the arbitrary on-disk hash folder: original dlc mount cpk-internal app id dedicated port resource namespace mp01:/ 410780 edf41mp01 mp02:/ 411380 edf41mp02 an edf4.1 installation stores each as <edf4.1>/dlc/<hash>/dlc.cpk. since the hash is not the mount identity, the converter scans the cpk index for its app-id directory. within the archive the relative path is taken from the app-id prefix; entries are looked up case-insensitively. if extractsize != filesize, the retained reader decompresses that entry through crilayla. this does not imply the complete cpk file is raw crilayla. one path in the dlc becomes two coordinated paths in edf6 for an original reference: mp01:/object/giantant04.sgo the source-aware conversion uses: runtime reference: app:/object/edf41mp01/giantant04.sgo mods file path: object/edf41mp01/giantant04.sgo for mp02: the namespace is edf41mp02. the original spellings inside a runtime script/string are retained where semantic resolution uses them; the on-disk mods destination is normalized to the loader's uppercase target convention. the rewrite() function also converts semicolon-delimited resource lists entry by entry; bulk string replacement would miss multi-resource fields. collisions are not theoretical. the source describes giantant04.sgo, giantbeequeen02.sgo and dragonsmall401_hs.sgo as names overlapping with edf6; anthill301large.sgo, giantant04sb.sgo and ari_half.rab may also differ between the two edf4.1 dlcs. putting everything directly under app:/object/ would silently select the wrong object for some mission paths. campaign shadow objects need their own identity edf6 already reuses several edf4.1 story filenames for edf5-descended variants. in particular the campaign's small-dragon sgo names dragonsmall401.sgo, redsmalldragon.sgo, and yerrowsmalldragon.sgo must not overwrite native edf6 equivalents. the source maps the original story object roots to private edf41_ names (e.g. app:/object/edf41_dragonsmall401.sgo), while related models, animations and source soldiers remain under the independent campaign source folder. previously generated app:/object/edf41/<dragon>.sgo aliases are canonicalized to the same edf41_ root target. the mount rewrite must be shared by the object converter and the mission/bvm converter; otherwise the new object is deployed correctly but a mission script still asks for the original mount or a stock edf6 object with the colliding name. boundaries the implementation proves a coherent naming and extraction policy for the studied dlcs, not that every dlc mission, physics rig or weapon effect runs unchanged in edf6. do not infer a universal rule from the example giantant04 for all unknown native packs; inspect the exact original cpk index, mount id and resource consumers. see edf4.1 bvm source conversion, resource identity and virtual paths and mod composition.

alias-free resource discovery and direct mission startup are separate paths a loader that correctly redirects a custom missionpack list is not automatically able to open the mission directory named by sgo, dsgo and resource-schema boundaries evidence level: reconciled binary/corpus rules from the unified assertion ledger and later mission/resource evidence. container grammar is not resource semantics implementation rule: treat sgo/dsgo as container/serialization families. shared container grammar does not imply that fields, versions, enums or object schemas are interchangeable between resources. a converter must know both: how to losslessly parse/write the container; and the schema of the specific resource carried inside it. do not derive a resource conversion law from a version number alone. mission list resources observed native behavior: edf6 mission list resources use dsgo in the qualified mission pipeline. the retained lossless path is block-oriented and should preserve unknown data rather than rebuilding it from guessed semantics. implementation rule: deployment truth comes from the actual binary list.sgo/dsgo payload. companion json, editor exports or stale manifests are secondary if they disagree with the deployed binary. text/name resources: the same .sgo suffix does not mean the same binary the resource name tells you its purpose; the file header tells you which serialization family to decode. in the measured mission-pack profiles, ordinary language/name-description tables such as missionlist.offline.txt.en.sgo use classic sgo version 258, while the corresponding mission-list ...list.sgo is dsgo. treating every file with an .sgo suffix as the same serializer can produce a parseable-looking json conversion but an invalid game resource. resource role observed binary format confidence / constraint normal mission-pack ...txt.<lang>.sgo classic sgo, version 258 verified for the studied pack grammar normal mission-pack ...list.sgo dsgo verified for the studied mission list format deployed e2_base_override/...txt.*.sgo dsgo in observed files file magic confirmed; whether all such overrides are actually loaded is untested other configuration *.sgo files resource-specific sgo or dsgo grammar inspect actual magic and schema; extension alone is insufficient practical rule: identify the magic and resource schema first; then apply the correct version/serializer and inspect the round-trip data. this is a profile-specific finding, not a claim that a universal txt = sgo-258 law applies to every edf mission deployment. schema-specific conversions do not assume: numeric field similarity means semantic identity. examples across the corpus include resource-specific enum/value translations, different embedded object types and target-only fields. weather dsgo values are particularly profile-specific; there is no accepted blind copy or scale rule. desert destruction-prop template case one late clean desert conversion line observes an edf5 destruction/collision prop template with 33 variables and an edf6 target form with 34 variables, inserting a target record (0x682, 1, 4, 0xffffffff) at index 17. the paired mapo/destruction-group work uses this as a resource-family conversion. this is not a global sgo 33 → 34 law. shared props may use target-native templates while source-unique desert props require the measured upgrade; unrelated sgo resources must be treated by their own schema. provenance and source-only output a source-only converter may reconstruct a valid target resource using independently derived schema knowledge. using native edf6 resources as research oracles does not permit shipping them as production donors/templates. implementation rule: preserve unknown fields losslessly when possible, document target-only synthesis explicitly and fail closed where a semantic field cannot be justified. baseline-relative semantic merging for legacy sgo/dsgo overrides two mods can supply whole-file replacements for one config.sgo even when they change different logical fields. overriding one file with the other loses data. conversely, blindly appending or byte-merging arrays can corrupt ordered or coupled resource semantics. a researched offline merge approach is: vanilla sgo/dsgo v ----\ mod a replacement ma ----> semantic parse -> diff against v -> merge -> serialize mod b replacement mb ---/ the parser/serializer must preserve the specific sgo or dsgo format; these are not automatically interchangeable. in the demonstrated workflow, a common sgott semantic json representation provides the merge view, with binary serialization delegated back to the corresponding existing formatter. identity precedence for independently edited records: top-level named variables: match by semantic name, not physical slot. real paired edf files may reorder these variables without changing their names. known tables (e.g. mission modelist or config weapon tables): use a schema-defined stable key whenever established. record arrays: infer a unique stable identifier only if baseline overlap makes it unambiguous. fixed-shape unnamed tuples: index merging is acceptable when tuple sizes are equal. variable-length arrays without stable identity: fail closed rather than guessing what a moved row means. changes relative to baseline treatment different fields/records merge same field, same resulting value deduplicate same field, differing resulting values conflict delete versus update of the same item conflict different newly keyed records merge, provided keys are stable ambiguous variable-length insertions manual/schema-level reconciliation the six initial semantic-merge poc scenarios passed offline, including reordered top-level names, independent fields, disjoint record insertions and true conflicts. a later exact air raider + edf5-port config case also showed a zero-conflict 112-byte air raider-owned delta composed with missionpack modelist additions, without rewriting unrelated scopes (see the concrete config example). do not assume: a generic last-writer-wins preview is a valid production conflict policy. a deterministic output can still be semantically wrong. the initial algorithm poc was not itself a successful in-game qualification. for a reader-oriented worked example of baseline-relative semantic three-way merging and failure cases, see sgo/dsgo merging by semantic identity. the exact air raider plus edf5 mission-port config.sgo proof is offline and profile-scoped, not an automatic arbitrary-resource promise.

sgo/dsgo semantic merge a mod that replaces an entire config.sgo can conflict at the file-path level with another mod even if the two mods edit unrelated logical data. choosing a winner silently discards the other mod's changes. concatenating their binary records is just as unsafe: sgo/dsgo uses relative pointers, typed nodes and tables whose physical order may not be semantic identity. the correct three-way model take a known canonical vanilla baseline v, then compare every mod's independently supplied full-file replacement m1, m2 against that same baseline: v (the game's exact original config.sgo) ├─ semantic_diff(v, m1) → delta a └─ semantic_diff(v, m2) → delta b ↓ merge deltas by semantic path ↓ reserialize sgo/dsgo this is not a two-way diff between m1 and m2, because both contain huge unchanged baseline regions. it is also not an unconditional last-wins load order. the binary frontend/backend in the studied proof was sgott; the merger operated on structured json containing typed nodes (type, optional name, and value). classic sgo and dsgo still need their respective serializers. what identifies the same logical object? structure identity policy why top-level variable nodes stable name, not serialized array position native paired resources can reorder the same named variables known config tables explicit schema-derived row keys, e.g. weapon id prevents mixing two distinct weapons with the same row position other record arrays unique stable string, path or id fields if proved allows independent record insertions and field edits fixed-size unnamed tuple position, provided length remains unchanged index is meaningful only while shape is stable variable-length unkeyed array conflict / manual review no defensible rule for matching old and new records nonconflicting operations: different fields, different keyed rows, identical writes to one field, or additions with distinct keys. conflicts: different writes to one semantic field, deleting a row that another mod edits, or adding the same key with differing content. competing reorder operations require special care if order controls gameplay or display; merely equal row sets is insufficient. the historical poc's preview could select a deterministic later winner under conflict. that preview behavior was not approval to use last-wins in production. production should fail closed or require explicit user conflict policy. measured example: mission packs plus air raider equipment a real september 2026 offline composition used three config.sgo inputs: file size canonical recompiled baseline 27,826 b air raider replacement, byte-exact sgott round-trip 27,938 b edf5 mission-port replacement 41,592 b merged result 41,704 b the mission port adds six modelist entries for offline/online missionpack03/04/05. the air raider mod expands named soldierinit weapon/category arrays. for example, categories elimpetgun01, edrone_attacker01 and edrone_airstrike01 add 302 and 331; evehiclenone adds 8, 9, 10. the two change sets did not overlap. the result preserved both, had zero semantic conflicts, zero warnings, and recompiled with exact json-semantic round-trip. it is precisely 112 bytes larger than the mission-port file, matching the independent air raider delta. the successful static/round-trip evidence is not a direct edf6 runtime proof of arbitrary future config compositions. cross-file relationships make a single-file merge insufficient config.modelist, missionlist.*.list.sgo, localized txt, preview-image rab and save namespace (missionpacknn.mst) may refer to the same logical campaign. likewise weapontable and weapontext are related by weapon identity. if a new list row changes ordering, a txt or image archive may need corresponding updates: a syntactically valid config.sgo alone does not establish a coherent game menu. do not use guessed positional merges to hide missing keys. cache the merged derived file with a key incorporating the vanilla baseline, ordered provider hashes, merger/schema versions and conflict policy. keep original mod archives untouched, report the exact winning source for every semantic change, and support rollback. see legacy missionpack namespace tests, rab/mrab named entries and resource identity. evidence boundary: september 1, 2026 poc and exact config audit. an arbitrary schema-unspecified variable-length table, a game binary, or the entire module graph cannot be declared mergeable from these results alone.

edf 4.1 hector and shield fidelity contracts this area contains three different problems that must not be conflated: hector projectile semantics, alientrailer/shield bearer collision, and hector401's own physical shield. hector projectile custom parameters the retained bridge now preserves the exact edf4.1 rocketbullet01 custom-parameter arrays: hector301 launcher: [0, 10, 0, 0]; hector401 cannon: [0, 40, 0, 0]; hector401 launcher: [0, 10, 0, 0]. the edf6 grandmother donor array [2, 120, 0, 0, 0.5] must not leak into these edf4.1 weapons. level scale v11 an older builder comment called the edf6 donor v11 mapping an assumption for source s = level / 10. binary re closes that uncertainty: edf6 computes/stores the difficulty-scaled raw level; the engine divides it by 10.0; the result is stored as game_object_level; the berserker donor node used by the bridge is exactly that value. therefore v11 is semantically the edf4.1 s = level / 10 scale. no gameplay patch is required for that mapping. projectile size/blast and salvo timing the later edf4.1 r13 functionality source line reports that the canonical edf41.exe projectile speed, size and blast formulas have been implemented and audited in the converted hector classes (70/70 substantive source/formula checks). those source-aware expressions supersede the historical assumed launcher/cannon/plasma tuning; they do not prove the projectile size or impact visuals have passed a real edf6 mission test. no new universal constants are inferred from the test count. do not retune them by eye. source hector salvo interval is: max(4, 31 - floor(s)) r13's interval 30 is exact at s=1, but no proven exact floor/trunc primitive was identified in the target calc surface. do not replace the source formula with a continuous approximation merely to make it expressible. alientrailer401 / shield bearer bridge this is the separate edf4.1 shield bearer family, not hector401's arm shield. r12 retains edf4.1 object/gameplay semantics while using native edf6 e513 shield collision shkt: s → e513_barrier_s.shkt; l → e513_barrier_l.shkt; ll → e513_barrier_ll.shkt; xl → e513_barrier_xl.shkt. source and target shield geometry are equivalent within centimetre/sub-centimetre deltas, while edf6's shkt uses its current hknp collision representation. no hp, blanket invulnerability, airstrike immunity or generic damage filter is invented by this bridge. m015 scripted-airstrike behavior still requires runtime qualification. hector401 physical shield historical state: an older compatibility version had only a visual graft. it lowered hector401's shield to a berserker gun-battery presentation node and discarded the source physical child. in that older build, a visible shield did not block projectiles as a real source shield. later source-state correction (november 15, 2026): the retained r13 functionality lineage now contains a hidden source-backed physical shield proxy for each shield arm. the proxy follows the reconstructed arm-world transform and is deliberately non-targetable and not an additional hp-bearing actor. this was introduced to restore the source's separate shield interception surface while retaining the edf6-compatible visual graft. it does not reinstate the entire old source object hierarchy as a normal independent actor. the edf4.1 source hector401_shield.sgo references ragdoll_hector401shield_has_hka.shkt, which has separate gun_arms and gun_shield bodies and collision/filter semantics. edf6's legacy object-shkt capability provides supporting binary compatibility, but the source proxy's exact gameplay effect still has to be observed. status: r4/r5 reported 18/18 source implementation and 6/6 closure checks pass offline; later r12 retains the physical proxy. real edf6 collision interception, arm tracking, lifetime cleanup and restart behavior remain runtime pending. it is incorrect both to say the latest source has no physical shield and to claim the tester's shield issue is already runtime-fixed. presentation fixes already present the r12 lineage already suppresses known donor-presentation leakage: donor damagebloodcolor suppressed; deadbloodscale = 0; deadbloodcolor suppressed; deadexplosioncolor neutralized to white while keeping the mechanical explosion; edf4.1 death material block retained; particle3_k.dds used for charge presentation; source muzzleflash01 used for muzzle flash. the static presentation audit is 8/8 pass, but runtime retest remains the final evidence gate. rule treat object visuals, projectile semantics, shield collision and damage policy as separate surfaces. a visually correct shield is not proof of a physical shield, and a valid target collision donor is not permission to invent edf4.1 damage behavior. hector ai is separate from projectile and shield fidelity the projectile and shield findings above do not restore the original hector's range-aware dual-arm attack selection, stop/retreat timers, bone aiming or turning gait. for the exact examined actor-class semantics, read hector ai, gait and arm aiming. the donor berserker's gun target is not equivalent to updating the hector's weapon-carrying arm bones and dependent muzzle matrices. 
## exact edf4.1 hector projectile parameters from the six native factories

the source-game edf41.exe audit identified six projectile setup functions, rather than inferring every weapon's projectile settings from the edf6 berserker used as a compatibility class. these are source-side expressions, with s representing the difficulty-scaled game_object_level (the level value after division by ten). the field called visual_size is a projectile-rendering parameter; it is not necessarily a hitbox radius.

| edf4.1 hector gun | speed expression | lifetime (stored value) | damage expression | explosion-radius expression | visual_size |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| hector301 cannon (301c) | 0.78425 + 0.0225*s | 1800 | 40*s | min(17, 8 + 0.45*s) | 3.15 |
| hector301 gatling (301g) | 1.55 + 0.5*s | 60 | 2.5*s | 0 | 0.6 |
| hector301 launcher (301l) | 0.5 + 0.1*s | 300 | 10*s | 5 + 0.3*s | min(10, 5 + 0.2*s) |
| hector401 cannon (401c) | 10 | 120 | 40*s | 30 | 50 |
| hector401 gatling (401g) | 1.55 + 0.5*s | 60 | 2.5*s | 0 | 1.6 |
| hector401 launcher (401l) | 0.5 + 0.1*s | 300 | 10*s | 5 + 0.3*s | min(10, 5 + 0.2*s) |

the launcher and hector401 cannon damage expressions use the corresponding source sgo rocketbullet01 custom value (10 or 40); the two gatlings have different visual-size values despite the same speed and damage expressions. the source's scale parameters therefore cannot be replaced with one universal hector-family visual or blast coefficient.

for an illustrative s=10, 301c speed is 1.00925, blast radius 12.5 and visual size 3.15; 301l/401l speed is 1.5, blast radius 8 and visual size 7. these are computations from the formula, not recorded gameplay measurements. the source launcher fire interval is max(4, 31 - floor(s)) frames, but an examined data-only target representation retained a fixed 30-frame approximation at s=1; therefore the launcher interval was not fully converted for arbitrary levels.

audit caveat: the historical r13 report recorded 70/71 checks pass and overall status fail because the r12→r13 change-set narrowness guard rejected unrelated modifications. the actual formula/value checks passed, but no edf6 runtime trial was reported. the later r18 source zip carries the same retained report. primary evidence: reports/r10_hf4_r13_hector_exe_evidence.json, reports/r10_hf4_r13_hector_projectile_fidelity_audit.json (edf4.1 source binary sha-256 39b4abf7fe722175741a5e0a154063b27ef8c589a1aa5f86c84853571ac7bda8).

## scripted bombing against the edf4.1 shield bearer is a separate damage path

a byte-for-byte edf4.1/edf6 source comparison found demoairstrikee50_10.sgo identical between the two games (sha-256 b186d3f74d4ee4d77f222087a15d26d6cc01c96d04eaff36dc0ad3d23dd08dad). the record creates demoairstrike, which references app:/object/bomber401.sgo as its bombingplane object. the shared configuration declares:

| source sgo field | value |
|---|---:|
| bombing_plane_damage | 1000 |
| bombing_plane_height | 250 |
| bombing_plane_speed | 3 |
| bombing_plane_spread | 10 |
| bombing_plane_target_distance | 100 |
| bombing_plane_target_adjust | 0.5 |

the three examined alientrailer401 / edf6 e513 shield bearer sgo pairings retain the sampled durability, approach distance, barrier range, route-update distance and item/encounter values; their barrier collision asset identities and parts of the sound/resource layout are different. separate shkt comparisons recover near-matching axis-aligned bound half-extents for s (50), l (100), ll (approximately 199.98 versus 199.9985) and xl (approximately 470). these are bounds, not a proof of every havok filter/contact response.

consequently, the reported killing of a shield bearer by a scripted m015 airstrike cannot be explained by a demonstrated demoairstrike sgo damage-value mismatch. it also cannot be dismissed as automatically impossible: demoairstrike delegates damage through a bombingplane, and the effective body/barrier hit and area-damage handling remain unresolved in the target runtime. do not infer global invulnerability or a universal shield-damage exception from these records. the shield-path audit recorded 15/16 checks pass, with the one failed item likewise being the scope-of-changes gate rather than a measured gameplay mismatch. sources: reports/r10_hf4_r10_m015_shieldbearer_static_evidence.json, reports/r10_hf4_r12_shieldbearer_native_collision_evidence.json, reports/r10_hf4_r12_shieldbearer_native_collision_audit.json; source-only, no new edf6 gameplay qualification.

edf5 to edf6 mdb: paired-model geometry, material and object changes edf5 → edf6 mdb migration is a semantic conversion, not a version-field rewrite. the findings below come from bounded paired native-model corpora and modded-game compatibility experiments; they do not establish a single universal mdb layout or a stock-game crash rule for every variation. paired-corpus measurements heigen: 63/63 source models passed structural and independent audit, with approximately 2.0 mb of semantic vertex lanes examined. nw_europe: 163/163 source mdbs passed source-integrity/binary checks, with approximately 31 mb examined. desert: 76/76 models passed audit, including approximately 6.5 mb of vertex data. these are validation counts on the studied corpus, not counts of distinct renderer profiles or proof of universal game compatibility. mdb vertex declaration formats code observed representation width 1 float32 ×4 (blendweight in examples) 16 bytes 4 float32 ×3 12 bytes 7 float16 ×4 (often position / normal / tangent / binormal) 8 bytes 12 float32 ×2 (texcoord) 8 bytes 21 uint8 ×4 (blendindices) 4 bytes legitimate edf6 material/geometry families in these samples include 60-, 68-, 76- and 84-byte layouts; several native-compatible records have repeated texcoord occurrence orders such as 0,2,1 or 1,0. therefore the visible uv-channel index and the physical declaration occurrence order are separate pieces of information. no evidence here shows that every alternative semantically equivalent ordering crashes the game. tangent space and precision changes in the studied compatibility path, position, texcoord, blendweight and tangent were preserved while binormal became (-x,-y,-z,w) across the game boundary. 16,796 half-float and 1,093 float32 binormals matched this sign rule; 1,093 float32 tangents were byte-exact. this is a cross-game relationship, not an instruction to negate binormals inside already-valid edf6 data. a set of 12 high-precision desert source meshes retained float32 lanes. compatible 76-/84-byte layouts occurred elsewhere in native edf6 even when the exact same shader-plus-layout combination was uncommon. source precision should not be assumed incompatible simply because half-float is prevalent in another sample. bone, object name and entry-offset identity keeping the edf5 source bone graph and its blend indices coherent proved a defensible compatibility strategy; matched edf6 targets sometimes re-authored helper-bone order or count, so this is not a claim that the source bone graph is native-identical. in edf6/v32, the first object dword behaved as the dedicated object nametable reference; the second reference retained the linked bone/node role. for 165/165 paired target objects, the two names resolved to the same semantic string, although the nametable integer indices need not be equal. offsets into name, texture, material, materialparameter, materialtexture, object, meshinfo and declaration entries were consistently treated as relative to the entry containing the offset in the studied corpus. any additional target-specific offset role must be established from its own records. shader and material migration is not a rename of 38 paired edf5 source materials using snd_map_simple_clip, only one native edf6 target used snd_brdf_map_simple_clip. other targets used common, common_clip, build or lod families; even the one brdf simple clip target changed its material abi. a matched palm leaf demonstrates the geometric implication: studied feature edf5 source edf6 native target leaf shader legacy simple_clip brdf common_clip samplers albedo only albedo + normal + packed parameters vertex stride 44 bytes 60 bytes tangent space no tangent/binormal tangent and binormal included first leaf mesh 888 vertices, 1944 indices 1380 vertices, 1944 indices second leaf mesh 36 vertices, 144 indices 72 vertices, 144 indices the unchanged index counts with greater vertex counts are consistent with tangent/normal/uv seam splitting rather than new triangles. in a tested modded-game conversion, swapping only the shader name while keeping the old material/geometry contract produced black leaves; restoring a coherent legacy contract removed the symptom. that test does not establish the full native brdf rebake for every asset. edf6 native counterparts can have genuinely re-authored packed textures. no universal source-mask → fpr channel shuffle is supported by these comparisons. see native mdb material profiles and packed r/m/fpr semantics. 162-material r5 abi census: why a shader-only change is detectable a separate source/target material audit of the studied desert508 r5 rab inspected 162 material records against the native edf6 heigen507 and nw_europe01 shader signature corpus. all 162 shader names were represented in that corpus, but exactly one material had a previously unseen parameter/sampler abi for its selected shader: leaf material 1 of sk_ptree007_11m_shuro.mdb. it was also the only shader-name change from the edf5 source. this is an independently bounded structural anomaly; it does not imply all shader/material mismatches necessarily crash. the original edf5 palm asset is byte-identical between desert508 and heigen507 (decompressed mdb 53,806 bytes, sha-256 b9bc10fcca56383701e0b1fe325f0adeb8667e061be1c1bf9b6f5bc7522b2caa). its legacy snd_map_simple_clip leaf material declares diffuse, specular_pow, specular_color, light_smooth, alpha_clip, and an albedo-only sampler. by contrast, the only sampled native snd_brdf_map_simple_clip material declares diffuse, specular_color, specular_diffuse_blend, metallic, roughness and an albedo sampler. replacing just the shader string therefore creates an unobserved hybrid abi. across the 38 paired legacy snd_map_simple_clip source materials: heigen507's 30 mapped to 17 common, 12 common_clip and 1 lod material, while nw_europe01's 8 mapped to 3 common, 1 common_clip, 1 simple_clip and 3 different build-family shaders. the exact palm's native target requires common_clip, extra texture maps, tangent/binormal data and vertex splitting; keeping the source's coherent legacy simple_clip material avoids the invalid hybrid in the bounded compatibility path. a full native-style rebake is a different operation, not accomplished by merely renaming a shader. this exact 162/162 inspected, 1 anomalous material result is an offline structural finding; the reported black-leaf observation belongs to a modified-game test. primary source: /edf5_edf6_research/research/knowledge/rab_mdb_simple_clip_root_cause_2026-08-23.md. do not generalize the native profile sample to every shipped edf5/edf6 foliage asset. scope and limits these findings describe bounded paired assets and compatibility tests. they do not prescribe the implementation of any third-party model editor. unknown shader families and opaque declarations need separate source evidence rather than forced normalization.

was 0.5 in 42, and 0.3435 in 2. signboard image_split was a raw type-4 u32 = 2 in its studied native instance. build_window.interior_wrap_count was raw type-4 u32 = 4 in the example. common_light.light_color used hdr-intended values above one, with non-uniform values across samples. snd_map_object_glass can have transparency flags/priority/layer profiles without containing _alpha or _clip in its name. a reflected shader list is not a universal recipe for initializing every mdb material field to float 1.0 or for classifying all transparency solely from a filename suffix. for raw type-4 encoding see u32 material lanes; for exact profiles see the native profile table. color customization and known limits the documented two-mask param_cm0_cm1 path interpolates diffuse → change_color0 → change_color1 using masks r/g before multiplication by albedo. it is distinct from a generic albedo tint, and some observed materials use packed names such as param_r_m_cm0_hr. these measurements concern native resource structure and shader-data descriptions. without an actual matched final-frame draw capture, they cannot alone prove that arbitrary profile modifications retain visually correct compositing.

native mdb authoring: observed interoperability boundaries observed native behavior: in the sampled edf6 multi-mesh static corpus, each mesh vertex-buffer start was 16-byte aligned. this is a native-conformance observation, not proof every misaligned file crashes. implementation rule: preserve per-mesh buffer alignment and respect practical 16-bit mesh-index limits. an authored source bucket with 65,538 vertices was split at triangle boundaries into 65,535 + 3 vertices rather than inventing a 32-bit index variant. vertex element width correction the reconciled mdb field/type table treats format/type 1 as a 16-byte float32[4] value. an older 4-byte interpretation is superseded. this matters for declaration parsing, stride calculation and round-trip writing: using the obsolete width shifts every following element even if a header/version gate still accepts the file. do not infer the meaning of the four lanes solely from this width. the semantic role still comes from the owning vertex declaration/material profile. known exception: snd_brdf_map_build_basic_nc uses a non-obvious verified three-uv stream declaration/order. semantic uv availability alone is insufficient; preserve native vertex declaration identity. observed native behavior: texture identity in mdb material tables and dds payload packaging are distinct. isolated texture-table binding changes and material-parameter-byte overrides have bounded runtime-lineage evidence; do not generalize to every parameter and appearance range. do not assume: every ordinary _lod.mdb requires a dedicated lod shader. ordinary base-material families are found in lod companions; fieldrender terrain follows a separate rendering path. character/weapon/vehicle compositor profiles remain less comprehensively sampled than props. evidence level: reconciled sample- and runtime-lineage-backed reverse census, not a universal edf6 specification. runtime-positive scope evidence for arbitrary authored geometry the retained september r7 authoring line reached bounded runtime-positive evidence with a nontrivial authored triangle mesh used as ordinary mdb visual geometry while separately-authored havok collision handled physics. this is important scope evidence: custom ordinary mdb geometry is not only an offline parser/writer hypothesis. it does not prove every shader, material, skinning or vertex-declaration combination. texture binding is a separate resource layer a later r12 lineage isolated a custom-texture change by rewriting one mdb material texture resource identity and appending a custom dds while keeping geometry, uv/tangent data, shader/parameter bytes and collision unchanged. the reusable rule is architectural: mdb logical texture binding and rab/dds payload/resource metadata are distinct layers. a converter/editor should be able to change one without silently rebuilding unrelated mesh/collision data.

edf6 mdb vertex layouts, foliage alpha, rigid blends and lod this reference summarizes measured mdb and texture data, not a particular model import/export plugin's implementation. vertex declarations and mesh strides native edf6 profiles in the examined map-model corpus include 60-, 68- and 76-byte mesh strides with one, two or three uv streams. visually static objects can still carry rigid blendweight and blendindices lanes. removing those streams changes the vertex declaration and stride; do not infer from visual stillness that the game data lacks skin attributes. the physical declaration order and repeated texcoord occurrence can differ between native files. this is evidence of multiple valid source profiles; there is no general proof that every semantically equivalent alternative declaration ordering is a runtime error. the edf5→edf6 paired conversion shows that normal/tangent/uv discontinuities can require splitting vertices while preserving the triangle index count. observed mesh serialization boundaries mdb mesh indices are 16-bit. any index greater than 0xffff cannot be represented in that field without restructuring the mesh. in sampled native edf6 multi-mesh mdbs, the start of each mesh vertex buffer was aligned to a 16-byte boundary. this is an observed native convention, not a demonstrated universal loader-crash condition for unaligned samples. blend indices in the studied profiles used the uint8 ×4 format. it should not be widened or narrowed solely because an asset happens to be stationary. full polygon-corner identity matters when vertices differ in uvs, normal, tangent or binormal sign. the target game does not recover those discontinuities from an averaged source control point. native foliage bc1 cutout example the sk_pshrub003-df.dds sample used by a common_clip material was dxt1/bc1 with 1-bit transparency at the top mip level. in the retained audit all 32,768 top-mip blocks had color0 ≤ color1, selecting bc1 transparent mode; 427,079 top-mip pixels had palette index 3 (transparent). this is positive evidence for bc1 transparent foliage in edf6, not a rule that every edf cutout texture uses this pattern. lod materials are not one universal shader family some explicit _lod.mdb companions retained the same base shader family as their higher-resolution models. other native assets used snd_brdf_map_lod, snd_brdf_map_lod_cc, snd_map_lod_cc or farmap families. the presence of a _lod filename therefore does not establish a specific material abi. consult native lod cases and profile matrix. evidence boundary the corpus proves these sampled structural patterns. a separate exact-build game test would be needed to determine whether every observed alignment, order or rigid skin field is an absolute runtime acceptance requirement.

lod and farmap — geometry, materials and shaders edf6 map models may have multiple geometry levels of detail (lod). a lower-detail mdb does not automatically require a shader whose name contains lod. this matters when reducing polygon counts, building a loader, or converting a model: the mesh, material family and switching behavior are separate systems. what the retained native materials show across the examined nw_europe01, heigen507, cave503 and desert508 map-resource archives, six shader names were explicitly related to lod or farmap: shader family name observed native materials in the four-map corpus snd_brdf_map_lod 5 snd_brdf_map_lod_cc 12 snd_map_lod 1 snd_map_lod_cc 15 snd_map_lod_noenv 1 snd_farmap_simple 5 these are measured resource occurrences, not a list of all shaders in every edf6 asset. an _lod.mdb name is likewise a clue about a model role, not a complete material specification. native lod geometry can retain an ordinary shader in the tested desert508 archive there are 16 _lod.mdb resource names, and none uses the six special lod/farmap shaders. most use the ordinary snd_map_build_noocc family, with ordinary object/build/glass families also present. nw_europe01 also includes an lod companion using the regular snd_brdf_map_common_clip shader. therefore the transformation “lower-detail mesh → replace shader with snd_brdf_map_lod” is not a general edf6 rule. for native round-trips, retain the original material unless a particular paired lod profile supports a change. what actually changes when authoring an lod a typical manually authored lod can reduce mesh complexity while preserving the normal native mdb material structure. a valid converter must still respect: vertex declaration and uv channels (including texture coordinates required for normals, macro dirt and occlusion); tangent space and skinning channels where native materials require them; material parameter type/size, ordering, sampler slots and raw values; resource identities and the engine's method of associating base and lod assets. a lower triangle count alone does not establish valid in-game switching. switch thresholds, visibility, and real performance were not verified by this particular four-map material census. the archived manual geometry lod writer passed offline format checks; edf6 runtime-switching qualification remained separate. three different questions can the material be loaded? check the native shader/material abi and required textures. is this a valid lower-detail mesh? check its geometry, uv and material identity and the applicable lod association. will edf6 switch it in the intended situation? requires a game/runtime observation; it is not proven by parsing the mdb or noticing a shader with lod in its name. specialized farmap shaders are worth preserving when found, but are not a prerequisite for every reduced-geometry model. their existence does not establish a universal shader conversion recipe. see also reading and writing native mdb materials and edf5→edf6 mdb migration findings. evidence boundary the figures above come from a finite four-map native rab census retained in our october 2026 research. they support the negative conclusion that special lod shaders are not mandatory for every native geometry lod in that corpus. they do not prove exact runtime switching thresholds, all model families, or a universal farmap authoring algorithm.

edf 4.1 highest-lod foliage failure family symptom family two retained runtime observations point to the same distance-dependent surface: earlier port builds showed black leaves on the highest palm/tree lod; later feedback reported leaves disappearing at close range and reappearing farther away, with scope/zoom not restoring them. the visible symptom changed, but both failures are tied to the closest/highest-detail foliage lod. strong suspects until the exact affected mdb/material family is identified, the highest-value candidates are: alpha-test / alpha-clip state; opacity texture semantic or channel interpretation; material/shader variant used only by lod0; highest-lod material binding; lod resource-path mismatch. distance dependence makes a generic “missing texture payload” explanation too weak by itself: a farther lod can render while the closest lod is wrong. diagnostic method for the exact affected tree/palm family: identify the runtime mdb and material used by the failing close lod; identify the next farther lod that renders correctly; compare material/shader binding, alpha-test/clip state and opacity texture binding; compare texture format/alpha semantics only for the actual bound resources; verify lod resource paths and model/material table indices; change only the first evidenced divergence and retest the distance transition. cross-project caution other edf6 foliage research has proven that some common_clip-family assets legitimately use bc1 transparent mode. that is useful background, not proof that this edf4.1 port issue is a bc1 problem. do not apply a global foliage shader or dds conversion merely because another foliage asset used alpha clipping. status this remains an open map-rendering/material issue family. the wiki records the stable diagnostic boundary so future work does not restart from “maybe the dds is missing” or conflate a lod0 binding bug with all foliage rendering. historical same-palm cross-generation discriminator a recovered historical edf5→edf6 desert case identified a concrete highest-lod sk_ptree007_11m_shuro palm mismatch. the old leaf mdb used snd_map_simple_clip, alpha_clip=0.5, a single albedo sampler and 44-byte vertices without tangent/binormal. a bad compatibility edit replaced only the shader name with snd_brdf_map_simple_clip while leaving all other material, sampler and vertex abi fields unchanged. that mismatched shader/geometry contract, not a missing diffuse dds, was the demonstrated problem for the historical black-leaf case. the corresponding native edf6 palm instead uses snd_brdf_map_common_clip, 60-byte tangent/binormal-bearing vertices, full albedo/normal/parameter samplers and fnm/fpr resources. the leaf diffuse texture itself matched the historical source, showing that identical diffuse pixels do not make two material abis equivalent. one further historical sk_ptree007_11m_shuro.trb pair had a branch value [0.0,10.0] on the source side versus [0.0] on the native edf6 side. with its generic schema migration, that one branch change reproduced the native trb bytes, but a corresponding runtime experiment did not fix the previous black-leaf defect. do not adopt a global [0,10]→[0] rewrite. the current edf4.1→edf6 converter does not perform the old shader-name-only substitution, and the latest close-range disappearance report has not been tied to that same palm. therefore this historical evidence narrows the differential diagnosis but does not explain or close the current issue. source: r10_foliage_recon_2026-11-15.md.

edf6 legacy shader abi: snd_chara_basic, specular_pow and the unknown compositor path some edf6 material resources retain older parameter families including snd_chara_basic and specular_pow. their presence must not be silently interpreted as an ordinary snd_brdf_* shader or translated into a modern roughness scalar. a bounded runtime-positive source/material conversion preserved a legacy simple_clip abi instead of renaming it to a brdf family. that establishes a compatibility boundary, not the exact native final-frame compositor routing of every legacy material. unresolved native renderer question for a named legacy pixel shader with specular_pow and no brdf marker, the presently retained evidence does not establish whether its outputs feed exactly the same scene-compositor render targets as newer common/brdf paths. verifying that would require examining: final sv_target writes and output register count/shape; the destinations of specular_pow, specular_color, light_smooth; actual shader-bound render targets and compositor inputs on the studied game build; a frame capture, not just a visually plausible replacement material. until then, a legacy material's source abi is the reference. no universally correct specular_pow -> metallic/roughness conversion formula follows from the available evidence.

material parameter type=4: raw integer bits in float-sized lanes material parameter type=4: raw integer bits in float-sized lanes this is a native edf6 mdb material-format finding. what was observed in native edf6 mdb material records, some scalar controls have type=4. their 4-byte value lanes are raw u32 bit patterns, not numeric ieee-754 float values. confirmed examples: snd_brdf_map_signboard_pattern.image_split = raw u32 2; signboard boolean/direction controls = raw u32 0 or 1; snd_brdf_map_build_window.interior_wrap_count = raw u32 4. why a float-only reader is deceptive the byte pattern for integer 2 is: 02 00 00 00 if those bytes are interpreted as a float32, the displayed numeric value is approximately 2.8025969e-45. if a tool later writes the numeric float 2.0, the bytes become: 00 00 00 40 that is a completely different value to the game. useful test vectors intended raw u32 native bytes (le) same bits interpreted as float32 wrong bytes if saved as numeric float 0 00 00 00 00 0.0 same 1 01 00 00 00 ~1.4012985e-45 00 00 80 3f (1.0f) 2 02 00 00 00 ~2.8025969e-45 00 00 00 40 (2.0f) 4 04 00 00 00 ~5.6051939e-45 00 00 80 40 (4.0f) important nuance: untouched round-trip vs editing a float-only implementation may accidentally round-trip an imported type-4 value bit-exactly if it reads the 32-bit pattern into a host float and later writes the exact same value back without editing. that does not make type 4 a float semantic. the dangerous operations are: interpreting it as an ordinary numeric float; emitting numeric float 1.0, 2.0, 4.0, etc. in a type-4 lane; assuming the engine default is always numeric float 1.0; arithmetic on the denormal before writing it back. the binary distinction is a declared type tag plus a raw 32-bit lane; any external interpretation that turns an integer bit pattern into an ieee float value changes the stored parameter.

a capability description, not necessarily a real-material schema. a reflected variable can be absent from a native mdb material, and native parameter order does not necessarily match cbuffer declaration order. legacy and brdf families coexist. do not infer that specular_pow is obsolete merely because newer brdf shaders exist. the same shader name can appear with more than one material abi
