nvmd / dmvn — binary format v0x120/v0x130 scope: the measured nvmd navigation metadata used by edf5 and edf6. this is a format specification derived from paired samples and the retained source-only converter, not a claim that every converted file reproduces the game's native navmesh bake. file header an nvmd uses a fixed header of eleven 32-bit words in total, whose first four bytes spell the magic dmvn; the remaining words are little-endian numeric fields. the fixed header occupies 0x2c (44) bytes. the measured variants use version 0x120 (edf5) and 0x130 (edf6). offset type field in the audited converter +0x00 four bytes magic dmvn +0x04 u32 le version: 0x120 / 0x130 +0x08 u32 le section a count +0x0c u32 le companion a count; target normalized to max(0, a_count − 1) +0x10 u32 le section a offset, normally 0x2c +0x14 u32 le section b count +0x18 u32 le section b offset +0x1c u32 le section c count +0x20 u32 le section c offset +0x24 u32 le section d offset +0x28 u32 le section d count the four section offsets are absolute offsets from the file start. section records section contents edf5 width edf6 width conversion policy a uint16 2 b 2 b preserve b uint32 state (edf5), uint32 state + float32 parameter (edf6) 4 b 8 b preserve state and add float c three uint16 values 6 b 6 b preserve multiset; canonicalize ordering d uint32 4 b 4 b preserve the added b float is not fully understood. some native edf6 rebakes contain nonzero values; the compatibility converter emits 0.0 because there is no verified derivation from the edf5 source record. this produces a well-formed target-compatible structure, not guaranteed native fidelity. the retained converter sorts c records in descending lexicographic order by (third u16, second u16, first u16). the multiset is preserved even when the raw record order changes. layout equations a_offset = 0x2c b_offset = a_offset + a_count * 2 c_offset = b_offset + b_count * (4 for 0x120; 8 for 0x130) d_offset = c_offset + c_count * 6 file_size = d_offset + d_count * 4 a reader should validate every range and final length, not just the version bytes. a writer should update offsets when changing b stride, normalize the target companion-a field only within the studied profile, and test c record preservation independently of ordering. what did the paired-map research prove? minimal cave low/high pairs were byte-identical after conversion in the compared native target files; cave503 low/high is an explicitly recorded case. the same 0x120 → 0x130 rule did not reconstruct native nvmd exactly for larger base502, heigen507 and kaigan502 controls. in particular, the semantics of the extra b float remain open. structural conversion success for additional edfroom pairs did not establish exact hkt graph parity or in-game ai behavior. hkt is separate. its havok tagfile architecture, graph and tile connectivity are not automatically converted by modifying nvmd metadata. correct counts and offsets are necessary but do not prove the target game will navigate correctly. related: hkt/nvmd compatibility vs native rebake, collision and navigation. evidence: source-owned nvmd_source_only.py and audit_nvmd_source_only.py, paired native sample observations and the historical nvmd source-only research. no new runtime test was performed for this article.

havok compressed-mesh primitives: shape keys, section records and failure modes native broadphase checker: inactive keys and rounding do not treat every 4-byte primitive row as a live shape key: the examined native nw map uses de ad de ad tombstones. a faulty validator counted ten false missing keys until those inactive slots were excluded. the same checker formerly used a fixed 1e-4 world-bound tolerance, which was too strict for float32 at this map's scale. see havok broadphase validation for the exact ulp-based budget and a deliberate +0.01 negative test. these tombstones are distinct from 0xffffffff encoded invalid key sentinels discussed above. a collision mesh in edf6 is not simply an array of triangles. the examined havok 2020 compressed-mesh representation carries packed/shared vertices, primitives, per-section prefixes and a hierarchy of keys used by runtime collision queries. a generated mesh can render or even parse correctly while producing invalid contacts when one of these structures is inconsistent. this article describes fields independently identified in the inspected edf6/havok-2020 wire representation and their observed consequences. offsets below are specific to that inspected hkcdstaticmeshtree::section layout; they are not interchangeable with generic hkx/mad file offsets. primitive storage: triangles, quads and keys the examined four-index map prop sgo: crashtype, resource ownership and safe schema translation a map placement's resource identity is not the same as the binary schema of the prop's configuration. in the inspected edf5→edf6 map family, a mapb t1 record can correctly point to a utf-16le resource name and embedded sgo while the game still interprets the prop's configuration incorrectly. what the paired prop comparison established a paired edfroom set of 30 matching t1-linked prop sgos demonstrated an edf6-side crashtype field with int32(0) in the studied target family. this is a semantic schema extension of the prop configuration, not proof that every sgo in the game requires an inserted field. the older desert508 regression package was observed running with the field absent for its specific set of objects. that negative/positive pairing matters: crashtype cannot be inserted globally as a magic positional patch merely because one native comparison found it. a known unsuccessful conversion attempted to insert a supposed 16-byte sgo variable at a fixed index. the classical sgo variable-node structure in this path is 12 bytes. the incorrect insertion displaced relative references and strings and caused corruption. correct conversion needs to parse the named variable graph and transform only the relevant object schema. mapb pointer integrity and prop semantics are separate for the measured source/target pair, mapb t1 resource descriptors widen 56→60 b, inserting a zero dword at t1+0x20. t2 instance descriptors widen 68→72 b. pointer rebasing then must preserve all resource identities. a successful structural mapb conversion proves neither that the embedded prop sgo has the target schema nor that its collision body is registered in the relevant mad or mapo resource. the actual model, visual placement and collision object can be held in different resource registries. a model missing from a map's rab inventory is not evidence that the corresponding physical body does not exist: source mad can retain named collision bodies that have no matching visual rab entry. conversely, having an mdb visual in a rab is not proof the mad registered its collision shape. diagnostics for a missing or misbehaving prop parse mapb/marc and validate t2→t1 references and utf-16le names. resolve the t1 embedded sgo and inspect its actual graph, not an assumed fixed property index. compare the same prop class with a paired native target; document which fields are target-only and which default values have evidence. independently inspect the referenced mdb/rab visual identity and the map's mapo/mad collision identity. distinguish loader success, visible rendering, destructible response and physical collision; none follows automatically from the others. refuse unrelated sgo transformations when the target schema is not known. preserve unknown values losslessly when the codec permits. see mapb record reference and sgo/dsgo schema semantics. evidence provenance: maintained mapb/embedded-sgo graph converter, 30/30 edfroom prop paired comparison, runtime-positive desert exception and negative positional sgo writer tests. this is a scoped example of target-only schema synthesis, not a universal sgo rule. crashtype is consumed by the building preload path the audited edf6 native code contains a crashtype sgo lookup in the preload_base family and a separate preload_structure path for structure-type .mosb resources. this proves that the target property participates in real engine preload behavior, not just a serializer-side naming convention. it still does not make fixed-index crashtype insertion valid for every sgo. map collapse topology itself is separately held in mapo's t50 table.

t50 building collapse graph edf5 versus edf6: where t50 comes from in the matched nw_europe01 map pair, edf5 has no native t50 or p58 tables at header offsets +0x50/+0x58, while edf6 has 3,264 t50 rows and 77 p58 rows. the five active building families map across 751 building placements with identical t2 indices and matched piece cardinalities, so edf6's graph is a new derived layer, not a verbatim converted edf5 table. the earlier source-owned convex/sat proximity heuristic is not the native sandlot collapse generator. in four paired building samples, it generated 17,020 vs 753, 24,531 vs 1,156, 29,161 vs 1,230, and 14,028 vs 617 edges, respectively. none matched native destination graphs; the sampled per-edge scalar had zero bit-exact matches. nevertheless, every native edge in those four samples appeared among the much larger candidate graph. the missing semantic is how edf6 prunes/selects candidates and derives its scalar, not how to write a t50 row. simplistic geometric threshold classifiers remained insufficient (f1 roughly 0.49–0.56 across four tested native graphs; the best measured single-example candidate gave f1 ~0.784 but still 188 false negatives and 123 false positives). preserve native graphs when doing native reuse, and never label the old sat graph a verified sandlot cascade algorithm. for authored static/dynamic prop bodies rather than cross-module links, see native destructible static/dynamic havok bodies. for numeric collision-validator pitfalls, see havok broadphase validation. a destructible edf6 building is not necessarily a collection of independent breakable meshes. the inspected native map data contains explicit connectivity between physical pieces of different building modules. mapo carries this connectivity as t50, alongside p58 piece/support records, and the edf6 crashmodel implementation consumes it as a pre-authored relationship graph. this article explains the observed binary/runtime contract. the numeric observations below come from retained nw_europe01 native data and a specific edf6 edf.dll build. they are not engine-wide constants. which resources are responsible? component observed responsibility mapb t1 resource/class identity, such as a .mosb building family mapb t2 placement of a building resource mapo slot ranges pieces/modules belonging to the placement mapo p58 piece/support representation and per-slot grouping mapo t50 pre-authored links between indexed pieces mad / havok physical bodies and collision representation; not a substitute for t50 crashtype in prop sgo relevant structure-preload behavior; not itself the t50 graph a complete reconstruction must keep these identities consistent: a t50 destination is meaningful only if its piece index resolves to a valid p58 piece and the intended runtime body. layout recovered from the mapo loader in the studied edf6 loader, the mapo header uses: mapo-relative offset field +0x50 t50 outer table address/reference +0x54 t50 outer row count +0x58 p58 outer table address/reference +0x5c p58 outer row count the parser walks existing 12-byte outer rows. a t50 row leads to per-piece 8-byte records, which each lead to a list of 8-byte edge records. for the examined edge record: edge + 0x00 : 32-bit scalar / exporter metadata (float32-shaped) edge + 0x04 : uint32 destination piece index the original parser's distance_bits nickname for the first field was an inference, not a verified gameplay distance. there are also offsets inside rows and nested data; a parser must honor their own measured reference-base convention rather than treating the diagram above as a complete standalone serializer. what the game actually consumes static edf6 binary analysis followed this path: mac "map.mapo" -> mapo parser / existing t50 row indexed by t2 -> mapobject_crashmodel initialization -> crashmodel object's stored t50 reference -> runtime body-relationship builder the identified runtime relation builder reads the t50 destination at edge+4, finds the corresponding physical body, and inserts a relation only if the bodies are valid. it checks existing pairs in both orientations before insertion, treating connectivity as undirected for deduplication. in the complete inspected builder function, the edge+0 scalar is not read at the graph site; no scalar is passed into relation placements 751 distinct referenced t50 templates 742 all t50 edges 708,064 cross-slot edges 322,114 (45.49%) cross-slot structural-to-structural edges 290,461 (41.02% of all edges) building placements havok compressed-mesh broadphase: tombstones, shape keys and float32 bounds the mad/havok collision pipeline stores compressed mesh primitives, keys and simd broadphase bounds. a reverse-engineered validator must distinguish real invalid geometry from unused primitive slots and unavoidable float32 rounding. otherwise it can falsely condemn an unmodified native edf6 map. 0xdeaddead primitive rows are inactive markers in the native nw_europe01 collision data, an older validator expected every 4-byte hkcdstaticmeshtree::primitive row to produce a reachable bvh leaf key. this included rows whose four bytes are: de ad de ad these represent inactive primitive/tombstone entries, not reachable geometry. in the checked native file, seven occurred in compressed-mesh item 656 and three in item 1054. their keys were correctly absent from reachable simd leaves. check before treating tombstones correctly with inactive rows excluded expected shape keys 82,686 82,676 reachable unique keys 82,676 82,676 missing keys 10 0 extra keys 0 0 duplicate leaf keys 0 0 practical rule: when building the expected-key set, recognize these inactive rows. do not create synthetic faces or change the native map simply to make the count equal. why a fixed bound tolerance can be wrong compressed vertices and simd bounding boxes may be reconstructed at different numerical precision. the original validator compared them using a global absolute bound tolerance 1e-4 (0.0001), regardless of map scale. in the native large nw field mesh, the worst apparent bound underflow was approximately 0.00023284967483050423. yet one float32 ulp at the relevant maximum coordinate magnitude was 0.000244140625—already larger than the observed difference. calling the native shape corrupt in that case confuses representational uncertainty with a meaningful geometric error. for each tested axis, the corrected validator used: allowed_bound_error = max( 1e-4, float32_ulp(max(abs(min), abs(max), abs(max - min))) ) here ulp means the distance between neighboring float32 representable numbers at the chosen magnitude. this is a rounding budget for structural validation, not permission to move vertices or relax collision geometry arbitrarily. controls on actual native and authored data input compressed meshes missing keys bound violations native nw_europe01.mad 102 0 0 native ig_heigen507.mad 767 0 0 authored destructible/native-physics mad 7 0 0 authored multi-t50/native-reuse mad 22 0 0 the most adverse measured heigen bound difference was roughly 0.00006373971700668335. to check that the new test was not simply too permissive, a leaf's minimum x value was deliberately shifted inward by +0.01 in a read-only in-memory negative test. the checker flagged one genuine violation. what this does not establish a correct broadphase test means the analyzed collision structure is internally consistent under this particular validator. it does not alone prove that the map loads, that dynamic debris behaves correctly, that ai will navigate it, or that the game accepts any arbitrary authored havok shape. the underlying failure mode is a validator mistake, not a license to replace bad collision with placeholder data. do not mistake other special key encodings, such as a 0xffffffff shape-key sentinel, for the same de ad de ad primitive tombstone. see compressed-mesh shape key and section formats. evidence boundary this explanation comes from a bounded audit of native nw_europe01 and heigen507 assets plus specific authored control mad files. the checker was validated offline, including a deliberate negative test. no new edf6 runtime collision or gameplay test is implied.

edf6 destructible props: static bodies, dynamic debris and native havok material profiles an edf6 map prop that changes from intact to destroyed is more than two visual mdb meshes. the retained native destructible-body examples include separate physics body roles, motion properties and mass distribution data in havok/mad. for a custom collision writer, preserving only the mesh shape without these roles is not sufficient to match the observed native profile. native single-slot example in the examined heigen507 native map, a single bounded reference model was used to understand the schema. the resource was sk_rock501a_l.mdx (t1 slot 5), with one p58 group and one piece. its paired bodies had these measured properties: role referenced native havok body motion mass motion properties intact / primary sk_rock501a_l.polymsh1 motiontype=0 (static) not used as the dynamic debris mass native source profile broken debris sk_rock501a_l_hk.polymsh1 motiontype=2 (dynamic) 5.0 id 1, with valid mass distribution reference for the tested pair the pose is identity; the xyz components of linear/angular velocities are zero. the stored vectors have four components and the source contained a non-zero w value. treating the whole vector4 as ordinary xyz velocity and demanding w=0 incorrectly rejects a legitimate native reference. a valid native-looking dynamic body also requires a hknprefmassdistribution and a valid motionpropertiesid; do not produce a decorative debris mesh whose physics record has an uninitialized mass distribution. rebuilding from authored geometry the retained tests generated new authored collision shapes and identities while using this native reference only for bounded system/material/quality/motion/mass semantics. the native shapes were not imported into the custom map. the standalone two-prop test yielded 7 mad bodies (3 base, 2 authored static, 2 authored dynamic), with each debris body mass 5.0 and valid motion properties. a larger mixed-source test retained 500 native bodies alongside four authored bodies, for 507 total. both passed source-only mad wire, first-primitive-index and compressed-mesh broadphase checks and were a/b byte-identical. these results show that static/dynamic body roles and mass distribution can be generated coherently at the binary structural level. they do not prove the game will trigger replacement, spawn debris, preserve the expected collision/motion or restore it after reload. practical implications do not infer a complete destruction system merely from the appearance of *_hk resources or a crashtype field. keep the intact body and dynamic debris body as different motion roles. preserve validated motion property ids and mass distribution semantics for the exact reference family. use the 3d vector components to check initial zero velocity; do not reject a valid vector4 because the padding/auxiliary w lane is nonzero. recheck collision broadphase and first-primitive-index invariants after composing native and authored geometry. treat damage triggering, broken-visual replacement and runtime debris physics as independent gameplay validation questions. the numeric 5.0 mass, id 1, and motion types 0/2 are scoped to the named heigen reference. they are not globally required for all edf6 destructible props, nor is this source-only result a runtime claim. for module-to-module destruction, see t50 collapse connectivity. for collision check pitfalls, see havok broadphase validation. placement-specific t50 is independent of the havok body set the five native heigen507 sk_rock50[1-5]a_set.mdx families collectively have 96 placements and 55 distinct t50 graphs, despite each family having a stable four-piece p58/body relationship. a body set that is structurally valid in mad is not enough to recover the placement's destruction edges. consult heigen507 per-placement rock t50 graphs.

direct bvm → ac audit across all 141 missions: reachability, spawn pairing and value-flow boundaries evidence level: reconciled static/source audit over all 141 original bvm missions and the reconstructed 1.0.6 ac corpus. this is not a 141/141 gameplay-runtime certification. why this audit matters a mission port can look convincing if only aggregate api counts or generated angelscript are compared. the r3 direct audit instead decompiled and inspected every original bvm and compared source-side event/spawn structure against the effective ac corpus. the result is useful precisely because it separates what was actually demonstrated from what remained open. corpus coverage original bvm decompilation: 141 / 141, zero decode failures; effective ac corpus: 141 / 141; independent comparison material included the 1.501 mod lineage and sandlot exact44 subset; source-event graph was built from bvm registerevent and compared with ac internal_createevent reachability. event graph source bvm reachable registrations from the main-root model: 5112 effective ac reachable registrations: 5114 three missions required case-specific interpretation rather than treating a raw edge-count delta as a bug. the audit also found 195 omitted source functions, but none was reachable from the modeled main → registerevent graph. this is a strong example of why “function missing from the port” is not automatically “active gameplay removed”. for the later binary-confirmed scheduler semantics, see the current r37 event-model article; this page is about source-to-port structural evidence. named spawn pairing the direct audit found 3213 reachable source bvm named spawn sites. 3209 paired to the same effective ac function family; 4 used a different function family and required semantic interpretation rather than name equality. examples of legitimate transformations include transporter/dropboat source calls becoming neutral/transport-specific target helpers, or route-bearing source spawns becoming an area spawn followed by explicit .setairoute(...). therefore api-name equality is not the migration invariant. actor/resource identity, target behavior and subsequent control calls matter together. parameter audit: useful but deliberately incomplete for 2353 paired sites, at least one simple literal operand could be compared safely between bvm and ac. no confirmed literal differences were found in that bounded subset. this does not mean 2353 fully verified spawns. another 860 sites lacked a safe literal comparison in this method, including: 728 unmapped opcodes; 43 non-trivial stack/value flows; 71 sites without a simple same-function api pair; 12 custom ac signatures; 6 cases without a comparable literal. even within the 2353 compared sites, variable arguments, branch conditions, difficulty-dependent values and downstream engine effects remain outside the proof. the m039 bug proves why value flow matters the direct audit found a concrete gameplay-relevant defect in missionpack03/m039 (displayed mission 89). source bvm difficulty branches use fractional ally level scales such as approximately 0.8, 0.85 and 0.9. the target ac had correct global float declarations, but two local temporaries in separate execution paths were declared as int before feeding createfriendsquad / createfriend calls. the fractional value therefore truncated to zero through the local variable path. nine allied-npc calls were affected by the problematic level flow. this bug survived an earlier “global scalar typing” audit because checking the declaration at the origin is insufficient. type/value parity must be followed through intermediate locals and the call path. the final 1.0.6 line changes the affected locals to float; exact-release runtime remains a separate qualification tier. important false alarms withdrawn by reachability/semantics m059 / func_4 the source function contains 12 dragons and is absent from the target ac, but the function has no entry from the reconstructed source registerevent graph. this is not proven loss of an active wave. m033 / func_15 the source contains ten createenemy2 calls, but the function is likewise not reachable from main in the modeled registration graph. raw call-count comparison alone would falsely classify it as missing gameplay. m070 / m083 / m098 / dm015 source createenemy calls for transporters/dropboats were intentionally represented by target-specific neutral/transport semantics, with associated object/crew/control calls retained. function-name mismatch is not by itself a regression. m038 / m063 / m078 source route-bearing spawns are lowered through an area/group helper plus explicit route assignment. whether motion is perfectly engine-equivalent is a runtime/consumer question, but the route operation is not simply absent. open cases from this audit the direct pass deliberately left unresolved cases rather than forcing parity claims: dm001: one source edge and callback mapping required special compatibility interpretation; later dm001-specific runtime work is the stronger authority for that mission; m065 / m067: the ac has more generated event edges because source logic was split across difficulty branches; path conditions/factors must be compared, not just event counts; general float/int/value-range propagation, counters and generator tempo still require dataflow/cfg or runtime evidence; rmpa, weather/mae, movement/flight, transporters, physics and navigation remain separate engine/format gates. what this audit does not prove it is not a symbolic interpreter for both bvm and angelscript. it does not prove: all branches execute identically; all variable values are equivalent; every factor/action has identical runtime side effects; navigation/physics/resource consumers behave identically; 141/141 missions are gameplay-qualified. use the audit as a strong structural/value-flow evidence layer below exact runtime qualification. practical conversion rule when reconciling bvm → ac, prefer this order: establish source reachability before treating a missing function/call as a bug; pair semantic actor/resource identity, not only api names; trace value types through intermediate locals, especially float/int and difficulty branches; compare event conditions and factors when generated edge counts differ; keep format/engine consumers (rmpa, mae, movement, nav, physics) in their own evidence lanes; promote to gameplay parity only with appropriate runtime evidence. sources report_direct_bvm_r3_pl.md bvm_event_reachability_141.json edf 4.1 earth eater panel physics lifecycle root cause: physical ownership begins too early edf4.1 panelbase does not own its physical shell immediately after object construction. the source binary reaches the panel shell builder only after the panel has been triggered and its fly-in delay has expired. the edf6 bridge uses eventanimationobject. that target object eagerly constructs the sgo ragdoll. before the r13 reconciliation, an earth eater panel could therefore exist physically during a source lifecycle interval where edf4.1 had only the controller/visual object. this explains a concrete gameplay divergence: enemies can already obtain ground/spawn/leg interaction against panels that should not yet physically exist. damage rejection alone does not solve this; a body can still participate in physics queries while rejecting damage. native edf6 mechanism the bridge does not invent a new collision filter. it uses native ragdoll world-membership control from the canonical edf6 binary: ragdoll::disable rva 0x6e97c0; ragdoll::enable rva 0x6e9840. disable removes ragdoll bodies from the physics world while preserving their previous body mode. enable restores the same bodies using the saved mode. r13 reconciliation behavior for mothership401 panels, the wip does the following: construct/register the edf6 eventanimationobject; immediately disable the panel ragdoll before online attach; retain a first-update fail-safe while the panel is untriggered or delayed; once triggered && delay <= 0, restore the same ragdoll before fly-in motion; leave batteries untouched. the focused offline audit reports 12 pass, including pe/rva/prolog validation against the canonical edf6 binary. what this fixes this specifically repairs the pre-activation shell divergence between edf4.1 and the edf6 bridge. it is intended to prevent inactive earth eater panels from acting as premature physical surfaces for spawning, grounding and movement queries. what remains open this does not prove active-panel collision fidelity. the targeted source-input package contains 13 mothership401_*.shkt files. the remaining active-state work is to compare: source rigid bodies; collision/filter layers; materials; query semantics; the current eventanimationobject shell. only evidence-backed active-state differences should be changed. implementation rule do not replace this lifecycle fix with blanket invulnerability, damage filtering or guessed collision layers. lifecycle ownership and active collision semantics are separate problems and must remain separately testable. later source-runtime collision-layer result (november 15, 2026) a separate active-state source audit resolved the previously unknown layer distinction. all 13 retained edf4.1 mothership401 shkts (29 bodies) author layer 0. among 18 part sgos, only ufomother401_corepanel.sgo has is_keyframe_ragdoll=1: edf4.1's panelbase then sets its ragdoll to layer 7. the regular branch retains the ragdoll's shkt-authored layer 0; its independent object+0x3f0 helper uses layer 13, not the ragdoll. the examined edf6 eventanimationobject forced its ragdoll to layer 17. source-aligned 0/7 restoration before disable is now a bounded candidate, not a runtime-proven fix. see full original mother401 ragdoll layer evidence. this new finding supersedes the older suggestion that no evidence-backed active-panel layer rule had yet been recovered. it does not change the requirement to test panel activation and actual enemy interaction in edf6. source: r13_functionality_wip_r12_mother401_source_runtime_layer_evidence.json. r175 active-panel query visibility is a third independent state the original pre-activation world-membership rule above is unchanged. a later exact-build source comparison adds a third, independent constraint after activation: the ordinary edf4.1 panel's main ragdoll rigid bodies remain on authored layer 0, while a separate internal query container uses layer 13. the keyframed core uses main ragdoll layer 7. merely calling enable() at the correct time does not reconstruct this query configuration, and merely changing the target ragdoll's layer does not prove the correct activation timing. the examined edf6 area-damage query also operates on layer 13. whether it sees an ordinary layer-0 target rigid body depends on the actual deserialized group-filter table, not on layer numbers alone. the later static translation is therefore conditional: preserve 0 when query 13 sees 0, choose 7 only if it cannot see 0 but can see 7, and otherwise keep 0 with visibility unresolved. this candidate cannot be called a runtime repair for spiders, deroye, flying units or the reported premature panel contacts. see the exact source and target layer/query matrix. evidence: the later r13_functionality_wip_r13_mother401_query_proxy_evidence.json, which refines the older r12 discussion; it does not supersede the already-verified source activation-boundary finding.

edf 4.1 friendly npc hybrid runtime contract vehicle runtime class compatibility and online ownership friendly-npc behavior is not independent of its vehicle's native abi. the edf4.1 v301 tank, v408 motorcycle and v406 begaruta case study shows failures caused by missing cas rest tracks, mismatched drive parameters, hand-ik producers and differing gun mount counts. registered object authority versus unregistered local-copy ownership is a separate multiplayer requirement for npc crew and vehicle-owned projectiles. another source-to-donor class abi example: dragonbig401 the giant dragon's timed flame behavior illustrates a parallel issue: target animation files may parse correctly yet the edf6 donor class can still fire a different projectile and lack the source mab attack events. this is class-specific gameplay-semantic reconciliation, not a generic file-conversion change. animation controller compatibility is independent of friend ai a compatible edf6 base class may require anmgroup player names and vcontrol variables missing from edf4.1's animation file even if the original model, clips and recruitment script are correct. the bounded source method uses trackless donor clips and plain-variable grafting, with validated index/string rebasing; it avoids copying donor motion onto foreign source bones. see cas players and vcontrols and canm pose rebasing. this is distinct from deciding whether edf6 ledge climb should be preserved. the missionbundle intentionally uses a hybrid friendly-npc strategy: preserve mission-authored edf4.1 semantics and source identity where material, while using edf6 runtime/base-class behavior when it remains functionally compatible. mission semantics preserved by the converter the maintained conversion path preserves source recruitment/follow intent: createfriend preserves source canrecruit; createfriendsquad preserves source canrecruit; createfriendgroup preserves source canrecruit; setaiautofollow remains direct follow semantics; recruitobject maps to the corresponding leader/follower relation via setaifollow. the converter therefore does not redesign all friend behavior around a new command menu or one universal recruitment model. friendly soldier identity ranger / heavyarmor / palewing npcs preserve source-facing data including: visual identity; appropriate cas contract; ragdoll/model-related source data; colors; voice/talk behavior; soldier weapon slots; private/source npc weapon contract; mission-authored role/squad data. their base/runtime behavior can remain edf6-native for surfaces such as steering or minor tuning only while mission-authored gameplay stays functionally equivalent. why edf6 ledge climb is removed edf6 ledge climb is deliberately not inherited by edf4.1 friends: the original edf4.1 cas does not contain the corresponding climb states; climb changes traversal semantics; it also appeared in a stuck-npc failure mode. rule: do not restore climb merely because the target engine supports it. what functional parity means do not chase float-for-float movement equality by default. a modest speed/steering difference can be acceptable if the npc still performs the authored behavior. a compatibility fix becomes necessary when the target runtime causes an npc to: fail an authored route; get stuck where source traversal does not; change tactic/formation materially; fail recruitment/follow transfer; break mission progression. navigation geometry must be checked before blaming actor ai, because all-16-map donor nav mismatch is already a known limitation. explicit exclusions from the minimal compatibility dll the missionbundle does not install the all forces gameplay redesign: player enemy control; controlled pvp; rts/support systems; m-menu command/recruitment redesign; automatic vehicle crew/gunner behavior; generalized player-vehicle systems. old upstream declarations retained only to compile selected translation units are stubbed/no-op where not mission-required. recommended runtime order a focused friendly-npc qualification sequence is: vanilla recruit marker; approach + recruitment; non-recruitable squad; leader death / squad transfer; setaiautofollow / recruitobject transitions; ranger traversal; fencer/heavyarmor traversal; palewing traversal; vehicle402/403/404 role/voice/icon/loadout/ai; mission restart/state reset. do not test the all forces redesigned command workflow as if it were the target product; it is deliberately outside scope. source skeleton axis and climb-state contracts the retained edf4.1 r9 source documents a separate spine-aim up-axis issue: sampled edf6 soldier skeletons put the up-axis on local x and use human_direction_adjust=2, while edf4.1 models use local y and mode 1. using the target mode with source bones makes a soldier bend instead of twist. source weapon grips also require animated, weapon-dependent ik rather than static wrist offsets, and a retained exact-build analysis explains how edf6 ledge-climb can deadlock on four missing cas states. see spine axes, ik and climb-state deadlock.

edf 4.1 m015 shield bearer demo-airstrike boundary source behavior the scripted “breaking through” demonstration establishes a real gameplay invariant: the demonstration airstrikes fail against the defensive screen and the shield bearer remains alive/unharmed afterward. a port in which that scripted airstrike kills the shield bearer is therefore a fidelity failure, not harmless target variation. why the fix is not “give it more hp” the old bridge relied heavily on stock edf6 shield bearer behavior. r12 improved the physical collision side by pairing edf4.1 alientrailer401 variants with corresponding native edf6 e513 shield shkt geometry. that does not prove identical damage semantics for: area damage; scripted/demo airstrike damage; forced-damage flags; shield/body acceptance routing. no evidence supports blanket invulnerability or a generic hp increase. current r12 collision bridge the collision mapping is: s → e513_barrier_s.shkt; l → e513_barrier_l.shkt; ll → e513_barrier_ll.shkt; xl → e513_barrier_xl.shkt. the geometry match is strong and the target shkt uses edf6-native hknp representation. this is a collision-format compatibility decision, not a damage-policy claim. runtime gate the required test is mission-specific: run the m015 scripted demonstration; verify the airstrike hits the intended shield interaction; verify the defensive screen behaves as in edf4.1; verify the shield bearer remains alive/unharmed after the demonstration; ensure ordinary later combat/damage remains functional. if the demonstration still fails, inspect the exact scripted-airstrike/shield damage path before changing the object globally. rule preserve the source interaction, not a guessed immunity property. a scripted demonstration can depend on damage type, shield query, forced-damage semantics or routing that a generic stock target object does not expose identically. r175 original script-object and collision evidence: do not infer immunity the original edf4.1 and edf6 demoairstrikee50_10.sgo files are byte-identical in the inspected source corpus (sha-256 b186d3f74d4ee4d77f222087a15d26d6cc01c96d04eaff36dc0ad3d23dd08dad). their source-controlled demoairstrike uses a bombingplane (bomber401) with damage 1000, height 250, speed 3, spread 10, target adjustment 0.5 and target distance 100. these are original object fields, not evidence that a target-side animation, physics query or damage result must match automatically. exact edf41.exe source analysis identifies the demoairstrike event handler at rva 0x2bd560. it accepts event 0x80000004, resolves its bombingplane and assigns a scaled bombing-damage value to the plane; the identified seam is not a direct forced-damage bypass into the shield bearer's hp. independently, edf4.1 alientrailer barrier construction attaches body metadata key 2 (around 0x1dc2f4 → 0x606b30). edf6 native e513's alientrailer_barrier also uses body key 2 to reach barrierinfo, which participates in hostile-projectile stopping. this correspondence makes the stock-native barrier route plausible, not proof of all kinds of scripted bombing protection. an earlier source-to-target shkt census establishes four bounded geometry pairs, not equal havok files: edf4.1 ragdoll_alientrailer401_barrier_{s,l,ll,xl}.shkt (havok 2014) and edf6 e513_barrier_{s,l,ll,xl}.shkt (havok 2020). their observed half-extents are close to 50, 100, 200 and 470 respectively, but even closely matching aabbs do not prove identical layer filters, projectile interception, explosion damage or runtime state. the exact component bounds and sha-256 values are in data/r175_edf41_edf6_shieldbearer_four_shkt_aabb_pairs.csv. these results refine the older statement that an unknown generic source/target damage-scalar mismatch was the obvious cause: no relevant divergence was established at the compared demoairstrike or bomber401 sgo scalar level. the real m015 demonstration remains an unresolved runtime fidelity test, not an authorization to grant blanket invulnerability. sources: r10_hf4_r10_m015_shieldbearer_static_evidence.json (november 5), r10_hf4_r12_shieldbearer_native_collision_evidence.json (november 6), and start_here_r13_functionality_wip_r13_2026-11-15.md (later binary-path clarification).

bigcannon part exists, hull damage is disallowed. after that gate, resolve the canonical edf6 rigid-body name ragdollproxys.weak. if lazy lookup fails, reject the current hit, clear the failed-lookup sentinel and allow a later hit to retry resolution. only exact identity with the weak rigid body permits post-gate hull damage. a generic hit on the visually exposed hull is not equivalent. the former fail-open behavior accepted arbitrary shell hits after an unsuccessful weak-body lookup, potentially reducing hull hp and advancing the mission's scripted phases prematurely. the source-level fix was subjected to nine focused static checks, not an edf6 runtime retest. this mechanism is a useful general lesson for ported multipart bosses: a missing collision-body reference must not turn a source weak-point requirement into global vulnerability. identity must be established before debugging a tester's visible “mission 40” label must not be mapped to an internal edf4.1 mission id by position alone. the pinned campaign source order's slot 40 is m501, not the mothership/starship case under investigation. the later audit identified the relevant internal starship mission as m210. this is an important conversion rule: use the built missionpack metadata/output identity, not displayed numbering assumptions, before patching a mission state machine. current object-action contract the ufomother301 bridge already exposes the source-expected parts/action sequence: part family enable action attack-on action bigcannon 3 5 cannon 8 10 panel 13 15 the retained m210 bvm action sequence is statically consistent with this objectaction / getpartsobject contract. two historical failure candidates already addressed parts availability on creation frame createhull() calls spawnparts() before returning from the factory because source mission logic can issue creation-frame objectaction / getpartsobject operations. a bridge that deferred parts creation would change the mission's state-machine semantics even if all parts appeared one frame later. hull damage acceptance hullaccept() is fail-closed while ragdollproxys.weak cannot be resolved. it retries later rather than accepting arbitrary hits during incomplete object setup. this prevents initialization timing from silently turning into a damage-state change. current conclusion there is no current source/static evidence for another m210 transpiler patch. the previously reported skipped turret-activation / directly destructible cannon/weakpoint behavior is still a runtime progression gate. if it reproduces, the correct next step is a source-bvm versus generated-ac event/factor/object-state trace using the confirmed m210 identity. do not do do not assume visible mission number equals internal mission id; initialization; do not call a static action-table match a runtime progression pass.

edf4.1 mission behavior: friendly npcs, actors, physics and content scope evidence boundary: original edf4.1 resources, later edf5/edf6 native comparisons and observed problems with converted edf4.1 playable stage or multiplayer session. campaign and add-on scope the retained content-accounting comparison reports 147 distinct edf4.1 missions across 89 base offline, 9 base online-only, 26 dlc1 and commands, map geometry, collision filter and navigation paths. in earlier converted edf4.1 maps, external testing observed allies stopping at terrain/buildings, choosing paths incompatible with the source geometry, and failures of ranger/wing diver recruitment. these are observations of the converted runtime, not established faults in original edf4.1 ai. simply transplanting donor edf6 nav or matching object names does not demonstrate traversal parity. the underlying research distinguishes different questions: recruitment: whether the corresponding class has an eligible follow/recruit state, whether the interaction is exposed and whether ai follow behavior actually changes in game. movement: whether the available nav connects start and destination regions and respects an agent's size, walkable surfaces and collision constraints. physical contact: whether the engine's rigid body/query layers allow or block particular actors against a given map feature. a havok collision the edf6 runtime or that their nav matches edf4.1. the earlier 16-map surface subset and later 18-map havok body census are different populations. earth eater panels and shield hector an earth eater ragdoll::disable/ragdoll::enable as relevant native calls in the investigated runtime. evidence for their use in a particular compatibility implementation does not establish that every original edf4.1 in-game playback. see dragonbig401 native sound roles. earlier modified edf6 gameplay exhibited vehicle boarding sounds and unusual behavior in all forces-derived vehicles. these effects may depend on third-party crew/boarding code and should not be attributed to stock edf4.1 mechanics without independent original-game evidence. bmpt floating rear-light placement and vehicle controls are separately source-list census. edf4.1 friendly npc recruitment and pathfinding across all converted maps in edf6 runtime. active earth eater panel contact/filter behavior; shield hector shield-body parity. edf4.1 mission content: offline campaign, dlc, online-only scope and before.bvm evidence level: source-file classification, original script/container observations and scoped conversion comparisons. the numbers describe distinct content sets; they do not certify complete edf6 gameplay behavior. see the original-versus-converted mission coverage explanation. how many edf4.1 missions belong to each set? the retained original-source comparison distinguishes 147 reported distinct edf4.1 missions from the 138-mission conversion subset documented in earlier research: content scope mission count in earlier 138-mission subset? main campaign, offline 89 yes main campaign, online-only stages 9 no dlc1 26 yes dlc2 23 yes reported original content union 147 138 included, 9 excluded the nine online-only stages are based on the retained original-source scope comparison; their complete ids and placement in the original online missionlist.sgo have not been independently verified by a full original list census. consequently, 147 is a bounded content-accounting result, not a new direct list-file enumeration. conversely, the converted set's 138/138 source test does not establish that original edf4.1 contains only 138 missions. original dlc mission identities include dm101 and dm202. their numeric ids are not evidence that dlc and online-only contents share one simple sequential numbering scheme. native source roles and cross-generation script differences edf4.1 original mission logic is stored in .bvm scripts, while edf6 normally consumes angelscript .ac mission scripts. a converter can pass source syntax and reference checks while still missing original gameplay effects, events or npc behavior. this is a distinction between native file semantics and converted content, not a description of a required editor workflow. observed edf4.1 bvm container elements include a 0x50-byte header, 16-byte function-table records, packed opcode/operand widths, relative branches and a utf-16le string pool. the native bvm structure reference explains these measurements and what is known to survive a cross-generation representation change. mission-specific .rmpa data and map .rmpa data have distinct source roles even if the filename extension is shared. a valid resource graph depends on preserving that context. one historical conversion corpus reported 138/138 passing offline checks, but those were source/link/build checks, not 138 successful edf6 mission playthroughs. the omitted online-only set remains outside that denominator. native before scenes four pre-mission scenes remain bvm/rmpa rather than being renamed into angelscript: m015; m016; m190; m192. the observed source roles are before.bvm plus before.rmpa, not ordinary .ac mission scripts. renaming a file does not change its semantics; pre-mission presentation has its own ui and event timing. see the observed black-screen case. runtime and evidence boundaries the historical offline source check included a compatibility implementation for edf4.1 enemy/boss logic, pre-mission scenes, audio and a current-hp-only mission command. these are cross-generation implementation observations, not evidence that edf6 natively provides every edf4.1 behavior or that npc movement is correct on edf4.1 geometry. there are three distinct checks: original content: establish the correct .bvm/.rmpa files, campaign/online/dlc scope and original source identities. structural translation: check whether the target representation retains the same intended events, values and resource references. gameplay: observe the mission, allied recruitment and pathfinding, bosses, before presentation, sound and multiplayer under a matching edf6 runtime. only the first two were meaningfully addressed by the earlier 138-mission source verification; the third was not established for the complete campaign. a structurally valid converted mission can still fail because the native map nav, asset binding or game-specific api behavior differs. related native command and presentation details the bvm 3025 research distinguishes a current-health multiplier from modifying maximum hp. the before.bvm ui case distinguishes a successfully running scene script and audible dialogue from visible presentation under an hq black fade. both are examples of game behavior that file conversion alone cannot certify. provenance and preservation: this explanation synthesizes the earlier 138-mission raw source check, its four before roles, the later 147-versus-138 original-content reconciliation, and the native bvm/3025 findings. the exact older technical/implementation-oriented wording is preserved separately in the archive as a prior-edition source snapshot; it is not promoted into the reader as a guide to an sdk, compatibility dll or editor.

edf4.1 mission bvm is a real virtual machine container, not a text script the edf4.1 mission.bvm / before.bvm container includes globals, a typed-function table, executable bytecode and utf-16le strings. a retained, source-backed converter can rebuild these scripts into the form used by the edf5 edf4.1 mission archive and ultimately by an edf6 compatibility runtime. this is a separate edf4.1→edf5 bvm stage from the edf5→edf6 bvm→angelscript transpiler; do not conflate the two sets of calls or source authorities. exact bvm envelope the examined files use little-endian words and this layout: offset field known contract 0x00 magic bvm (including trailing space) 0x04 header bytes 0x50 0x10 version 0x01150138 0x18 / 0x1c global count / global-name table 4-byte name pointer per global 0x20 / 0x24 function count / table 16-byte rows; call-stub offset, name offset, parameter-type offset and packed signature 0x28 / 0x2c vm stack capacities both 0x200 in the studied profile 0x30 initializer entry after the function table 0x34 function-code base offsets for call stubs are relative to this base 0x38 string-pool start immediately after code 0x3c script name offset string name such as mission or before 0x4c file size header-asserted 16-aligned total; padding 0xba strings are utf-16le, null-terminated, with literal occurrences deduplicated in the source compiler's first-use order before global and function names. the parameter type codes in the measured table include 0x01 int, 0x02 float and 0x03 string. the observed high signature flag 0x100 indicates a returned value left below the return address for two shipped helper patterns; unknown flags are rejected rather than guessed. vm instruction encoding and branch sizes the low six bits of each first byte are the opcode. the top two bits select the operand width: 0, 1, 2 or 4 bytes. certain typed opcodes have one additional trailing type byte. signed operand interpretation applies to the studied push, relative branch and call opcodes; other immediates are unsigned. four native opcode families 0x2c..0x2f use ids local to each native table — a raw id is not an api identity without its table. function rows point to call/end stubs at the end of executable code; the bodies appear in table order and begin after a three-instruction epilogue (pushl 0; fp+ n; ret). a parser must resolve branch and call targets against real instruction boundaries and reject a jump outside its own function. the retained generator reproduces the historical compiler's variable branch sizing: it first reserves four bytes for every branch/call, then resolves smaller operands forward rather than running an ordinary repeated relaxation pass. that distinction matters for byte-exact output even when both generated programs behave the same. the source documents parse/build byte identity over 270 edf4.1 base and 55 dlc bvm files. it separately reports that the edf5 compiler's transformation of 135 paired edf4.1 base scripts reproduced edf5 bytes. these are retained corpus assertions; this release did not obtain/re-run the original game archive comparisons. edf4.1 → edf5 source recompile is a semantic transformation beyond opcode renumbering, the paired source compiler has rules affecting mission behavior: edf5's common helper functions replace the edf4.1 library before main; numbered funcnnn event handlers become sequential func_1, func_2, etc., including their counter names. four edf5 g_sergent slots (main plus three followers) are inserted after the handler counters and initialized to -1. the converter rebases all referenced user globals, including values passed through the vm's indirect global-store pattern. registerevent receives an extra argument; for the clearing handler the extra value is 100 rather than the usual 0. handlers that have the original run-once guard gain a progress update and an additional mission still running / clear-state gate. main preloads three edf5 result screens following the original setup native, and unconditional jump-to-jump chains are threaded. native opcodes are mapped using an explicit table; a script-native from edf4.1 that has no compatible edf5/edf6 binding is rejected rather than emitted as a wrong call. for dlc calls absent from the base-game pairs, the source also records engine-dispatcher mappings. the edf4.1 table-1 3000 setencountreportradius has no native edf5/edf6 script binding in this path; the studied compatibility plugin supplies a distinct table-1 id 3003. this is not edf5's separately documented cuscall0 3450 setaisearchradius, whose omission from the edf5 port was consciously accepted. identical english ideas about a “radius” do not make those two abi calls interchangeable. what authors should check validate the header, every indirect offset, each string, all function stubs, function-level branch targets and type bytes. compare raw bvm and edf5-recompiled bvm separately from later angelscript ac. preserve the original event graph and source resource-path rewrite policy. do not infer that a successful static source conversion proves mission completion under an edf6 runtime. related: bvm custom calls explained, edf4.1 raw bvm mission pipeline and dlc resource namespaces. six original edf4.1 bvm missions: native event and creation-call census a separately retained set of six decompiled original edf4.1 mission.bvm scripts (m001–m004, m012, m014) allows a bounded source-level comparison of mission structure. this is not the edf5 m014 cave case or the edf5/edf6 edf5_old_script 141-mission corpus; equal numeric mission ids from different games are not interchangeable. the table counts textual native cuscall0 instructions in the saved asm, not proven runtime-executed calls or distinct spawned enemies. original edf4.1 source createenemy 2000 createenemy2 2001 createenemygroup 2002 registerevent 2 allenemydestroy 9100 m001 0 0 1 1 1 m002 10 0 0 0 0 m003 0 0 1 1 1 m004 1 0 0 1 1 m012 2 0 5 19 4 m014 0 20 0 14 1 m002 caveat. the original nw_testmap.mac scene creates 10 individual enemies (three ants, two bees, three nephila, two ufo10) by cuscall0 2000. its decompiled program still includes a generated func1709960674 clear-handler body, but no textual call to registerevent (cuscall0 2) or createeventfactorallenemydestroy (9100). the mere presence of that handler is not proof it is registered or reachable, nor proof that the map is impossible to complete; enemy generators: count semantics, lifecycle and controller pattern evidence: shipping mission.ac call corpus and source-level api interpretation. unknown native caps and exact e505 landing-completion signal remain unresolved. edf6 exposes several generator-related concepts that must not be collapsed into one generic “spawn limit”. the shipping mission corpus supports a more specific model. generator api families setenemygenerator periodic producer: setenemygenerator( slot, resource, count, level, unit_interval, wave_interval, encountered ) the strongest shipping-ac interpretation is: emit count units in one group/cycle; space individual units by unit_interval; wait for the next group according to wave_interval; repeat until cancelled/host lifecycle ends. shipping comments describe count as the number generated, unit_interval as the interval per unit, and wave_interval as the interval until the next group generation. there is no established explicit total_limit parameter in this call. setinstantenemygenerator finite producer: setinstantenemygenerator( slot, resource, count, level, unit_interval, encountered ) the corpus pairs this call with factor_waitgeneratorend(host, slot), including missions that start one or multiple finite batches and wait for their completion. this is the strongest evidence that the instant form has a natural finite end after the requested batch is emitted. cancelenemygenerator cancels one generator slot on the receiver/host. a historical script/helper addresses slots 0..7; this is evidence for that helper only, not proof that every edf6 object type implements eight functional slots. factor_generatorenemycount is not live child count this is the highest-value semantic correction. factor_generatorenemycount(n) tracks a generator-object/host population threshold rather than the number of living children emitted by one pylon. corpus evidence distinguishes it from live-object counters: missions use factor_generatorenemycount while operating multiple nest/carrier/generator hosts; a retained source comment explicitly distinguishes whether a mother object is counted as a generator; missions may combine factor_teamobjectcount(team_id_enemy, n) and factor_generatorenemycount(m) in the same logic, showing that the two predicates observe different state. do not use factor_generatorenemycount to answer “how many spawned spiders are alive?” live-object counters use the factor whose ownership matches the desired population: need appropriate factor family all live enemy-team objects factor_teamobjectcount(team_id_enemy, n) live objects in an area factor_areateamobjectcount(...) live objects in a controlled group factor_groupobjectcount(group, n) active generator/host population factor_generatorenemycount(n) finite producer slot completion factor_waitgeneratorend(host, slot) do not substitute one family for another because the names all contain “count”. no proven native active_limit / total_limit parameters the recovered mission-script call signatures expose: slot resource count level unit_interval wave_interval (periodic only) encountered no evidence-backed generator signature adds native active_limit or total_limit arguments. this does not prove the edf runtime has no hidden global/per-host/per-slot population cap. it means such a cap has not been recovered as an exposed mission api parameter and cannot be treated as an established native mission argument. deterministic total-spawn limit when an authored mission needs a real total production cap, use finite batches plus author-owned state rather than pretending the periodic call has a total-limit argument. example requirement: 20 enemies per wave 0.5 s per enemy 30 s between waves 100 total emitted robust pattern: spawned_total = 0 repeat: current_batch = min(20, 100 - spawned_total) setinstantenemygenerator(slot=0, count=current_batch, unit_interval=0.5) arm next event with factor_waitgeneratorend(host, 0) on finite batch end: spawned_total += current_batch if spawned_total >= 100: cancelenemygenerator(0) stop wait(30) start next finite batch in edf6 mission-event terms, factor_waitgeneratorend is an event factor, not a synchronous/blocking function call. incoming anchor / e505 timing boundary a retained incoming anchor script sequence creates/configures the producer and then triggers e505_generator_action_fall. therefore it does not establish the semantic guarantee “begin producing exactly 20 seconds after landing”. the corpus did not establish a first-class factor such as: factor_e505landed factor_objectactionend waitanchorlanding an arbitrary wait() after action(fall) is therefore not exact “time after landing” semantics. without a proven landing-completion factor, an action-relative wait() is only an approximation. exact timing needs the actual native landing-completion signal. runtime questions still open the retained source/api evidence does not yet settle: whether the native periodic generator has a hidden live-child/global-team/per-host/per-slot cap; whether exceeding such a cap delays, skips or queues a spawn; whether wave_interval is measured from cycle start or from completion of the prior batch in every native path; the exact e505 pylon landing/action-completion signal. a minimal runtime discriminator should compare periodic batches with survivors left alive, partial kills, global enemy pressure, two slots on one host, two hosts, mid-batch cancellation and host destruction. the native interpretation remains unknown without such observations. related native edf game references native edf5 generator 0x20100 fields and wave loop r174 source-call count versus producer capacity: a 141-mission counterexample an independent audit of 141 original edf5 bvm mission scripts found 571 cuscall0 2100 and 270 cuscall0 2101 sites, alongside 664 2000 and 722 2001 sites. these are distinct source api transactions, not 841 produced waves plus 1,386 living enemies. for example, m004 contains 162 source-side enemy/generator/drop-boat transactions in the historical corpus, but neither that figure nor its breakdown fixes how many actors exist at once. the different identifiers and per-mission counts are catalogued in data/r174_edf5_original_141_mission_spawn_source_call_census.csv. source-site totals must not be substituted for factor_generatorenemycount, factor_teamobjectcount or factor_groupobjectcount: those factors inspect game state, whereas the atlas counts authored instructions. no new first-class active/total limit api, native generator cap, or runtime scheduling rule was proven by this census. the source corpus is edf5, not the six-file edf4.1 script subset used in the old lifo engine reversed it. enemy02 is different: below hardest it uses ordinary giantant04×3, with goldant×3 only on the higher branch. thus on easy the first golden trio is not expected, while the later five goldant are unconditional in source. source dm019 creates three recruitable friend squads and immediately assigns their routes and speeds. there is no later source call that starts their routes only after recruitment. the relevant lowerings are global setairoute(obj,route) and setaimovespeed(obj,speed); the 44 official-port corpus contained 708 global route calls and 514 global speed calls, with zero method-form instances in that corpus. 2008 is createenemygroup_area by opcode, not an sgo-dependent ground/flying heuristic. 2006 is the flying-area opcode. r37 formalizes this distinction and regression-tests both. 2001→createenemy2 remains runtime-confirmed for the wall anthill/spawner case. the lighting omission and spawner orientation were mission-semantic defects, not reasons to mutate map collision. 15.2 dm020 read-only globals source constructs tank01_1..tank01_4 only. tank01_5 and tank01_6 are later read/used, but no source constructor/store was found. do not synthesize vehicles 5/6. treat this as a declaration/type-inference problem; do not ask for a nonexistent fmb. the deep-convex source-consistency detector uses source hkt plus source mad/mac context, closed convex primitives only, closest-edge bridge, penetration length >=0.05 m and fraction >=0.90, with fail-closed guards. it selected only dm019 high, ig_edfroom01 low and ig_edfroom02 high in the audited set; it selected zero on dm019 low, the opposite ig variants, cave503, heigen507, nw_europe01, kaigan502, sangaku506 and desert508 low/high. desert's largest tiny contact with thresholds disabled was only about 0.0139 m. the dm019 high structural candidate was a 2↔3 streaming relation (face24/edge74 ↔ face195/edge735) whose closest-edge bridge gap was about 1.114206 m; about 1.108306 m lay inside a roomb closed convex, penetration fraction about 0.994704. this is a real structural inconsistency finding, not the behavioral root cause: r2o removed it and the ai-vs-ai wall-targeting symptom remained. exact reversed-boundary streaming matching achieved 100% precision at strict tolerance in the audited same-map native pairs, but recall was insufficient—especially for edfroom. therefore “retain exact reversed matches only” is invalid. native edf6 frequently rebuilds topology;
