is higher authority for the subsequently identified m039 local variable defect. this page records source-derived port semantics, not a claim that unmodified edf6 has these bugs.

edf6 weapon-drop candidate eligibility: weapontable.p8 and level windows edf6's weapon candidate selection checks more than a mission's difficulty and nominal reward-level range. binary analysis and a limited test in a modified edf6 runtime identify a class filter driven by weapontable source property p8. it is a loot-family discriminator, separate from the mission's modelist or missionpack number. candidate-filter sequence observed in one edf6 binary in the examined edf.dll (sha-256 0d5092393a1b9d8f1b75b0c93d8a8f65615a36a92c46e40349c2b66c733d0916), the trace is: resolveresult() at edf+0x2c92e0 derives the eligible weapon-level interval. a downstream candidate-builder entry near edf+0xd81e0 reads decoded weapon rows; the analyzed source fields include p5 and p8. the p8 filter is applied before the level-range filter. in the observed native rule, p8=0 passes this classification check; nonzero p8 must equal the active logical missionpack id. eligible rows then continue through their level checks and the remaining game-selected reward steps. the decoded runtime structure at this stage included source p5 at +0x1c and p8 at +0x28; these are runtime decoded record offsets, not asserted bytes within raw file storage. the symbol names and rva observations apply only to the cited binary build. p8 is not the missionpack number intended loot pool base p8=0 candidates dlc1 p8=1 dlc2 p8=2 base/ordinary class 0 eligible by class no no dlc1 class 1 eligible by class eligible by class no dlc2 class 2 eligible by class no eligible by class this table describes the class gate, before considering level ranges or other downstream conditions. dlc1 and dlc2 classes each include common/base p8=0 rows; p8=1 and p8=2 are not interchangeable. in the observed custom port, missionpack03, 04, 05 represented native content classes 0, 1, 2; that relationship was created deliberately and is not an automatic stock edf6 rule. actual dlc2 discrimination test the retained 5 october 2026 test used a modified missionpack09, explicitly assigned dlc2 class 2, with edf6's native ig_test_bluefld map. five silverspiders were placed in a simple mission to supply boxes. the offline preflight validated the source and binary signatures; a separate later game run reported: runtime observation recorded value class resolution packentry=9, desired class 2 candidate level calculation lo=81.25, hi=106.25, extra=1.25 scanned p8=2 rows 110 newly admitted rows (fix_add) 34 added candidates' levels 106.25–107.50 sample added row index 1451, level 107.50, p8=2 visible result-screen drops n9 eros vulture zam and gigantocopter 3 delta, both lv 107, air raider this test is runtime-positive evidence that the patched candidate builder can admit and reward dlc2-exclusive weapons for a custom missionpack that the native id-to-p8 comparison would otherwise exclude. it is not evidence that unmodified missionpack09 naturally selects dlc2 loot, that higher than lv 107 rewards were observed, or that every row in the 110-row class was awarded. the high-end hi+extra behavior was recorded in the test interval; it should not be generalized into an undocumented global reward formula. why some older negative tests are not evidence earlier experimental runs labeled r1 and r2 failed their binary signature validators before the required game hooks could run. their apparent no-op behavior therefore cannot falsify the loot-class hypothesis. in r1 the caller signature was anchored at an incorrect instruction boundary; r2 expected an incorrect resolveresult() prologue. the later runtime observation comes from a distinct, validated test candidate. this section concerns confidence in the findings, not instructions to install any of those loaders. follow-up: original edf5 dlc2 port mission in mp05 a separate, later game run used the actual edf5 dlc2 mission content in a customized edf6 missionpack05, rather than the earlier instrumented missionpack09 demonstration. the validated diagnostic log reported four true mp05 scans (n=2…5), with packentry=5 translated to loot class 2. its recorded eligibility interval was lo100=8798, hi100=11298, extra100=125 (hundredth-unit values). the log contained 392 fix_add records across the mp05 scan output. the newly admitted dlc2 p8=2 candidate levels included 106.25, 110.00, 111.25, 112.00 and 112.50. this is stronger evidence for class-2 candidate admission in real edf5 dlc2 port content, rather than only the deliberately assigned mp09 test fixture. the number 392 is a count of logged additions, not a proven count of 392 distinct weapon identities or awarded items. nor is a candidate of level 112.50 proof of an on-screen lv112 reward: the earlier mp09 run separately showed two awarded lv107 weapons, while the later mp05 evidence establishes admission to the scanned pool. attribution and scope: /edf5_edf6_research/research/active/patch_1_0_5/edf5_edf6_patch_1_0_5_rc1_source_and_audit_authority_2026-10-05.zip, inner package/real_mp05_dlc2_loot_runtime_evidence.txt and handoff; reported user game log and qualified modified binary. the original game engine's p8 field behavior is static-binary evidence. the additional mp05 scan is a modified edf6 runtime test, not the unmodified native edf6 drop table, a complete dlc1 acceptance matrix, or a verified distribution of rewarded items. what remains unproven the mp09 runtime acceptance confirms dlc2-exclusive lv 107 rewards in one instrumented game session. a separate real-mp05 dlc2 session confirms additional eligible candidates up to 112.50, not on-screen 110+ awards. together they still do not qualify all dlc1/dlc2 or arbitrary packs, all difficulties, every weapon level, or the distribution of high-level rewards. no new game run was performed for this wiki article. source provenance: /edf5_edf6_research/research/active/mission/dlc_loot/edf5_edf6_dlc_loot_r3c_runtime_acceptance_2026-10-05.md; the corresponding r3c_mp09_native_map_test_final_offline_audit_2026-10-05.json is a pre-runtime static qualification and is not itself runtime acceptance; the earlier r2_static_ledger_2026-09-21.md documents the binary filter trace. for the short class/pack distinction see loot classes versus missionpack ids.

edf5 versus edf6: dlc mission completion and the ending presentation the last mission of a downloadable-content campaign may complete normally, set the correct mission result, and still omit the dlc-specific ending scene and audio. the retained edf5/edf6 mainscript.as comparison explains why this can occur when edf5 missions are hosted in new edf6 missionpack ids. edf5 source-side behavior for the final mission of a dlc campaign, the recovered edf5 mainscript uses a post-mission dlcending() path when getcontentid()!=0. its named presentation resources are: ending ui: app:/ui/lyt_endingdlc.sgo. music cue: bgm_e5s08_endingteloponline. this is a result-side/mainscript event, not simply a special enemy-death event placed inside the last mission's mission.ac or mission.bvm. why edf6 behaves differently with new pack ids the examined stock edf6 mainscript handles the recognized content identifiers 0, 1, and 2 after the last mission. when edf5's dlc1 and dlc2 content is instead hosted as custom identifiers 4 and 5, those custom ids do not select an equivalent dlc-ending branch in the native handler. the mission can still proceed to ordinary result processing. this is a cross-generation/custom-id compatibility boundary, not a claim that official edf6 dlc modes omit their own endings. distinguish final mission clear from dlc ending native mission/ascommon.h exposes two distinct in-mission clear presentations: call cue/layout wait result classification missionclear_edf5() jingle_missioncleared, lyt_huimissioncleared.sgo 6 s mission_result_clear finalmissionclear_edf5() jingle_missionclearedfinal, lyt_huimissioncomplete.sgo 10 s mission_result_clear both terminate through internal_exit(mission_result_clear); the latter differs in ui/audio/time but does not reproduce the separate edf5 dlcending() mainscript path. the original inspected edf5 dlc final-mission bvms use ordinary missionclear, so replacing it with finalmissionclear_edf5 would change the authored in-mission sequence rather than restore source fidelity. presentation resource checks the lyt_endingdlc.sgo ui layout is present in the examined edf6 resource corpus. however, the retained archive did not contain the target audio-bank acb bytes needed to prove that edf6 can actually resolve bgm_e5s08_endingteloponline at runtime. presence of a named cue in source text is not evidence that the target audio bank implements it. a source-preserving custom mainscript branch for custom content ids 4/5 was statically prepared in the research. this page does not present that as stock behavior or as a fully tested ending. a global mainscript override may also have compatibility effects unrelated to dlc endings. source provenance: /edf5_edf6_research/research/active/mission/dlc_audit/edf5_edf6_tester_feedback_r6_release_policy_2026-09-27.md and edf5_edf6_tester_feedback_r5_offline_checkpoint_2026-09-27.md, backed by comparisons of edf5/edf6 mainscript.as and edf6 mission/ascommon.h. no new in-game audio/end-scene test was performed for this article.

edf6 fmb terrain: complete leaf semantics and secondary-layer boundary the .fmb terrain resource is not an ordinary .mdb model. in the examined edf6 source corpus it contains a spatial directory of tree records and compressed leaf payloads. a leaf combines triangle/vertex geometry, a mass cell grid, local material identifiers, shader selectors and material weights. the correct interpretation depends on each leaf's own descriptor and reference bases; merely unpacking the cmpl wrapper or displaying the triangle mesh does not establish semantic correctness. full native control corpus an exhaustive read-only census of the six retained ig_heigen507*.fmb files decoded and structurally validated all 1,200 leaf records. the combined directory contained 2,394 records: 1,194 internal/tree records and 1,200 leaves. the scan evaluated 1,045,523,544 decoded bytes, 2,058,350 triangles, 1,085,605 vertices and 12,582,869 mass cells. all listed semantic error classes were zero in this bounded corpus. a separately inspected ig_cave503.fmb added 102/102 passing leaf controls. this does not mean all fmb assets in every edf6 build have identical flags, counts or selector assignments. main ig_heigen507.fmb example measured property observed value fmb version 0x110 (decimal 272) directory 511 records: 255 tree + 256 leaves material / config tables 6 materials / 27 config rows main-map triangles 2,040,200 main-map vertices 1,070,192 main-map mass cells 1,620,528 mass cell x/z dimensions approximately 77–80 cells per leaf main mass-cell size 2 m × 2 m native terrain xz bounds approximately −1250 to +1250 on both axes leaf sizes, geometry counts and mass-cell layouts vary within these ranges. a decoder should verify each leaf rather than using main-file averages as constants. checks that distinguish a correct decoder from a plausible-looking preview for each leaf, the recovered structural relations include: exact cmpl decompression and agreement of wrapper versus decoded bounding boxes. the index array and triangle count must agree: index_count == triangle_count * 3. index storage must be followed by the properly aligned mass-cell region; mass_count == dividex * dividez. the decoded vertex tail occupies vertex_count * 24 bytes in the audited native layout. the material list is a fixed-size sparse list; active material ids must resolve within native material tables. material weights may reference only active local slots, with valid selector/config-row bounds. reserved fields and weight padding must satisfy observed zeros. a successful render does not excuse inconsistent reserved data. the 16-byte materialidlist is sparse. the byte value 0xff means this slot is empty, not stop parsing now. its actual arity is the count of non-0xff slots, not the index of the first hole. a capacity-like word in the leaf descriptor is a separate field; it is not universally identical to the local material-list arity. merging those concepts would misdecode valid native leaves. shader selectors are not proof of finished rendering one flat, experimental fmb record used two triangles, four vertices, two local materials, config index 4 and the shader config row (2,1,0,0,0,0,0). the associated selector/capacity pair 0x0202 + cfg4 also occurred in 80 of 118 inspected native heigen enkeiright leaves, supporting the established filename resolution map_field_render2_1_14_0.sgo for that particular selector. that selector match is structural evidence. it cannot prove that non-native material/orientation records render correctly. the experimental record's two 80-byte material records did not match any of the retained heigen/cave native material records exactly. orientation and texture-slice bindings also differed. a black terrain surface therefore cannot be diagnosed solely from filename selection without direct rendering evidence. for source texture-array and preview-attribution boundaries, see fieldrender/fmep records. planar material orientation is a separate native byte contract the native ig_heigen507_enkeiright.fmb planar material and orientation records survived an exact parse/re-serialize round-trip: material 0 and both orientation records were byte-identical. comparing the retained experimental fmb with native enkeiright material 0 gives a narrower, unproven rendering discriminator: semantic field native enkeiright material 0 experimental flat record planar paint mode / correction 0 / 6.0 0 / 6.0 base/color and normal slices 0, 0 0, 0 base/detail orientation pair (0,1) (0,0) detail/multiplier texture slice 1 0 euler orientation (90°,0°,0°) for both native orientations (0°,0°,0°) projection scales (7,7,7) and (100,100,100) (20,20,20) the exact shader specialization already matched a native-observed selector; these remaining byte/semantic differences are why matching an fmb shader filename alone does not validate planar terrain rendering. no direct in-game experiment in the inspected source establishes the root cause of a black surface or grants a universal material conversion rule. the separate auxiliary floats were deliberately not assigned a guessed native role. why ig_heigen507_2.fmb should remain a distinct unknown the retained _2 file is not corrupt. it passes the same structural checks with 468 leaves, a 1-metre mass-cell grid, sparse geometry of roughly 1–61 triangles and 3–46 vertices per leaf, and central coverage around 2500 × 2500 metres. it shares the main map's six-material/two-orientation structure and material lookup table, although its 27 config rows appear in a different order. however, the examined ig_heigen507.mac explicitly names the main and four enkei fmbs but does not name _2; the retained rab also provides no _2 name link. the sources did not establish an implicit *_2.fmb loader rule. the only defensible classification is structurally valid secondary fmb with an unresolved native loading role. its presence is not permission to assume all secondary fmbs load automatically. evidence: primary r39_fmb_full_semantic_census_2026-10-16.json, map_studio_r39_progress_2026-10-16.md, and r39_authority_supersession_2026-10-16.md under /edf5_edf6_research/research/active/map_authoring/r39_fmb_full_semantic_census_2026-10-16/. only native file semantics are reported here; the separate preview/authoring code is not part of the game contract. native planar-material orientation field example a separately decoded enkeiright material 0 uses two orientation bindings, base slice 0, detail slice 1, normal slice 0. this is a material/orientation table example; it must not be confused with the leaf-local 16-byte materialidlist, whose non-0xff occupancy has different semantics.

edf6 heigen507: same rock family, different native collapse graph an edf6 native mapb t1 object family does not always identify one universal destruction graph. the five ig_heigen507 rock-set families examined here have one mapo slot per placement, four p58 pieces per placement, and stable body/resource ownership, yet their t50 graph differs from one placed t2 instance to another. complete five-family native census t1 native resource t2 placements distinct t50 graphs slots per t2 pieces per t2 14 sk_rock501a_set.mdx 17 9 1 4 15 sk_rock502a_set.mdx 17 10 1 4 16 sk_rock503a_set.mdx 15 6 1 4 17 sk_rock504a_set.mdx 20 10 1 4 18 sk_rock505a_set.mdx 27 20 1 4 total five families 96 55 all five families were observed to have one stable slot pattern, one p58 group schema, one mad body set and one rab closure each. together their native body-set union contained 20 distinct bodies and their family resource closure 22 rab assets (without a separately required shared donor reference). the variation is not caused by a different number of mesh slots or a different rock body type in each placement. the changing information is the t50 topology attached to its specific placement. exact per-placement identity matters a converter cannot safely cache one t50 template under the t1 resource name and reuse it for every t2. doing so can silently change which rock fragments are connected, even when all referenced geometry, p58 pieces and collision bodies are identical. the stable native association is: mapb t1 rock-set family ↓ mapb t2 exact placement / variant ↓ mapo slot -> p58 four indexed pieces ↓ mapo t50 associated with this exact t2 ↓ mad bodies used for those piece indices an offline enumeration verified 96/96 placements without coercing any to a different template. a separate composition of all 55 distinct graphs preserved exact parsed t50 semantics and passed basic mad structural checks; no new edf6 runtime test accompanies this evidence. this is distinct from the nw_europe01 multi-storey buildings, where t50 often connects different building slots. the heigen rocks show that placement-specific t50 variation also occurs inside a single slot with a fixed four-piece set. scope and unresolved questions the evidence covers these five named native rock-set resources; it does not establish that all edf6 destructibles vary per t2, or explain why each heigen placement receives its exact graph. a generic proximity or radius-based generator remains unverified. if faithfully reusing a native placement, preserve its t2 → t50 identity; if authoring new fragments, do not present a guessed graph as exact sandlot output. related references: native building t50 graphs and crashmodel and native havok static/dynamic body roles. evidence: map_studio_r43_heigen_rock_set_multi_t50_progress_2026-10-16.md, r43_all_variants_summary.json, and r43_unique_t50_result.json under the retained /edf5_edf6_research/research/active/map_authoring/r43_heigen_rock_set_multi_t50_2026-10-16/ source set.

edf5→edf6 hkt: graph edges, clearance caches and numeric decoding a source navigation graph can look valid in a high-level hkt inspector and still be misinterpreted if a parser uses the wrong element widths. the ng_dlc_edfroom03 / dm019 comparison is a concrete case: graph topology, narrow flags, cache arrays and havok's 16-bit real encoding have distinct rules. these observations describe paired edf5-to-edf6 navigation data, not a universal reconstruction of edf6's proprietary navmesh baking process. graph connectivity is independently countable the examined dm019 low/high navmeshes retain a coarse inter-cluster graph that can be reproduced directly from current face cluster adjacency: graph edges derived from face adjacency stored edges missing extra duplicates low 84 84 0 0 0 high 374 374 0 0 0 both versions used 8-byte graph edge records in this particular compatibility comparison. the source dm019 record's byte2 flag and byte3 padding were zero in the audited set; native edfroom01's comparable flags16 fields were also zero. no “padding interpreted as active flag” defect was demonstrated here. consequence: rebuilding the exact same cluster graph from unchanged face adjacency cannot add missing connectivity. a real route defect may lie elsewhere: underlying faces, streaming links, agent queries, clearance, or the target selection logic. the graph check is a structural invariant, not a diagnosis of why an npc chose a target behind a wall. hkhalf16 is not ieee float16 and not four-byte float32 one earlier decoder consumed four bytes when reading a two-byte hkhalf16 bedgecost, inadvertently incorporating the next two bytes and reporting false numeric graph differences. in the examined havok type family, hkhalf16 represents the upper 16 bits of an ieee float32 value; reconstruction places the stored 16 bits in the high half and zeroes the lower 16 bits. it is not an ieee binary16 conversion. for example, a stored high-half word 0x3f4c reconstructed as 0x3f4c0000 is a float32 value, not the number obtained by decoding 0x3f4c as ieee half precision. a byte-exact round-trip and a semantic decoder must implement their respective roles independently. correctly decoding this field removed false numerical mismatches during the dm019 comparison. it did not repair edf6 gameplay, because the affected source serialization already retained the relevant raw data. clearance arrays: element abi versus generated semantics the audited edf5→edf6 pair included these physical arrays: array inspected element type important interpretation faceoffsets uint32 index/range lookup, not real-valued clearance edgepairclearances uint8 per-edge-pair clearance byte mcpdata 2-byte record first byte: interpolant, second: clearance vertexclearances uint8 per-vertex clearance byte those element widths are compatible in this bounded pair, even though the enclosing cache structures and target generation behavior may differ. a precomputed edf5 clearance value can be syntactically valid yet semantically stale for an edf6 navmesh or agent profile. a controlled source-only experiment omitted clearance seed datasets and initial cache objects while retaining 10 low / 10 high navmesh records. the resulting hkt remained structurally comparable outside that intentional omission. this proves a feasible wire-level subtraction; it is not a positive in-game fix for ai targeting or route selection. evidence hierarchy static: graph edge counts matched source face adjacency (84/374); no extra/missing/duplicate coarse edges; correct hkhalf16 decoding; 2-byte mcpdata and documented array widths. runtime-negative in the broader room test: changing facedata/nvmd section identity did not correct spiders' wall-targeting symptom. unresolved: whether a particular cache, query filter or hkainavmesh variant changes ai line of sight. structural hkt validity is not evidence for one specific perception mechanism. see hkt/nvmd native rebake versus compatibility and physical wall versus ai targeting. source evidence: /edf5_edf6_research/research/active/edfroom/audits/edfroom_graph_and_clearance_audit_2026-08-25.json, runtime/edfroom_r2n_no_clearance_seed_manifest.json, and the independently observed negative wall test runtime/edfroom_r2i_runtime_negative_2026-08-25.json. the numerical findings are scoped to the examined maps and file versions.

edfroom mad: triangle conservation and physical wall integrity a havok compressed-mesh conversion may perturb the decoded coordinates of individual vertices while preserving shared seam continuity and physical blocking. the ng_dlc_edfroom03 research provides measured source-versus-target collision geometry and a later gameplay observation that distinguish those properties from ai decisions. full controlled collision inventory the retained candidate mad represented 101 direct compressed meshes. the source triangle census and the deterministic degenerate-triangle filtering result were: item count source logical triangles before filtering 315,460 removed by the bounded degeneracy predicate 17,509 expected kept triangles 297,951 target metadata triangle count 297,951 independently decoded target logical triangles 297,951 the degenerate-filter study used a 1e-7 source-area tolerance. this is the converter's audited filtering rule, not proof that every native edf6 map filters its geometry with this exact tolerance. the candidate's compressed-mesh broadphase audit reported 166,084 expected shape keys, exactly 166,084 reachable unique keys, and zero missing keys, extra keys, duplicate leaf keys or >1e-4 bound violations in that examined run. the audited mad also contained 289 physics bodies (287 static and 2 dynamic). passing these checks establishes physical wire/graph consistency for this candidate; it is not equivalent to a full native havok gameplay qualification. shared-section seams were preserved despite coordinate rounding an independent exact identity audit examined 20 named wall/corridor/collider records, including multi-section wall geometry. every audited record reported zero seams exceeding 1 mm, 5 mm or 10 mm, with maximum measured shared-boundary discontinuity 0 under the audit's source-key comparison. this does not mean the target compressed positions equal source floating-point vertices exactly. the largest measured individual quantization errors included: collision record triangles maximum decoded coordinate error (source units) shared seam maximum ya_edfroom_roomb.roomb_collider 1,701 0.0458995 0 ya_edfroom_rooma.rooma_collider 966 0.0276907 0 ya_edfroom_corridor_slope.side_wall 144 0.0225413 0 ya_edfroom_corridor.side_wall 144 0.0217197 0 ya_edfroom_corridor_r.side_wall 164 0.0210661 0 interpretation: the compressed coordinates are quantized; however, vertices that are supposed to represent the same seam remained co-located under the measured source-key identity relation. a nonzero source-to-target error is not by itself an opening in the wall. conversely, this localized metric does not guarantee every triangle in every map is topologically or physically correct. independent in-game observation in the affected edfroom/dm019 scene, characters could not walk through the tested wall and spider web projectiles hit the wall rather than penetrating it. some spiders still aimed/fired toward allied npcs on the far side. a later controlled high-only streaming-link change did not remove that ai behavior. this makes the following explanation unsupported: “spiders attack npcs through the wall because the collision exporter created a gap.” the surviving candidate explanations belong to ai-vs-ai target selection, perception/los queries, agent-specific navigation and target routing; none was conclusively identified in the retained runtime experiment. see physical wall versus ai targeting and navigation graph and clearance data. source evidence: edfroom_mad_filtered_conservation_2026-08-25.json, edfroom_mad_wall_seam_exact_audit_2026-08-25.json, edfroom_mad_broadphase_2026-08-25.json, edfroom_mad_wire_2026-08-25.json, and edfroom_ai_wall_runtime_observation_2026-08-25.json under /edf5_edf6_research/research/active/edfroom/. all metrics are bound to the specific source/converted collision corpus.

edf6 static water: the native class-10 map object the examined native edf6 nw_europe01 water surface is not merely a blue texture on a terrain plane. its mapb object class, object sgo, mapo resource companions, render mdb and static mad/havok body form a distinct map resource family. the measured example is eu1_nw_field01_water.mdx; the geometry and material values here are scoped to that native object rather than all water in the game. observed cross-file object graph native resource component retained observation mapb t1 class 10, eu1_nw_field01_water.mdx t1 object sgo 33 named fields including type="水", collision_enable=-1, durability=0, crashtype=0, fencetype=-1 mapb t2 one measured native placement in the retained map mapo slot closure visual .mdb, _hk.mdb and .hkt companion identities mapo destruction topology 0 t50 pieces and no p58 destruction group for this water object visual mdb shader snd_brdf_map_water, 26 parameters, four sampler slots, mesh stride 60 bytes native mad collision named body eu1_nw_field01_water.water, static hknpcompressedmeshshape mad body fields materialid 0, motiontype 0, mass −1, massdistribution 0, motionpropertiesid 0xffff in this exemplar geometry visual mesh 10 triangles, matching native planar collision representation 10 triangles with nearly identical aabb the material's four observed sampler names are bubble_albedo, normal_map1, normal_map2, normal_map3. its other parameters concern water colour/specular/roughness, bubble/normal-layer controls and uv behaviour, but the exact shader equations are not recovered from the object graph alone. how to interpret these values class 10 is the observed water t1 role, not proof that every resource with class 10 must be a water plane. type="水" (japanese water) is a named sgo value on the native object. collision_enable=-1 and durability=0 are stored values; they do not by themselves define the full water physics or damage model. the mad body is a static compressed mesh, not a simulated fluid volume. its special mass/motion fields must not be copied indiscriminately to ordinary destructible props. absence of p58/t50 fits this non-destructible water exemplar; it does not prove that all aquatic objects in edf6 have no destruction support. the retained native geometry is planar with a shared visual/collision footprint. this is distinct from assuming a generic actor can swim, drown or collide with a volumetric fluid. binary-format consistency versus rendered water a controlled experiment recreated a different, simple two-triangle horizontal visual/collision water surface with the same kind of class-10/sgo/mapo/mad graph. its wire, first-primitive and compressed-broadphase checks passed offline. that establishes that the investigated structure can be serialized in a bounded authored case. it does not establish accurate in-game water draw, near/depth fading, texture scrolling, collision, culling or performance for a new map. across the four retained map-family rab scans (nw_europe01, heigen507, cave503, desert508) exactly one snd_brdf_map_water material was observed. no separately named universal river or ocean material family appeared in that finite sample. this is not a global statement that edf6 lacks rivers or oceans. related information: native edf6 static-water material, mapb structure, mad/havok body roles. primary evidence: map_studio_r51_water_surface_authoring_2026-10-16.md, particularly its read-only nw_europe01 native source census; cross-check map_studio_r48_water_family_reconciliation_2026-10-16.md and map_studio_r40_native_specialized_material_abi_2026-10-16.md. the native object observation and experimental authored serialization have different proof levels.

edf4.1 earth eater: panel ragdoll collision layers and generation mismatch the mothership401/earth eater in edf 4.1 distinguishes between ordinary panel ragdolls and the keyframed core. in the inspected source binary, most ragdolls retain their authored shkt collision layer 0, while the core's sgo takes a separate branch that changes its ragdoll to layer 7. a native edf6 eventanimationobject constructor used by the investigated conversion instead assigns the constructed ragdoll to layer 17 (0x11). these are concrete, build-scoped engine facts, not proof that changing the converted object's layer alone fixes the observed enemy ai/physics anomaly. edf4.1 sgo policy: which panel is keyframed? the retained source corpus contained 18 mother401 part sgo records. exactly one has is_keyframe_ragdoll=1: ufomother401_corepanel.sgo (class=ufomother401_core, ragdoll mothership401_centershaft.shkt). the remaining 17 examined sgos have no such enabled field, including panel, weak-panel, generator, cannon, final-generator and battery components. the edf41.exe panelbase shell-builder function at rva 0x26fab0 reads is_keyframe_ragdoll: edf4.1 condition observed source action loaded panel ragdoll layer absent/zero key ragdoll loader mode 1; no later ragdoll-layer override in this branch retains source shkt-authored 0 non-zero key (core) ragdoll loader mode 2, then source ragdollsetlayer at rva 0x334370 with argument 7 7 all 13 source mothership401 shkt files, representing 29 examined bodies, carry authored collision layer 0. the layer 7 on the core is therefore a runtime branch decision, not a pre-authored core shkt layer. why layer 13 must not be applied to ordinary panel ragdolls the non-keyframed branch additionally changes a different component reached via object+0x3f0, setting that component's collision-filter low layer bits to 13 through the source helper around rva 0x0eec00. this component is not the loaded panel ragdoll. the complete recovered source flow therefore does not say that all ordinary ragdolls run on layer 13. three values belong to three different entities: 0 (ordinary ragdoll), 7 (keyframed core ragdoll) and 13 (separate non-keyframed helper). merging them is a collision-modeling error. target edf6 behavior and limits of the comparison the inspected edf6 eventanimationobject creates a ragdoll and forces its collision layer to 0x11 / decimal 17. its native ragdoll setter was identified at edf rva 0x6e9320; the generation comparison also identified native ragdoll disable/enable control at 0x6e97c0 / 0x6e9840. the source-compatible candidate restores 0 or 7 after target object construction but before pre-activation removal from the physics world; when the panel is activated the same ragdoll is re-enabled. restoring the layer through edf6's native setter preserves non-layer filter/grouping bits. this is a source-informed compatibility hypothesis; it has not yet been confirmed in a windows edf6 gameplay test. battery objects are excluded from this candidate. three separate gameplay/physics questions before activation: does a panel have an active collision body in the world when edf4.1 would not? this is a lifecycle/world-membership question, independent of collision layer. after activation: does the panel have the correct ragdoll layer, filter group, body set and collision/query behavior? this is the 0/7 versus 17 comparison. ai and interaction: even a source-consistent filter does not prove that spiders, deroye, flying enemies, explosions and grounding queries behave identically. a direct mixed-enemy runtime regression is still necessary. the tester's reported problem—enemies spawning/standing on inactive panels, later climbing or sticking to active panels and sometimes leaving the map—was observed in the port, not demonstrated as a stock edf6 bug. there is no justification for changing global collision filters, blindly writing layer 13 to ragdolls, or claiming all mother401 variants share the core's layer. evidence and version scope source binary: edf41.exe, sha-256 39b4abf7fe722175741a5e0a154063b27ef8c589a1aa5f86c84853571ac7bda8. edf6 engine binary: build identified in the retained r12 comparison, native ragdoll setter at edf+0x6e9320. rva values are not universal across releases. direct retained inventory: 18 source sgos, 13 shkt files / 29 bodies. static source audit pass; new edf6 runtime result absent. primary source notes: r13_functionality_wip_r12_mother401_source_runtime_layer_evidence.json, start_here_r13_functionality_wip_r12_2026-11-15.md and r12_tester_feedback_coverage_audit_2026-11-15.md. see also earth eater panel physics lifecycle, earth eater grid and multiplayer identities. r175 exact native query-container and edf6 visibility decision the earlier layer 0/7/13 distinction is correct but incomplete without the native query stage. in the pinned edf4.1 panelbase branch, the main ragdoll wrapper is at object+0x328. its separate, legacy query/collision container is reached through object+0x3f0 (= ragdoll+0xc8). the non-keyframed path at rva 0x26fc52 calls helper 0x0eec00, assigning layer 13 to the container's primary and linked bodies while retaining other filter fields. the keyframed path at 0x26fc43 instead calls ragdollsetlayer(ragdoll, 7); it does not turn all normal panel rigid bodies into layer 13. in the examined edf6 build, the relevant area-damage query uses query layer 13 (rva 0x106070). the target eventanimationobject initially sets the created ragdoll to 17 at rva 0x5b6401; its main-body array/count reside at +0x78/+0x88 in the studied wrapper. a target group-filter table can be read via the identified vtable path (0x17e0788, table offset +0x58). this is a build-scoped description of the original engine's visibility mechanism, not a stable public api or a claim that these numeric offsets work on another patch. situation layer relevant to the examined body/query what is actually known edf4.1 ordinary panel 0 main ragdoll and 13 separate internal query container both are present in the source branch; two objects, not two names for one layer edf4.1 keyframed core 7 on main ragdoll only ufomother401_corepanel.sgo enables is_keyframe_ragdoll in the 18-part corpus edf6 eventanimationobject default 17 on target ragdoll different engine generation; not an equivalent translation of the source query container investigated target-side compatibility: query 13 sees 0 keep main ragdoll 0 source-faithful rigid-body layer already passes the relevant query target-side query 13 cannot see 0, but sees 7 select main ragdoll 7 conditionally an explicit conditional approximation of the missing source query container, not proof of equal collision response filter table missing or both candidates invisible keep 0, report unknown visibility no unconditional fallback to 7 or direct assignment of 13 the full original collision corpus has 18 part sgo descriptors, 13 shkt files and 29 rigid bodies. all 29 studied shkt rigid bodies author layer 0; some keep nonzero subsystem/system-group/don't-collide fields, so an all-zero filterinfo rewrite is not equivalent. the exact per-part class, selected shkt, body name and original filter fields are retained in data/r175_edf41_mother401_original_18_part_sgo_collision_roles.csv and data/r175_edf41_mother401_original_29_shkt_rigid_bodies.csv. the decision cases are in data/r175_mother401_source_target_physics_query_decision_table.csv. provenance and limit: r13_functionality_wip_r12_mother401_source_runtime_layer_evidence.json (original sgo/shkt/branch evidence) and subsequent r13_functionality_wip_r13_mother401_query_proxy_evidence.json (the later, stronger query-container and target-filter interpretation); edf6 projectile rng consumers: ammoclass and networkbullet reference scope: static analysis of one edf6 edf.dll build, sha-256 0d5092393a1b9d8f1b75b0c93d8a8f65615a36a92c46e40349c2b66c733d0916, joined to an audited 1,315 active-configuration weapontable/star-state corpus. this is a reader reference for the game binary, not an sdk promise or an in-game synchronization test. how a random state reaches a projectile common weapon projectile creation at edf+0x696fd0 derives a value from the 64-bit weapon lcg. the engine writes the upper-derived projectile value to the class-specific bullet initparam +0x1a0 at edf+0x69776d. bulletbase construction at edf+0x22e9c0 loads the initparam field and stores the zero-extended value in the finished bulletbase +0x130. they are different object layouts. common bulletbase does not itself continuously consume +0x130; derived classes may do so. state_next = (state * 0x5d588b656c078965 + 0x269ec3) mod 2^64 all seven subtype1-capable projectile families in this shipped corpus the star-envelope join produces these capable-weapon counts by ammoclass (a configuration is counted as capable even if some of its star states choose direct fire): ammoclass weapons capable of subtype1 proven class-owned consumer of bullet +0x130? laserbullet01 72 no in the audited constructor/vtable region solidbullet01 46 no in the audited constructor/vtable region flamebullet02 18 yes, constructor-dependent motion lightningbullet01 16 yes, constructor + onupdate path acidbullet01 8 no; an apparent +0x130 reference was stack-local solidexpbullet01 6 yes, detonation countdown laserbullet03 6 no in the audited constructor/vtable region this table must not be read as an assertion that other projectile types never use rng. several such as spiderstringbullet03, plasmabullet01, napalmbullet01 and missilebullet02 do consume projectile rng, but are not subtype1-reachable within this particular audited shipped-weapon star envelope. three important class consumers class native observation gameplay effect what networkbullet does not transmit flamebullet02 constructor edf+0x260aa0 advances +0x130; writes +0x11d0/+0x11d8; onupdate edf+0x2622a0 uses them motion/direction of flame evolves from locally constructed random scalars scalars +0x11d0/+0x11d8; selector1 only, selector0 disabled lightningbullet01 constructor edf+0x259e40; onupdate edf+0x25ad10; rng helper edf+0x04eb60 and direct lcg randomized path and replicated movement direction rng +0x130 and internal path +0x1160; selector1 only, selector0 disabled solidexpbullet01 constructor edf+0x28db80 sets countdown at +0xf00; onupdate edf+0x28f340 decrements and later spawns blowhit01 randomized detonation/hit-spawn time countdown +0xf00; constructor clears inherited selector1 to 0, no common selector enabled in checked path a subtle but important distinction: the class state can diverge after remote subtype1 reconstruction even when initial spread is deterministic. of the 40 subtype1-capable weapons using these three families, 38 have firespreadtype 0, one spread1 and one spread2. their distribution is: class capable always subtype1 switchable via stars flamebullet02 18 18 0 lightningbullet01 16 7 9 solidexpbullet01 6 5 1 total 40 30 10 separately, six always-subtype1 weapons have rng-sensitive initial spread types 1/3; lightning rapid bow t2 belongs to both groups. thus the union is 45 subtype1-capable configurations, of which 35 are always subtype1. these are two related but distinct scopes, not conflicting counts. receiver catch-up and why eventual seed equality is not enough subtype1 publishes a cumulative shot target after the normal six-weapon-update delay. a later receiver can catch up on shot count by creating missed projectiles locally. under strict equal-seed and equal-total-update/projectile-step conditions, the current weapon lcg can reconverge after that catch-up. nevertheless the newly created projectile gets the receiver's later historical sample, not the sender's original sample. a later common networkbullet selector does not serialize the class-specific random fields in the table above. no automatic recovery of those historical values is established by the inspected recurring protocol. this explains a possible static synchronization gap, not a guarantee that every visible multiplayer shot desynchronizes. the size and frequency of actual divergence require paired runtime traces. other true rng consumers excluded from the subtype1 set spiderstringbullet03::onupdate (edf+0x285700) advances +0x130 and derives a class scalar at +0x108c. napalmbullet01::onupdate (edf+0x2641f0) derives a randomized spatial vector. missilebullet02::onupdate (edf+0x26e4c0) derives and stores a randomized spatial vector around +0x15d0. plasmabullet01 constructor (edf+0x25b650) consumes bullet-local rng; another later code path uses process-global rng and must not be conflated with the projectile state. simply matching a memory displacement like +0x130 is insufficient: for example laserbullet02 and barugacannonbullet contain similarly named/positioned accesses that were not qualified as consumers of this bullet-local lcg state. evidence boundary and related reading the quoted offsets, class inventory and star-envelope counts are from static native binary and source data analysis. no new edf6 multiplayer runtime test is claimed. read weapon rng and batching, networkbullet selectors and star-dependent fire policies. sources: edf6_engine_re_post_r12_rng_lifecycle_wip_2026-09-29.md, edf6_engine_re_post_r13_projectile_rng_consumers_wip_2026-09-29.md, edf6_engine_re_post_r14_networkbullet_reconciliation_wip_2026-09-29.md, and the respective qualified r13–r15 checkpoints. exact native reference tables projectile and weapon layout fields — static r17 per-build catalog; byte-identical records: native material 0 and native orientations 0 and 1. it also retained a four-float auxiliary vector on material 0: (6.0, 0.5019609928131104, 0.5019609928131104, 0.0) the 6.0 slot is the studied correction scalar. the downstream meaning of all auxiliary lanes is not fully proven from this isolated record; do not invent gamma, tint or alpha roles merely because two values resemble 128/255. the native fmb used in the audit was identified by sha-256 0027ed493827ccfcdc0906f5efb5714c00b68567400fe505f741df756074dd31. this hash identifies one retained binary source, not all edf6 versions/maps. limits on interpretation source bytes establish the field values and serialization identity. they do not prove the exact gpu coordinate formula for every fmb shader family. a mismatch with an experimental fmb identifies plausible discriminating variables; it does not prove the mismatch caused any black-terrain symptom. enkeiright material 0 is one native exemplar. other heigen fmb leaves and directional variants use different tables and may require config-index remapping. offline parity is not evidence of new edf6 map rendering success. primary sources: /edf5_edf6_research/research/active/map_authoring/r40_native_planar_profile_preflight_2026-10-16/r40_native_planar_profile_preflight_2026-10-16.json and the matching r40 native-planar preflight report. see also native fmb leaf and material-slice semantics, fieldrender texture-array and slot model, and native fmb family/config variants. the shader's more general mode 2 (three projections, including a row1-axis sign-dependent slot 1/2 selection) was established independently by controlled september r4 dxbc comparisons. this one native mode-0 enkeiright record does not constrain the edf6 insect and tadpole attacks: damage, volleys and levels evidence: source-attributed static analysis of the studied edf6 steam-678ccb46 binary and object sgo records, collated by novae (ajane) in the edf knowledge hub (14 november 2026, revision 54f89cd). these are base attack formulas, not measured damage against a particular player at a particular difficulty. no new edf6 runtime experiments were performed for this article. read the formulas correctly l is the raw game-object level read by the enemy's level setup, not the difficulty name and not the player's armor. some source records use v = l / 10 instead. each line is per projectile or per hit, unless explicitly called a volley total. multi-projectile attacks must be counted separately. online game modes may multiply a delivered hit according to the hit-record type. thus these formulas are not necessarily the final on-screen hp loss. values such as ant_ex_damagescale, spd_ammo and dragon_attackbulletsetting come from each enemy's source asset and can distinguish variants of the same class. ants: one class, two different projectile behaviors attack raw source formula other parameters normal ant acid (ant_bullettype=0) max(0.5 × l, 1) × ant_ex_damagescale per drop min(trunc(l/5 + 1), 16) drops per volley; speed l/400 + 0.4 m/frame; lifetime 180 frames queen ant stream (ant_bullettype=1) 0.08 × l × ant_ex_damagescale per drop speed 1.0; lifetime 240 frames; 90-count initial stream counter, with one bullet emitted per observed firing call ant bite 0.5 × l × ant_ex_damagescale, then animation-event damage_scale sent through the type-3 hit path, unlike the projectile's type-0 record the acid path uses a capped bullet-count function; do not multiply its damage by 16 at low levels. at l=10, the count is 3, whereas at l=100, it is capped at 16. giantant04sb has source ant_ex_damagescale=2.5; the regular recorded value is 1.0. the queen stream's 90-count field is not independent proof that all 90 hits actually land. the source stores the ant's bullet init parameters beginning at giantant+0x1680; ant_bullettype is at +0x1670 in the examined build. these are version-specific memory offsets. hornets: regular needles versus queen needles variant damage per needle other observed parameters normal giantbee max((l/1.5 − 20/3) × 0.58 + 20/3, 1); equivalently about max(0.3867l + 2.8, 1) count min(trunc(l/5 + 1), 16); lifetime 180 frames; size 0.2 queen hornet (insectbase_type=1) 0.5 × l + 15 1.5× speed multiplier, lifetime 300 frames, size 1.0, blast radius 3.0 the queen is not just a larger normal bee: the code selects another branch with another damage curve. the source analysis found no extra bee damage-scale sgo key in this calculation. spiders: thread count and sgo multipliers the spider thread uses spd_ammo = [size, speed multiplier, damage multiplier]: field formula / value thread damage 0.375 × l × spd_ammo[2] per thread; the source also contains a lower-bound fallback when the calculated value is nonpositive thread speed (l/400 + 0.8) × spd_ammo[1] thread size 0.1 × spd_ammo[0] thread count min(trunc(l/5 + 1), 16, spd_maxstringcount if present) lifetime 300 frames ordinary recorded spiders use [1, 1.2, 1]. queens use [5, 2, 2], doubling the base per-thread damage before any online modifier. the light spider e651_spider01_light has spd_maxstringcount=3. an additional +0x1958=l field was hypothesized to be bite damage; its consumer was not proven, so that value is not presented as a verified bite formula. tadpoles: fireball and bite are independent attack paths the fireball formula is max(l/3, 1) × b[4], where b = dragon_attackbulletsetting: source variant b=[size, base speed, speed divisor, spread, damage factor] resulting fireball damage dragonsmall401 and _hs [0.3, 0.6, 200, 0.1, 0.75] max(l/3,1) × 0.75 redsmalldragon and _hs [0.6, 0.8, 100, 0.1, 1.0] max(l/3,1) yerrowsmalldragon and _hs [0.3, 0.8, 100, 0.1, 1.0] max(l/3,1) volley size is min(trunc(l/10+1),8), projectile speed l/b[2]+b[1] m/frame, lifetime 360 frames and gravity scalar 0.25. the source bite uses l × c[2], with c[2]=1 for all six inspected tadpole assets; an animation event may multiply it further. how online mode can change the result the inspected native hit path marks bullets with hit-record type 0, and bites with type 3. in the community's analyzed solo normal online example, the type-0 insect bullet multiplier was 2.64, whereas the type-3 bite route used 1. these are observations of a specific modelist configuration, not universal online difficulty multipliers. do not infer: a monster's final damage from a single sgo damage value; the engine may generate multiple shots, apply hit-record-specific mode scaling, and run a separate damage-reduction path. sources and related pages original edf6 enemy attack evidence, fact ids and binary sites: ant-acid-attack-level, ant-queen-spray-level, ant-bite-damage-level, bee-needle-damage-level, spider-thread-damage-level, insect-attack-online, dragonsmall-fireball-level, dragonsmall-fireball-keys, dragonsmall-bite-level, insect-ex-attack-same. edf6 projectile contact and collision filters. native enemy/boss attack scaling. attribution: novae (ajane), edf knowledge hub, 2026-11-14, including the source contributors identified in that appendix. this page is an editorial explanation, not a new native disassembly.

edf6 drones and deroys: sgo attack records, level curves and volleys evidence: static, build-specific analysis of edf6 steam-678ccb46, contributed to the edf knowledge hub (14 november 2026, revision 54f89cd). the data below is sourced from native enemy level-setup routines and named sgo rows. it does not certify in-game dps or online damage for every scenario. gold drones (ufosmall507): bullet_info is a mini expression language the gold drone's bullet_info is not a fixed damage scalar. each entry can be a literal or a sequence of operations on raw level l. the native evaluator supports addition, multiplication, bounded minimum/maximum, reciprocal, interpolation and other operators. the resolved values determine burst count, spacing, bullets per shot, damage, speed, size, lifetime and (for bomber variants) explosion size/gravity. variant and projectile shot pattern damage per bullet other properties e507_goldufo, _hi: beambullet01 five shots per burst, spaced five frames; five bullets in a line per shot 0.07l + 1 speed 0.015l + 0.5; size min(0.003l + 0.3,0.6); life 300 frames _ace: laserbullet01 30 single shots, spaced one frame max(0.0476 × (0.6l+4),0.1) speed 30; size 0.4; life 15 frames _charge: laserbullet01 unlimited burst; one shot every max(10/(0.02l+0.8)+1,2) frames max(0.0714l,1) speed 30; size 0.4; life 30 frames _big: plasmabullet01 three bombs in a line per shot, 45 frames apart 4.5l per bomb life 2000 frames; interpolated size, gravity, radius and speed for _big, let t = clamp((l-10)/150,0,1). the source interpolation uses radius lerp(15,25.5,t), size lerp(8,13.6,t), speed lerp(0.45,0.5625,t) and gravity lerp(0.8,1.6,t). these fields should not be mistaken for a single explosive damage number. interpretation limit: a burst's number of bullets is not the number that hit the player. the drone ai's choice to begin a burst was outside the cited trace. imperial drones (ufosmall515): battery rows and difficulty-sensitive damage imperial drones instead read battery_config: per-muzzle rows with a bullet key, shot count, interval, damage source and sound information. the observed level factor for their bullet damage is: f(v) = 1 + (v - 1) × 0.5, where v=l/10. the source can select a difficulty-indexed base-damage row before applying f(v), so level and difficulty are different inputs. variant base damage before f(v) pattern / important distinction e515_imperialufo 5.5 six shots 12 frames apart; interval can shorten with level, bounded below by three frames; one projectile per shot _ace 2.0 128 shots 30 frames apart; 16 bullets per shot, spread 0.1; right battery delayed 15 frames; interval remains fixed in observed row _prototype [5.5,5.5,11,16.5] by difficulty six shots three frames apart; speed 2; life 120; blast radius 2.25 for the prototype, the source's difficulty lookup is not interchangeable with l: easy and normal use the first damage value in the cited selection rule, while hard/hardest/inferno use the corresponding later values. the exact row-index logic is explained in the source appendix. deroys (deiroi): the hull and legs use different curves the main body and its leg batteries are separate consumers of the sgo attack configuration: weapon derived per-bullet / per-missile damage evidence boundary main-body plasmabullet01 1.5l + 20 body's deiroi_battery_config; base sgo item 3 = 20 in examined variants leg beam (pulsebullet01) 1.4 × v, where v=l/10 leg-part row, static inference from level setup leg missile (entitymissilebody) 10 × v leg-part row, with missile durability also 10 × v through a separate native scaling function at l=10, these raw formulas yield 35 for the main plasma shot, 1.4 for a leg beam bullet and 10 for a leg missile. these numbers are not necessarily observed hp loss after game-mode and collision/damage routing. the binary also reads deiroi_fire_config to determine level-sensitive leg fire timing. that timer path was not fully traced, so no definitive deroy attacks-per-second curve is claimed here. model for interpreting enemy configs identify the actual native enemy class and sgo row; a shared visible mesh does not guarantee shared attack code. distinguish raw level l from normalized v=l/10 and from the difficulty-selected table value. resolve how many projectiles a fire call creates and how they spread. only then consider online damage and collision filters. source and related pages see edf6 enemy attacks — original evidence appendix, particularly drone-bullet-info-items, drone-level-expressions, drone-attack-values, imperial-drone-fire-rows, imperial-drone-attack-values, deroy-battery-damage and deroy-attack-values. related explanations: insect attack scaling and physical hit filters. attribution: novae (ajane), edf knowledge hub (2026-11-14) and original contributors documented in the appendix; static-only interpretation.

edf6 boss attack scaling: monsterbase, erginus and archelus evidence: static edf6 steam-678ccb46 reverse engineering and sgo data in the edf knowledge hub snapshot of 14 november 2026. the equations below describe source attack values, not observed player damage after online and other multipliers. why boss speed and boss damage cannot be treated as the same level scalar monsterbase stores a current attack record from an attack_setting array. the analyzed record contains the attack name, a speed value, damage values (sometimes a list), an auxiliary scalar and flags. the level setup computes g = l/10, with l the raw object level. for an attack's animation-event melee hit, the native callback uses the record's first damage value multiplied by g. its other attack fields may control the contact region, hit flags and attack speed. speed changes with level only if the sgo speed item is an expression array; plain source floats remain constant. erginus: per-hit and per-projectile damage named attack family original erginus (monster501) king variant (monster501_king) ordinary chop 100l 150l step chop 160l 240l two-handed step chop 200l 300l tail 240l 360l tackle 280l 420l ground hit 6l to 8l 12l to 15l these are the interpreted data-derived contact values by source attack row. a source speed number (e.g. 1.0 or 1.5) is not an additional damage multiplier unless the attack consumer uses it that way. erginus's breath uses an embedded lightningbullet01 projectile. for the observed attack_breath_t row, damage is 12l per fired bullet; for attack_breath_b, 2l. the king version has 18l and 9l. the source did not close the total number of bullets per breath, so the article deliberately avoids a fabricated “total breath damage” figure. archelus (monster504): sparks and contact hits differ the main attack record's damage item may contain multiple values. archelus's projectile constructor selects the second entry if present, whereas an animation contact hit uses the first. this is why “attack damage” cannot be one scalar for the entire row. attack example source value ordinary spark projectile 1.5l per bullet thorn-roll thorn projectile 1.5l per thorn thorn-roll contact 2l _vs_big spark or thorn projectile 10l _vs_big thorn-roll contact 100l the e504_monstera_m034_3 variant has lower source values in several attacks; applying the normal archelus numbers blindly to that variant would be inaccurate. speed adjustment and attack intervals the source-defined optional speed rule for list-valued speed fields is: attack_speed = min(l × a + b, c), for an item encoded as [b,c,a]. in the inspected erginus, king and archelus attack rows the speed fields were ordinary floats, so that particular per-attack speed did not scale with level. archelus also has an independent monster_base_animation_speed array. for its example [0.8,1.5,0.9,0.01], the corresponding expression is clamp(0.9 + 0.01l,0.8,1.5). this is a separate animation-speed control, not a damage curve. archelus's bullet_level_adjust was [1.0,4.0,20.0,400,400] as plain source values. some byte-level parameter interpretations remain unverified, and the exact attack-interval consumer was not followed fully; they should not be promoted to a complete physics model. evidence limitations these are native data and code reads, not full combat sessions at fixed difficulty. the emitter's animation event, projectile count, collision filter and modelist may alter what a player experiences. a stage-specific enemy asset may have different sgo rows while retaining the same broad family name. source: edf6 enemy attack evidence and exact binary sites: monster-base-level-setup, monster-attack-setting-record, monster-attack-speed-item1, monster-melee-damage-level, monster501-melee-values, monster501-breath-level, monster504-shot-level, monster504-bullet-level-adjust. attribution: novae (ajane), edf knowledge hub revision 54f89cd (2026-11-14).

ace variant 1v cyclops stomp 30v grenadier bomb object ordinary 20v; middle bomb 60v this table is not a claim that every attack in a class uses one global damage scalar. the source data place values under berserkersettings/partsshootlist, gun-battery entries and distinct bomb objects. the linked community source records identify the exact classes. scylla, haze and heavy dango creature attack asset-derived base value scylla e603_merman water-gun bullet 1v per projectile; runtime integer conversion not separately asserted here heavy dango contact lerp(100,70,q) × v or lerp(50,30,q) × v depending on attack/variant heavy dango large projectile lerp(0.2,1,q) × v the dango formulas show an important distinction: the per-level coefficient may decrease while the total product still increases. reading only the start/end interpolation endpoints leads to misleading claims about absolute difficulty. siren / glaukos (e604_radon*) attack base value and pattern flame-breath projectile 0.04v per projectile; source row mentions 120 bullets at two-frame intervals fireball 60v, 11 projectiles per volley; a source online_damage_adjust=0.7 is recorded form-2 flame channels 1.575v and 0.9v vertical channels 3.375v and 1.6875v form-2 spark 10v, blast radius 20 dive contact 60v, or 20v in named mission-specific asset variants wind pressure / wing flap fixed source values 150 / 12.5, not level-scaled the mission variants _m051, _m118_5 and _rm034 change some source values; a universal siren attack table would hide this. some entities, such as nephila (aranea), have attack logic in code that the cited sgo pass did not follow. practical boundaries these formulas are excellent for comparing which native asset paths control which attacks. they are not a substitute for determining the attack's firing count, collision and target type, online adjustment, and any class-specific code multiplier. consult native stop/hit filter behavior and the raw enemy evidence appendix before extrapolating a final damage number. attribution: novae (ajane), edf knowledge hub (2026-11-14), facts dsgo-family-damage-keys, android-attack-level, scylla-haze-dango-attack-level, siren-attack-level. no new runtime testing.

edf6 bullets: stopping ray, damaging sweep and the 32-layer collision table evidence: a combination of reported in-game filter tests and exact native steam-678ccb46 binary inspection from the edf knowledge hub (2026-11-14, revision 54f89cd; original tests credited there). the full matrix in the optional csv is derived from the source's 32-layer table; it is not newly measured in this release. two filters answer different questions in the studied edf6 build, a bullet has two collision-filter values: field default low-five-bit layer what it does flag 1 (bulletcontrol+0x890, bullet +0x9d0) 12 sweeps a thin ray along the projectile's trajectory. a blocking result shortens the path and stops motion. flag 2 (bulletcontrol+0x894, bullet +0x9d4) 11 runs a projectile-sized sphere/shape cast over that already-shortened path to find damageable targets. a piercing shot can continue through these targets. a flag-2 hit is not necessarily a flag-1 stop. a shield is a documented special case: a hit in the damage-query route can stop the bullet. an object matching neither query is ignored by that bullet path. that difference explains why a target may block a shot but take no damage, or take damage without ending a piercing shot. the order also matters: flag 2 is evaluated over a path potentially shortened by flag 1. layer comparisons are not naive integer equality the basic layer is filterinfo & 31. more complex filterinfo values may additionally contain subsystem and system-group information. when query and body belong to the same non-zero system group, the native filter may use sub-id and exclusion fields rather than the ordinary collision table. the matrix below therefore applies to the zero-group ordinary game-layer policy examined in the source, not every possible fabricated filter value. the community's numeric experiments verified that, for the tested zero-group cases, values 32, 64 and 128 behave like layer 0, and 255, 32767 and 0xffffffff like layer 31 because their low five bits match. frequently encountered body layers layer observed native targets consequence 5 live small enemies and allied infantry in the examined mode-1 family alive enemy's direct-hit body can differ from its corpse 6 dead mode-1 enemies, several vehicles, some physical debris most ragdoll parts default here 7 queen-class insects and several red anchor devices distinct from ordinary ant hit body 8 monsterbase family (e.g. siren and archelus), war barga boss-style body classification 14 kraken/red anchor shield bodies shield contact is a special projectile boundary 15 buildings and some small nests ordinary geometry/hit queries may include these 17 terrain not the same layer as breakable map objects 19 generatorpoll, large nest and some anchor devices generator devices have their own collision path 20 map props including poles and trees not necessarily treated like terrain 27/29 certain modeldebris bodies layer 29 has no ordinary collisions except with layer 0 the evidence includes direct game tests for many target-layer assignments, but several layer labels are still unresolved. a layer number is not an entity class identifier. multiple unrelated objects can use the same layer. explosion queries do not use the same filter as ordinary bullet contact the studied explosion/area-damage query uses layer 13. in the ordinary collision table it collides with layers 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 14, 15, 16, 19 and 20 (and the universal layer 0). terrain layer 17 does not appear in that list. it is therefore possible for a body to be contacted by one bullet route but excluded from an explosion query. this distinction is especially important for source-to-target shkt collision mismatches and for diagnostic reports like “the beam touches the object, but the explosion does nothing.” it does not by itself prove the cause of any specific genocide cannon problem; the accepted damage handler and visual effect also matter. data reference: complete ordinary collision table the optional 32×32 collision matrix csv is distributed as data/edf6_native_collision_layers_32x32_r117.csv in the public zip. rows are the queried filter layer; columns 0–31 are body layers; 1 means the ordinary table allows contact, 0 means it does not. it deliberately omits the nonzero-system-group special case. the reconstructed matrix is also checked for symmetry before packaging. notable properties of the recovered matrix: layer 0 matches all 32 layers; layers 30 and 31 match only 0, 30 and 31; layer 29 matches layer 0 only. these statements are about the native filter table, not about whether a body is present in the game world or whether its class can take damage. provenance and limitations the code's two-phase bullet query and the reported collision experiments are distinct evidence grades. recovered layer positions and addresses are valid for the cited build, not a guarantee for all edf6 updates. no in-game physics test was performed for r117.
