edf 4.1 sk terrain–object contacts: original seven-map source census scope: original edf 4.1 source shfb heightfields, static-object mad triangles and mapb placements across seven sk_* map families. these are offline observations about geometry and data relationships, not edf6 pathfinding, vehicle physics, obstacle avoidance, or in-game collision acceptance. this page reconciles five adjacent source audits (r24–r28, 16 november 2026) rather than listing development steps. the game-data relationship these seven maps carry source height samples in *_fld2mgrid.shfb. their placed objects and collision triangles are separate sources: the shfb defines terrain elevation and its cell layout; mapb establishes object instances/placements; mad contains physics shape geometry. a meeting point between a terrain triangle and a placed-object triangle is a geometric contact candidate. it does not say which side of the contact an npc can enter or whether a havok pathfinding agent has a passable link. for the examined terrain triangulation, the fmb-style cell diagonal is a–b–d and a–d–c. choosing the opposite diagonal changes contact geometry even when the four corner heights agree. this matters especially where roads, bridges or walls intersect slopes. source actor positions in these reports use a candidate rz × ry × rx placement transform; bit-exact parity with the original engine has not been demonstrated. seven-map census: sample contacts versus expanded placed geometry the following table deliberately separates two different investigation scopes. r24/r25 inspected only 81 selected placements and reported edge/contact contours. r27 examined 1,770 matched placements of recognized static-mesh models in the same seven map families. r27 did not establish that every obstacle shape, movable body, object or gameplay-affecting collider was covered. do not add sample counts to expanded counts as though they were disjoint bodies. original map family r24 sampled instances r24 edge–terrain intersections r25 raw contact segments r27 matched placements r27 complete r27 placed triangles r27 unresolved sk_crater01 12 579 748 187 185 49,469 2 sk_heigen02 9 359 379 265 265 41,874 0 sk_kaigan01 12 1,111 893 182 182 114,220 0 sk_sangaku01 12 693 813 207 207 35,433 0 sk_sangaku02 12 827 940 311 311 105,184 0 sk_stepmountain01 12 828 923 199 199 48,975 0 sk_valley01 12 276 324 419 417 110,478 2 total 81 4,673 5,020 1,770 1,766 505,633 4 r24 tested 28,956 unique sampled edges, excluding 15,558 shared-triangle edge duplicates and detecting 4,673 terrain intersections (none unresolved within its sampled edge scope). r25 tested 14,838 source triangles against 46,606 terrain facets and reconstructed 5,020 raw intersection segments. those segments yielded 151 closed-loop candidates and 787 open-chain candidates, with zero unresolved source triangles in that sample. loops/chains are contour diagnostics, not navigation regions or edges. r27 recorded 147,094 facet-intersection observations on 505,633 transformed/placed triangles, plus 146,989 unique segment observations in its per-instance diagnostic. these are not all the same thing as the 5,020 sampled r25 contours. five of seven maps had complete classifications within the restricted recognized-static-mesh scope; the crater and valley maps still had boundary exceptions. why the r26 and r27 figures differ the earlier r26 pass matched 1,770 placements but classified 1,765 complete, one rejected and four unresolved; it processed 502,895 placed triangles. a child/linked mapb record for sk_valleybridge1 lacked sufficient parentage qualification in that pass. r27 examined the original group relationships and retested the valley map: 1,766 complete, zero rejected and four unresolved, now 505,633 placed triangles. r27 did not fix the remaining four geometry exceptions. the r27 group-list evidence across all 16 inspected map families reported 193 child references in 18 linked groups. this is a source-data hierarchy observation; a child record cannot safely be treated as a freestanding or nonexistent placement simply because a one-level traversal misses the link. these values describe references and groups, not a count of 193 distinct colliders. four source-domain edge cases (r28) the remaining exceptions arise where source triangles and the finite shfb terrain domain only partially overlap. r28 subdivided intersecting triangles, kept track of the domain edge and counted diagnostic seam segments. it analyzed 6,040 source triangles in four affected source instances, producing 10,179 welded contact segments and 100 seam segments; one vertical/degenerate water-body case required 293 adaptive splits. all four remained partly outside the source field domain. map mapb record native object original triangles boundary crossing outside seam segments inside-area fraction sk_crater01 1 sk_craterroad01 2,430 20 60 20 84.2% sk_crater01 2 sk_craterroad02 2,394 20 20 20 92.7% sk_valley01 1 ig_valley01_water 296 15 4 20 96.5% sk_valley01 310 sk_valleyroad1 920 40 11 40 95.7% the four rows are source-body instances, not four missing maps. in particular, ig_valley01_water should not be assumed to be a traversable floor merely because its geometry crosses the terrain domain. r28 classified five water-body triangle cases as vertical/degenerate domain overlaps, and its inside-domain fragment analysis reported no ambiguous facets. that does not prove that original edf 4.1 or target edf6 applies water, wall or road collision in the same way. what this evidence does not establish no native edf4.1 havok narrow-phase contact outputs or edf6 installed collision outcomes were collected in these passes. no high/low hkt navigation meshes were generated, installed or played through for these seven maps by this research. no agent-radius, step-height, walkable-slope, off-mesh connection or dynamic-actor policy was checked in game. the placed-body rotation is a source-backed candidate but not bit-exact certified against the original engine; the field-domain seams are not an entire-world completeness proof. these seven sk maps are not all sixteen original edf4.1 map families; the other nine have different source geometry profiles. the 16-map r1d/hillycity counts (4,971 footprints, etc.) concern a different navigation reconstruction and cannot be combined with this contact census. the later r29/r30 missionbundle packaging/discovery work was offline source/runtime-code validation only, not gameplay. it does not promote these source geometric observations to game-proven collisions or fixed npc pathfinding. related original-game documentation shfb terrain field and fmb/mad generation rules original 16-family mad 3d surface survey donor-nav mismatch and target collision boundaries source mapb/mapo object hierarchy and placement data edf 4.1 navigation entry point source provenance and preservation the five unaltered source summary jsons are included under reference/r150-source-evidence/ in this release. corresponding library source folders are the original checkpoint_2026-11-16_r13_functionality_wip_r24_… through r28_… trees; edf4.1 sk source terrain and edf6 navigation: original 4 m grid, hkt/nvmd structure and limits evidence scope: seven original edf4.1 sk_* terrain source maps, the retained native shfb/fmb diagonal research, and the bounded edf6 hkt/nvmd low/high offline structural pairs documented in the 16 november r31/r32 research. no user-run edf6 game, navigation/ai runtime or installed missionbundle result was produced by these tests. this page describes game-file data and inferred structure, not an editor's release history. three distinct terrain-related grids source height samples. the seven original edf4.1 shfb assets contain 1001 × 1001 height samples at 2 m spacing, spanning a 2000 m × 2000 m horizontal source domain. the measured samples occupy a 2 m heightfield; their values are not obstacle masks. terrain render/collision geometry. the audited fmb-style terrain extraction uses every second shfb sample: a 4 m lattice with 500 × 500 = 250,000 cells and 500,000 triangle candidates. each 4 m cell uses the observed native diagonal joining a–d, yielding a–b–d and a–d–c. choosing the opposite diagonal alters local slopes and contact lines. earlier source-to-target terrain work used 625 fmb render leaves and 2,500 compressed-mesh mad collision tiles; those are different resource arrangements and must not be mistaken for hkt/nvmd streaming tiles. navigation streaming and agent data. a navigation hkt tile carries faces, edges, traversal metadata, graph/clearance and streaming relations. its nvmd companion supplies separate per-tile/placement/facedata identity information. a source-mesh triangle that can be serialized into an hkt is not thereby an accepted walkable face for ranger, fencer, hector, vehicles or a pathing agent. source shfb terrain, placed mad objects and mission-local rmpa routes are different data owners. exact seven-map source-lattice inventory all seven original shfb profiles examined have the same sampled dimensions and 4 m grid plan; their mapb source object counts differ. the 256 planned tiles per map are a 16×16 layout using up to 32×32 source cells per tile, including truncated edge tiles where required. these totals are preflight plans only; edf6 fieldrender terrain: native dds arrays, fmb leaves and mac resource registration the edf6 fieldrender/fmep terrain path is not an ordinary mdb prop. it spans terrain material and geometry records, dds texture arrays, and map-container references. a correctly decoded part does not establish that the whole chain loads in-game. this reference combines original edf6 native-asset observations with a separate, explicitly modified-game diagnostic sequence. evidence and boundaries original edf6 source files: native fmb leaves and dds from cave501, cave503, cave601_2, heigen507 and base502, plus the directional heigen507_enkeiup fmb; the september 2026 native-correlated audit decoded 1,477 leaves without errors and checked 20 dds mip payloads against exact block-compressed sizes. modified edf6 runtime observations: an experimental island4 fieldrender branch encountered two distinct loader faults. this diagnoses resource lookup and native mac directory parsing but does not establish successful custom fmep gameplay. separate known playable route: island4's static mdb map had a runtime-positive x20 r4c control; it is not proof that its later fmep branch worked. the accepted desert508 baseline is a different native-resource-continuity study, not a generic fmep source-only recipe. native terrain dds: the measured container contract all 20 examined native terrain dds payloads in this bounded corpus use dx10 headers, 2d texture arrays, complete mip chains, depth 1, flags = 0xa1007, caps = 0x401008 and caps2 = 0. the reported size checks were 20/20 exact, not just header-parse successes. texture role dimensions mip count full-resolution color 2048 × 2048 12 lod color 512 × 512 10 full-resolution normal 2048 × 2048 12 lod normal 128 × 128 8 the array slice count is map-dependent, not a universal fixed four-slice rule: native edf6 map color slices normal slices reported normal dxgi value cave501 4 3 77 (bc3_unorm) cave503 4 4 77 (bc3_unorm) cave601_2 5 3 77 (bc3_unorm) heigen507 8 6 71 (bc1_unorm) base502 12 9 71 (bc1_unorm) all five native color profiles are reported as numeric dxgi 71, i.e. bc1_unorm. source terminology correction: one audit calls that value "bc1 srgb"; according to the official microsoft dxgi enumeration, bc1_unorm_srgb is 72, not 71. this article preserves the source's numeric value and does not silently turn it into 72 or infer the final shader's color-space sampling policy. the same enumeration distinguishes bc3_unorm = 77 from bc3_unorm_srgb = 78. material records contain slice indices; the highest referenced index sets a minimum array length, not necessarily its exact native allocation. for example, base502's native color array contains 12 slices even though the cited maximum material index requires only 11. the one-material island4 candidate referenced color slices 0 and 1 and normal slice 0, so its strict minima were 2 color / 1 normal; its test used 4/4. overprovision by itself is not evidence of a broken dds. native fieldrender fmb leaves: capacity is not the active material count the corrected native audit found these wrapper counts; the six rows include one directional fmb without a separate full dds-profile row: original fmb native leaves measured material-list capacity cave501 257 1×5; 2×203; 3×49 cave503 102 2×6; 3×44; 4×52 cave601_2 484 1×484, active arity 1, field +0x30 = 1 heigen507 256 range 2–5 heigen507_enkeiup 120 range 2–4 base502 258 range 3–8 total 1,477 0 decode errors a later paired desert control additionally had 114/114 directional leaves with capacity=1, arity=1, config index 2, and a byte-identical nine-row shader-config block to the studied small terrain candidate. it is an independent profile check, not part of the 1,477-leaf corrected-five-map count. the accepted desert main fmb and the deprecated desert508_working_best_effort file are different artifacts: the latter must not substitute for the former when asserting runtime provenance. interpretation: native edf6 definitely permits capacity=1. do not force a field to 2 because an earlier sample did not show 1. conversely, do not infer every fmb leaf must use this minimal profile; native leaves with larger lists and material indices exist. fmb tree and auxiliary fields: sample-grounded rules the accepted desert-versus-small-fmb comparison found an fmb directory whose leaves and internal tree nodes are decoded in postorder. each leaf contributes its leaf ordinal; a type-0 tree node combines two child subtrees and stores the inclusive range of leaf ordinals. it does not store a split at a raw directory-entry index. the same study decoded a 256-leaf / 255-node desert main tree, a 114-leaf / 113-node directional tree, and a 2-leaf / 1-node experimental candidate without tree-range errors. the native directional desert profile's nine-row config blob and eight-byte auxiliary block (00 00 00 00 08 00 00 00) were byte-identical to the studied candidate. a source-generated 256-row float4 lookup table had the same broad data domain as the native oracle but different exact bytes; no accepted gameplay experiment isolated the lut as the loader's cause. exact native geometry/tree format is an independent issue from locating fmb by resource name. runtime loader chain: why valid terrain files can still crash the modified-game diagnostic sequence illustrates the engine's separate resource-lookup and map-directory contracts. it is included here to identify native reader semantics, not as a recipe for developing a particular editor. source-controlled observation what it shows what it does not show island4 initial fmep tests: edf+0x1170b7, fault address 0x4 loader derives a sibling .fmb for a referenced .fmep, performs resource lookup, and dereferences record+4 with no observed null guard; corresponding fmb registration was missing from the mac's externals.sgo dds mip size or leaf capacity was proven wrong adding externals.sgo to mac the next runtime log no longer showed the +0x1170b7 signature; the engine progressed past that lookup map successfully rendered, or entire game was stable later observed edf+0x19026a, fault address 0x0 a separate mac directory-name relative-pointer problem was exposed in the investigated load that reported first-chance access violation is necessarily the terminal game crash site corrected mac directory rel32 (static proof) the parser's directory and name pointer bases were reconstructed; bad directory target was 12 bytes off and corrected to 0 post-correction gameplay was runtime-qualified for this observed native marc v5 directory parser, mac header field +0x14 is a signed 32-bit displacement relative to the address of that field, pointing to the first 24-byte directory entry. at each directory entry, +0x00 is itself a signed rel32 from the entry to a utf-16 resource name. the edf.dll read site analyzed was edf+0x1901f0; the loader used a relative-dword load and pointer addition at +0x190226…+0x190233, then read the utf-16 name at +0x19026a. this explains why a three-entry heuristic could appear to work, then fail when a fourth resource changed directory placement. the reported four-entry error targeted 0xb21c instead of the correct directory start 0xb210, producing a 12-byte pointer displacement and a zero name-relative field. the corrected value (header+0x14 = 0xb1fc) reaches 0xb210. these are a single measured mac profile, not license to assume the same offset for unrelated formats or game builds. the exact source-generated externals.sgo registered ss_island4_fmep.fmb while the map object graph referenced ss_island4_fmep.fmep; the resource names play different roles. the corrected r2f fix1 package passed static and transaction checks, but the source record ends at runtime pending. in particular, it does not prove that the complete experimental fmep terrain ever rendered successfully in that branch. rendering/material diagnosis is a separate axis renderdoc analysis of the static mdb island4 control showed a real artist-material mismatch: its source texture packed roughness / metallic / ao into rgb, but the observed control shader bound that resource as a reflect/spec-style mask. a direct runtime dump matched the expected model prefix exactly, ruling out an outdated mdb/rab for that sample. the tested legacy shader variants did not establish a complete artist-faithful material translation. that finding should not be imported wholesale into fmep's native terrain texture-array abi. static mdb shading, fieldrender dds slices, fieldrender leaf materials, mac resource registration, physical mad collision and hkt/nvmd navigation are distinct contracts. fixing one does not prove the others. what is proved, and what remains open original game evidence: 20 native dds payload byte-length matches; 1,477 correctly decoded fmb leaf wrappers; a native valid capacity-one pattern; distinct texture array sizes and normal formats per map. binary loader evidence: precise field-relative mac directory and name references for the studied edf6 build. modified runtime evidence: specific missing-fmb and subsequent bad-name failures, with the original missing-fmb signature no longer present after registration. not proved: runtime success of the corrected custom fmep branch; generic custom fmb authoring for arbitrary maps; stock-game inferences from an experiment-only asset; actual color-space treatment when the numeric dxgi enum is 71. primary research and independent format reference /edf5_edf6_research/research/audits/edf6_fmep_native_dds_capacity_corpus_audit_r2_corrected_2026-09-12.{md,json} — native five-map dds and six-fmb leaf corpus. /edf5_edf6_research/research/audits/edf6_swordstrike_island4_fmep_r2a_desert_oracle_comparison_audit_2026-09-12.{md,json} — accepted desert controls, fmb tree semantics and shader config/lut comparisons. /edf5_edf6_research/research/audits/edf6_swordstrike_island4_fmep_r2f_fix1_final_package_audit_2026-09-12.json — loader evidence, exact marc relative-pointer chain and runtime pending status. /edf5_edf6_research/research/audits/island4_renderdoc_material_rca_2026-09-11.json — separate static-mdb material evidence. microsoft, dxgi_format enumerated values — 71 vs 72 and 77 vs 78. related: map resource stack, island4 static map case study, dds and packed-channel contracts, map/navigation guide.

edf 4.1 original havok 2014 map and object corpus: what is actually established evidence: a read-only, exact-consumption audit of 21 original edf 4.1 binary tagfile payloads dated 5 september 2026: 5 .mad map collision files and 16 .shkt object physics files. it is not an edf6 gameplay test, and the original game assets are deliberately not shipped in this reference. the format identity is precise but not a converter all 21 examined payloads report binary tagfile version 5 and havok sdk identification hk_2014.1.0-r1. the audited decoder consumed the exact payload byte count in all 21/21 cases; each source file has a separate sha-256 and explicit source/payload sizes. this supports the original edf4.1 serialization observations, not the assertion that edf5 or edf6 uses the same physical shape layout. a shared havok family label does not make later hknp collision bodies compatible with edf4.1 hkp shapes by renaming a header. .mad represents map-side physics/collision; .shkt represents object-side physics. neither is an edf6 fmep vegetation/texture-array container. an original .mad can contain a large mixture of mopp meshes and relatively simple shape primitives; the file extension alone does not predict triangle counts or convex representation. five original edf4.1 map collision profiles original map rigid bodies direct mopp mesh paths accepted offline compact primitive branches accepted / examined direct primitive branches accepted ig_cave01 4 4 / 4 0 / 0 0 / 0 ig_testlightmap 177 14 / 14 161 / 163 0 / 0 ig_test_bluefld 1 0 / 0 1 / 1 0 / 0 nw_underground01 386 45 / 45 334 / 334 7 / 7 nw_kousoubld01 3,379 248 / 248 3,061 / 3,064 67 / 67 total 3,947 311 / 311 3,557 / 3,562 74 / 74 these counts are audited offline shape-route coverage, not runtime collision success. the 311 direct mopp mesh paths account for 283,381 vertices and 471,929 triangles in the source geometry survey. nw_kousoubld01 alone has 3,379 map rigid bodies, 248 accepted mopp paths and 3,064 tested compact-primitive branches; nw_underground01 includes direct box and convex roots alongside lists and mopps. a target physics format must represent the effective contact surface and transformed shape, not just a leaf class name. five negative compact-convex candidates are meaningful the compact branch had five failed map/body occurrences across two maps, representing three unique source body names. sk_car_sedan02_hk.polymsh and sk_car_minivan01_hk.polymsh each recur in ig_testlightmap and nw_kousoubld01: the high-vertex hulls did not satisfy the audited uint8 convex-reduction geometry budget (484 → 228 and 594 → 214 vertices in the error reports). nw_hct_koujimaku2.polymsh is a distinct failed hull with duplicate directed edge 1→0. those failures do not mean that the original map collision is invalid. they mean that this particular neutral compact representation was not qualified for those bodies. blindly lowering vertex counts can change support, contact extents and gameplay geometry. a separate exact edf4.1/edf5/edf6 comparison of the two car shapes demonstrates why a support-surface-preserving approximation matters. for the selected minivan, source expanded half-extents and the derived target-oriented profile agreed within approximately 0.000328 in the reported comparison; edf6 eos two-pc a/b/c/v experiment: delivered state versus applied soldier state evidence: direct two-computer edf6 runtime traces analyzed on 7 september 2026, eight primary logs across four variants and one exact edf6 binary. these observations apply to the tested traffic, session and build; they do not prove universal packet-loss freedom, correct remote animation, or a successful fix to player desync. what the four variants actually changed the baseline v left the transport unchanged. a enabled ballowdelayeddelivery=true for the audited ordinary unreliable eos physical send, while b provided only the link ready reset and c combined the two. all four variants had the same canonical edf.dll sha-256 0d5092393a1b9d8f1b75b0c93d8a8f65615a36a92c46e40349c2b66c733d0916 and the same trace-dll identity. the trace explicitly proved a/c activated the intended physical-send option; this was not a silent failure to load the test change. the decisive count comparison run host 0x3300 sent = client enqueued client 0x3300 sent = host enqueued host remote-soldier applies host mean / max apply spacing v 22,863 = 22,863 22,956 = 22,956 3,803 100.20 / 125 ms a 27,382 = 27,382 27,305 = 27,305 4,557 100.18 / 125 ms b 27,386 = 27,386 27,347 = 27,347 4,558 100.20 / 125 ms c 28,748 = 28,748 28,672 = 28,672 4,784 100.16 / 125 ms the recipient's rx3300_parse count also equalled rx3300_enqueue in every direction. every observed eos physical send returned success: zero observed noconnection, limitexceeded or other nonzero send results. the dominant remote soldier applied its networkobject updates at an approximately 10 hz cadence in all variants, without a measured gap greater than 125 ms over each corresponding host interval. these are distinct checks: network delivery, sceneobject parser admission and concrete apply cadence. the exact direction-by-direction figures are in data/r158_edf6_eos_vabc_3300_two_pc_runtime_matrix.csv. they show that ordinary eos packet disappearance was not the failure in this capture. they do not establish that decoded position changes reached the final world/render/physics transform correctly. why a, b and c do not establish a repaired desync the a/c delayed-delivery bit changed as intended, but the baseline already delivered all recorded ordinary sceneobject messages. there was therefore no observed physical loss for a to correct. the b ready-reset branch was not meaningfully exercised: neither mid-session stale ready nor a matching reconnect failure signature occurred. normal ready=0 initial transitions and late teardown-related clears are not evidence of that bug. the combined c run inherits those limits. damage_event totals matched across peers per run, but 0x3500 networkbullet was not exercised (bullet_tx=0 and rx3500_bullet=0). do not claim a projectile synchronization result from an ordinary movement matrix. what the later two-pc capture added the subsequent narrower r7 capture and r8 investigation found a different, later boundary: persistent position divergence (approximately 183 world units in the reported case) while sender updates continued and remote position-bearing staging/consumption became sparse. matching physical packet hashes did not guarantee matching actual soldier transforms. the later r8/r9 work therefore targeted per-object sceneobject staging, sequence freshness and concrete soldier application rather than blindly changing eos reliability. do not conflate the r6 matrix's stable apply call cadence with proof that every individual call applied a fresh positional payload. a received absolute transform should generally recover after a single lost snapshot. persistent divergence with present physical packets instead demands checks for packet-field composition, generation/index/type keys, decode/stage freshness, overwritten pending state, player movement controllers and world-transform interpolation. an action/jump 0x3400 or strong correction path must be analyzed separately from ordinary 0x3300. timing and authority limits the pcs had substantial and varying windows wall-clock offsets. ordered cumulative captures suggest a low-latency local path, but one-way per-record latency is not established from unsynchronized clocks. host-local apply intervals avoid that cross-pc ambiguity. also, the observed results do not invalidate the separate stale-ready reconnect hypothesis: that failure state simply did not occur in the v/a/b/c sessions. primary source: /edf5_edf6_research/research/audits/edf6_network_eos_runtime_matrix_vabc_analysis_2026-09-07.md; earlier binary hypotheses and initially open questions: edf6_network_eos_repair_evidence_ledger_2026-08-30.json. related: player packet lanes, r7/r8 sceneobject staging, rudp reconnect lifetime, protocol-aware tracing.

edf6 island4 renderdoc: reflect/spec-versus-rmo material evidence evidence: three preserved modified-runtime r6b captures, two control captures, the 11 september 2026 renderdoc material report and a separate 9-entry capture sha-256 ledger. this is a bounded investigation of ordinary static mdb material rendering on island4. it is not a generic fieldrender/fmep texture contract, nor an in-game confirmation of a finished replacement shader. why a loaded texture can still appear chrome-like the artist's source packed mask is r = roughness, g = metallic, b = ambient occlusion, used with the artist-side snd_brdf_common_basic group and param_r_m_occ_hr slot. in the r4c/r6b static-mdb control, a reflect/spec-style mask contract received that artist rmo texture instead. this is an interpretation/binding mismatch, not equivalent to missing ss_island4-rmo.dds. r6b runtime logging admitted ss_island4-df.dds, ss_island4-nm.dds, ss_island4-rmo.dds and ss_island4_00001.mdb. its 2,048-byte mdb0 runtime dump prefix matched the expected package prefix byte for byte, sha-256 b915c7431e9d210a8ec0a19c62b378712cfa8ed8dcccb81b9c05474c3f359e22. that rules out stale rab/wrong package/early mdb corruption for this run, not every possible late material or shader bug. four relevant pixel-shader observations scoped shader observation pixel-shader sha-256 prefix key reflected resource names control f555c7ee albedo, normal, param_reflect_cm0_spec_hspec r6b d73dc06b albedo, normal, param_reflect_xxx_spec_hspec r/m/o + hr sample 635b46e2 albedo, normal, param_r_m_occ_hr, param_cm0_cm1, roughness, xgl_user_param r/m/o + light sample 889c44ee albedo, normal, param_r_m_occ_hr, param_r_m_occ_light, light_color the full hashes and string sets are in data/r158_edf6_island4_renderdoc_four_shader_observations.csv. the control/r6b shader reflections each list three samplers aligned to their three reflected resource lanes. these captured dxbc strings are compiled runtime evidence, but they do not prove a specific snd_* source shader filename or the final exact mathematical channel interpretation for all families. what the native map corpus actually supports the sampled native ig_heigen507.rab and nw_europe01.rab contain 52 and 49 snd_brdf_map_common materials, respectively, with native samplers albedo, normal, param_r_m_xxx_hr. there are 29 and 15 snd_brdf_map_common_clip samples across those same areas. the europe sample also contains five snd_brdf_map_common_light profiles with param_r_m_light_hr and one signboard-pattern sample with param_r_m_occ_light in its samplers. the artist's exact snd_brdf_common_basic shader family was not found in the audited native map corpus. a proposed r7 material using that identity and rmo slot conserved the recorded geometry bytes offline, but was not packaged or runtime-qualified by this report. its parameter ordering/type choices therefore remained partially inferred rather than copied from an exact native profile for the artist shader. negative tests narrow the cause, not the final answer temporary roughness=1 and native-no-ao mask candidates reduced the shine in earlier r5b/r5c runtime checks, but were not artist-faithful solutions. later r6a/r6b modifications using build simple / object no-ccao did not repair the chrome-like response. these outcomes argue against more blind swapping of reflect/spec shader names and for exact r/m/o semantics with an abi-qualified material. three separate quality axes material: rmo mask read as reflect/spec causes wrong response despite valid resource load. texture resolution: the x20 static map still uses a 4096² atlas; area-weighted density and anisotropy remain problematic even if roughness is correct. terrain backend: static mdb shaders and their parameters are independent from fmep/fieldrender projected texture arrays, leaf wrappers and mac resource registration. neither a valid source dds nor a byte-exact mdb model is a visual-compositing pass. a completed, artist-faithful material translation would require the actual shader family, parameter type/order, sampler bindings, render state and a matched runtime visual test. source provenance: island4_renderdoc_material_rca_2026-09-11.json and island4_renderdoc_capture_hash_ledger_2026-09-11.json under /edf5_edf6_research/research/audits/. nine saved capture/thumbnail/derived-frame identities are listed by byte size and hash in data/r158_edf6_island4_renderdoc_nine_capture_identities.csv; this wiki does not redistribute game captures. related: island4 map-control study, native mdb material families, fmep native terrain. how this case should be read beside the broader shader corpus the edf6 shader inventory's 485 dx11 archive entries / 3,449 dxbc programs is an offline census. island4's four retained pixel-shader observations, in contrast, identify compiled paths seen in bounded captured runs. those are different sample populations and must not be numerically combined or presented as four newly proven shader families. the island4 evidence establishes a particularly useful diagnostic separation: stage observed result still not established asset admission mdb/texture records were accepted and the tested prefix matched every later material command and its final visual interpretation reflected resource contract reflect/spec and r/m/o pixel-shader samples expose distinct parameter names automatic equivalence between the artist r/m/o texture and an unrelated reflect/spec binding captured shader specific dxbc hashes identify the programs complete scene-wide equivalence for every model/material final image diagnostic material changes reduced shine in some runs an artist-faithful native pixel/compositor reproduction this is why texture presence, shader presence and attractive final pixels are separate claims. see the five-family proof matrix for the state/binding/pixel evidence required to promote a material rule.

original navigation and collision: low/high, source layers and passage clearance evidence: selected original edf5/edf6 hkt files, bounded original edf4.1 mac/mad geometry, and offline static analysis (17 november 2026). not evidence of correct npc pathfinding in a live edf6 mission. this article concerns game-engine data and measured original-source geometry; the research tools used to inspect them are not part of the game's file format. two native nav resolutions are materially different the original nw_europe01 pair of maps in edf5 and edf6 each contains separate low- and high-detail havok hkainavmesh files. their native topology is not one shared mesh with different bounds: original-file measurement edf5 low edf6 low edf5 high edf6 high navmesh tiles 4 4 16 16 faces 4,419 4,059 32,787 30,216 edges 21,858 20,329 122,457 114,551 hierarchy nodes 218 205 1,665 1,543 both variants contain native clearance-cache data. a root erosionradius of zero in this example does not prove that npcs have a zero physical radius. the counts describe one matched map and game builds, not universal low/high file sizes or an algorithm that can be copied to another map. edf4.1 original map sources in the examined corpus do not supply a transferable navmesh.hkt file. thus source terrain and collision geometry must first be identified and qualified before target-style nav can be generated. a structurally valid hkt/nvmd pair does not prove agent clearance, active-body semantics or gameplay behavior. see hkt/nvmd compatibility versus rebake and edf4.1 4 m source terrain. original edf4.1 source-body attribution: a floor is not automatically walkable the source-backed 4 m layer studies in two small map windows separated candidate height/surface samples by whether their original mapb/mad body owner was classified as a field source. a nonfield-only layer might represent a platform, bridge, roof, staircase or another meaningful surface; classifying it as nonfield is not grounds to delete it from navigation. bounded map/source window candidate upward sheet nodes field-candidate nonfield-only unresolved nw_hillycity_light 568 503 65 0 nw_soukogai01 226 200 26 0 the numbers apply to the studied two rois, not the complete city maps. field source is a selected source-object anchor, not proof of native walkability or real contact activation. the initial step-only graph already missed obstacles at some connecting edges. centerline, side and radius experiments on original source triangles a four-neighbor grid can make a plausible nav connection even when real collision triangles intersect that path. direct original-source tests distinguish observed contacts from candidate edges with no sampled contact. map window and nav profile candidate edges centerline contacts additional side-ray contacts remaining edges without sampled contact hillycity low 1,216 93 47 1,076 hillycity high 1,154 56 41 1,057 soukogai low 419 0 8 411 soukogai high 401 0 5 396 the original geometric source windows contained 2,035 clipped facets in hillycity and 724 in soukogai. centerline tests sampled three heights (0.25, 0.9 and 1.7 m); side tests added lateral offsets of ±0.75 m. contacts are source-triangle intersections conditional on actual actor/rigid-body activation and placement. in particular, 0 intersected centerline rays in soukogai did not prove that the crossing corridor was free. separate sparse source-geometric sphere-distance samples at radii 0.25, 0.50 and 0.75 m found further contacts beyond those point-ray samples: radius hillycity new low / high soukogai new low / high 0.25 m 1 / 0 0 / 0 0.50 m 4 / 2 7 / 5 0.75 m 18 / 16 19 / 11 these are chosen diagnostic radii, not the measured dimensions of ranger, fencer, hector or any edf6 navigation agent. the sphere tests use sparse segment axes, not a full upright swept capsule or verified native havok clearance. nor should the per-radius counts be added to infer a total number of distinct npc failures. mapb group placement changes the collision interpretation the bounded hillycity native-source index showed five group-owner records with 40 child links. of those linked children, only one resolved to the selected static mad collision-source route; the other 39 remain unresolved, not nonexistent or non-colliding. for that one child, using its stored pose independently placed its conservative collision candidate inside the selected window, while hypothetically composing its parent group's pose moved its conservative candidate elsewhere. soukogai had no group links in this control. this shows sensitivity to transform interpretation; it does not establish whether original edf4.1 actually applies parent-composed transforms at runtime. applying parent composition blindly, or discarding 39 unresolved child links, could corrupt nav exclusions. the source's candidate rz*ry*rx actor pose and activation/layer rules are still not native-runtime verified. what remains unproven these measurements do not close full-map coverage, native collision-body activation, actor/group world transforms, layered roofs and caves, agent capsule size/height, ledges, erosion, bridge semantics or native low/high polygonization. in-game npc behavior for ranger/fencer/hector, vehicle movement and the 16-map-family scope remain unqualified. no result here establishes a playable npc-pathfinding fix. source provenance: original retail hkt measurement and 147-mission scope in r49_nav_and_online_decisions.md;
